docs.title: Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL🤖 Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL
docs.text:
Enterprise-grade autonomous robotics platform powered by NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super

⚡ Real-time AI Perception • 🗺️ Advanced SLAM • 🚀 Production-Ready Deployment

🚀 Get Started 📚 Documentation ⭐ GitHub

docs.title: 📊 Performance at a Glance
docs.text: 35+ FPS Object Detection <20ms Inference Latency 10-15W Power Consumption 98.5% Detection Accuracy

docs.title: ✨ Key Features
docs.text:
🧠 Advanced AI Perception

State-of-the-art object detection with YOLOv8 and NanoOWL, optimized for real-time inference on Jetson hardware with TensorRT acceleration.

🗺️ Real-time SLAM

Visual-inertial odometry with 3D reconstruction, path planning using A* and RRT* algorithms, and dynamic obstacle avoidance.

📡 Multi-sensor Fusion

Seamless integration of cameras, LIDAR, IMU, and GPS sensors with synchronized data processing and advanced sensor calibration.

⚡ CUDA Acceleration

GPU-optimized computer vision pipeline with custom CUDA kernels for image processing, feature extraction, and neural network inference.

🌙 Night Vision

Thermal camera integration with AI-enhanced low-light performance for 24/7 autonomous operation in any lighting condition.

🚀 Production Ready

Complete deployment stack with Docker, Kubernetes, Helm charts, OTA updates, and comprehensive monitoring solutions.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick Start
docs.text:
Get up and running in minutes:

DockerNativeKubernetes Bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL

# Build and run with Docker
docker-compose up -d

# Access the system
ros2 launch jetbot_nanoowl bringup.launch.py
Bash
# Install ROS2 Humble
sudo apt update
sudo apt install ros-humble-desktop

# Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
colcon build --symlink-install

# Source and launch
source install/setup.bash
ros2 launch jetbot_nanoowl bringup.launch.py
Bash
# Install with Helm
helm repo add tng-blue https://tng-blue.github.io/charts
helm install jetbot-nanoowl tng-blue/jetbot-nanoowl

# Check status
kubectl get pods -n robotics

Get Started →

docs.title: Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Documentation 2.0.0 February 4, 2026
docs.text: Comprehensive documentation suite for Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL platform with complete API reference, tutorials, and deployment guides.

docs.title: What's New
docs.text:
This release introduces a complete professional documentation suite replacing ad-hoc guides with enterprise-grade, well-structured documentation covering all aspects of the platform:

  • API Reference Documentation:

    • Complete C++ API with motor control, camera interface, IMU sensor, object detection
    • Pythonic API for rapid development with Jupyter notebook support
    • ROS2 Interfaces with 15+ message types, 10+ service definitions, action types
    • REST API with 20+ endpoints and multi-language client examples (Python, JavaScript, cURL)
    • 40+ working code examples across all APIs
    • ~54KB comprehensive documentation with implementation details

  • Tutorial Series - Learning Paths:

    • Basic Tutorials (9 total): First Mission, Camera Calibration, Sensor Setup - covering beginner operations
    • Advanced Tutorials (3 total): Custom Models, SLAM Configuration, Multi-Robot Setup - intermediate to advanced
    • Deployment Tutorials (3 total): Production Setup, OTA Integration, Monitoring & Maintenance - professional deployment
    • 2,000+ lines of tutorial documentation with 75+ code examples
    • Estimated learning time: 10.5 hours total for complete path
    • Step-by-step instructions with verification checklists

  • Deployment Documentation:

    • Docker Deployment: Multi-stage Dockerfiles, docker-compose with 8 services, GPU integration, registry management
    • Kubernetes Deployment: Cluster setup, manifests (deployments, services, StatefulSet), kustomization, RBAC, monitoring
    • Helm Charts: Parameterized charts with 3 environment profiles (dev/prod/edge), dependency management, templating
    • OTA Updates: Update server infrastructure, staged rollout strategies, automatic rollback, fleet management
    • Cloud Integration: AWS (EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFormation), Google Cloud (Compute Engine, Firestore, Pub/Sub), Azure (VMs, Cosmos DB)
    • ~61KB documentation with 45+ code examples for 5 deployment methods
    • Covers 3 major cloud platforms with complete CLI commands and infrastructure templates

  • ROS2 Modules Documentation (11 modules):

    • Object Detection with YOLOv8 integration and real-time performance metrics
    • SLAM & Navigation with visual-inertial fusion and loop closure detection
    • Control System with PID tuning and motor feedback
    • Sensor Fusion using Extended Kalman Filter
    • Night Vision with thermal imaging and RGB-thermal fusion
    • Network Bridge supporting WiFi 5GHz, LoRa, 4G/LTE
    • Monitoring with real-time system health tracking
    • RF Spectrum Analysis with interference detection
    • Stereo Vision for 3D perception with point cloud generation
    • Microcontroller Integration with ARM Cortex-M7 real-time scheduling
    • ~4,870 lines of documentation with 75+ code examples and 20+ diagrams
    • Performance benchmarks and configuration parameters

  • CUDA Vision Documentation:

    • Complete CUDA acceleration library documentation
    • GPU kernel implementations for real-time vision processing
    • Performance optimization guide with benchmarks
    • Integration examples with ROS2 pipeline
    • 450+ lines of comprehensive API documentation

  • Doxygen Configuration Documentation:

    • Doxyfile.in template with CMake substitution explained
    • DoxygenLayout.xml configuration for HTML generation
    • Complete explanation of Doxygen purpose and workflow
    • Practical guide with step-by-step instructions
    • Code comment examples for C++ and Python
    • ~4,000 lines of Doxygen education and practical guide

docs.text:

docs.title: Version Format
docs.text:
Follow semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH

  • MAJOR: Major documentation restructuring, complete section rewrites, significant coverage additions
  • MINOR: New documentation sections, new tutorials, new API coverage, new deployment guides
  • PATCH: Documentation corrections, typo fixes, example updates, clarification improvements

docs.title: Release Entry Format
docs.text:
Markdown
## Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Documentation X.Y.Z Month Day, Year

Brief overview of documentation changes in this release.

### What's New

Documentation updates including:

* **Section Name**:
    * Feature or update description
    * Key improvements with metrics
    * User-facing benefits

### Quality Improvements

* Specific improvements to documentation quality
* Better examples or explanations
* Enhanced organization

### Platform Support

Platforms and features covered in documentation

### Limitations

Known limitations in current documentation

### Issues Addressed

Documentation improvements addressing user feedback

docs.title: Writing Guidelines
docs.text:
When to Update: - Addition of new APIs or modules - New tutorial series or guides - New deployment strategies or platforms - Major documentation reorganization - Significant content improvements or corrections - Performance documentation updates - Security improvements to documentation

What to Include: - Clear description of documentation additions - Technical accuracy and completeness - Code examples demonstrating features - Cross-references to related documentation - Performance metrics and benchmarks - Platform requirements and support - Known limitations and workarounds

What to Exclude: - Minor typo fixes or formatting - Internal documentation reorganization without content changes - Temporary or staging documentation - Outdated reference materials

Structure Your Entries: - Group documentation by functional area or topic - Lead with most significant additions - Include specific metrics (number of examples, lines of documentation) - Reference specific files or sections - Use clear technical terminology - Mention target audience (beginner, advanced, professional)

Language and Tone: - Use clear, professional technical language - Focus on completeness and accuracy - Be specific with numbers and metrics - Mention compatibility and platform support - Use active voice for improvements - Highlight practical benefits for users

docs.title: Breaking Changes Documentation
docs.text:
When significant documentation structure changes occur:

Markdown
### Documentation Structure Changes

* **API Reference Reorganization**:
    * Old: Combined C++ and Python APIs
    * New: Separate sections with dedicated examples
    * Migration: See API reference index for new structure
    * Reason: Improved clarity for language-specific users

* **Tutorial Path Restructuring**:
    * Old: Linear progression without clear difficulty levels
    * New: Three progressive paths (beginner/advanced/professional)
    * Migration: See tutorials/index.md for new organization
    * Benefit: Faster learning for appropriate skill levels

For questions about documentation or to report issues, please open an issue on GitHub or contact the documentation team through the project channels.

docs.title: 1. Motor Controller
docs.text:
Python
from jetbot import MotorController

class MotorController:
    """Control robot movement"""

    def __init__(self):
        """Initialize motor controller"""

    def set_velocity(self, linear_x: float, angular_z: float) -> None:
        """
        Set robot velocity

        Args:
            linear_x: Forward velocity in m/s (-1.0 to 1.0)
            angular_z: Angular velocity in rad/s (-3.14 to 3.14)

        Examples:
            motor.set_velocity(0.5, 0.0)  # Move forward
            motor.set_velocity(0.0, 1.0)  # Rotate left
            motor.set_velocity(0.5, 0.5)  # Move forward + turn
        """

    def get_velocity(self) -> tuple:
        """
        Get current velocity

        Returns:
            (linear_x, angular_z) tuple
        """

    def set_motor_speed(self, left_speed: int, right_speed: int) -> None:
        """
        Set individual motor speeds (0-255)

        Args:
            left_speed: Left motor speed (0-255)
            right_speed: Right motor speed (0-255)
        """

    def get_motor_state(self) -> dict:
        """
        Get motor state

        Returns:
            {
                'left_velocity': float,
                'right_velocity': float,
                'left_current': float,
                'right_current': float
            }
        """

    def emergency_stop(self) -> None:
        """Perform emergency stop"""

    def is_healthy(self) -> bool:
        """Check if motors are healthy"""

Example:

Python
motor = MotorController()

# Move forward
motor.set_velocity(0.3, 0.0)
time.sleep(2)

# Turn and move
motor.set_velocity(0.3, 0.5)
time.sleep(1)

# Check status
velocity = motor.get_velocity()
state = motor.get_motor_state()
print(f"Velocity: {velocity}")
print(f"Motor state: {state}")

# Emergency stop
if not motor.is_healthy():
    motor.emergency_stop()

docs.title: 2. Camera Interface
docs.text:
Python
from jetbot import Camera
import cv2

class Camera:
    """Access robot camera"""

    def __init__(self, width: int = 1280, height: int = 720, fps: int = 30):
        """Initialize camera"""

    def read(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Get camera frame

        Returns:
            BGR image as numpy array (H × W × 3)
        """

    def get_frame(self, timeout_ms: int = 100) -> tuple:
        """
        Get frame with timeout

        Returns:
            (success: bool, frame: np.ndarray)
        """

    def get_camera_info(self) -> dict:
        """
        Get camera calibration info

        Returns:
            {
                'width': int,
                'height': int,
                'camera_matrix': np.ndarray (3×3),
                'distortion': np.ndarray (5,)
            }
        """

    def load_calibration(self, filename: str) -> None:
        """Load calibration from file"""

    def undistort(self, frame: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Remove lens distortion from frame"""

    def set_exposure(self, exposure: int) -> None:
        """Set exposure (-13 to 0)"""

    def set_gain(self, gain: int) -> None:
        """Set gain (0 to 100)"""

Example:

Python
camera = Camera(1280, 720, 30)

# Load calibration
camera.load_calibration("camera_calibration.yaml")

# Capture frame
success, frame = camera.get_frame(timeout_ms=100)

if success:
    # Undistort
    undistorted = camera.undistort(frame)

    # Display
    cv2.imshow("Camera", undistorted)
    cv2.waitKey(1)

# Get calibration info
info = camera.get_camera_info()
K = info['camera_matrix']
dist = info['distortion']

docs.title: 3. Object Detection
docs.text:
Python
from jetbot import Detector

class Detector:
    """Run object detection"""

    def __init__(self, model_path: str):
        """
        Initialize detector

        Args:
            model_path: Path to model file (.engine, .onnx, .pt)
        """

    def detect(self, frame: np.ndarray) -> list:
        """
        Run detection on frame

        Returns:
            List of detections:
            [
                {
                    'class_id': int,
                    'class_name': str,
                    'confidence': float,
                    'bbox': (x, y, w, h)  # Normalized [0, 1]
                },
                ...
            ]
        """

    async def detect_async(self, frame: np.ndarray, callback) -> None:
        """Asynchronous detection"""

    def get_stats(self) -> dict:
        """
        Get performance statistics

        Returns:
            {
                'inference_time_ms': float,
                'fps': int,
                'cpu_usage': float,
                'memory_usage_mb': float
            }
        """

    def set_confidence_threshold(self, threshold: float) -> None:
        """Set detection confidence threshold (0.0 to 1.0)"""

Example:

Python
detector = Detector("models/yolov8n.engine")

camera = Camera()
success, frame = camera.read()

if success:
    detections = detector.detect(frame)

    for det in detections:
        print(f"{det['class_name']}: {det['confidence']:.2f}")

        # Draw bounding box
        x, y, w, h = det['bbox']
        x1 = int(x * frame.shape[1])
        y1 = int(y * frame.shape[0])
        x2 = int((x + w) * frame.shape[1])
        y2 = int((y + h) * frame.shape[0])

        cv2.rectangle(frame, (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (0, 255, 0), 2)
        cv2.putText(frame, det['class_name'], (x1, y1-10),
                   cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5, (0, 255, 0), 2)

    cv2.imshow("Detections", frame)

docs.title: 4. IMU Sensor
docs.text:
Python
from jetbot import IMUSensor
import numpy as np

class IMUSensor:
    """Access IMU (accelerometer + gyroscope)"""

    def __init__(self):
        """Initialize IMU"""

    def read(self) -> dict:
        """
        Get latest IMU data

        Returns:
            {
                'acceleration': np.array([x, y, z]),  # m/s²
                'angular_velocity': np.array([x, y, z]),  # rad/s
                'temperature': float  # °C
            }
        """

    def register_callback(self, callback) -> None:
        """
        Register callback for real-time updates

        Example:
            def on_imu_data(data):
                print(f"Accel: {data['acceleration']}")

            imu.register_callback(on_imu_data)
        """

    def calibrate_accelerometer(self) -> None:
        """Calibrate accelerometer (keep still)"""

    def calibrate_gyroscope(self) -> None:
        """Calibrate gyroscope (keep still)"""

    def get_calibration(self) -> dict:
        """Get current calibration values"""

Example:

Python
imu = IMUSensor()

# Get single reading
data = imu.read()
print(f"Acceleration: {data['acceleration']}")
print(f"Angular velocity: {data['angular_velocity']}")

# Stream with callback
def on_imu_update(data):
    accel = np.linalg.norm(data['acceleration'])
    print(f"Total acceleration: {accel:.2f} m/s²")

imu.register_callback(on_imu_update)

# Keep running
import time
time.sleep(10)

docs.title: 🎯 Complete Example: Obstacle Avoidance
docs.text:
Python
from jetbot import MotorController, Camera, Detector
import cv2
import time

class ObstacleAvoider:
    def __init__(self):
        self.motor = MotorController()
        self.camera = Camera()
        self.detector = Detector("models/yolov8n.engine")
        self.detector.set_confidence_threshold(0.7)

    def run(self):
        print("Starting obstacle avoidance...")
        running_time = 0

        while running_time < 30:  # Run for 30 seconds
            start = time.time()

            # Get camera frame
            success, frame = self.camera.read()
            if not success:
                continue

            # Detect obstacles
            detections = self.detector.detect(frame)

            # Check for obstacles in front
            obstacle_in_front = False
            for det in detections:
                if det['class_name'] == 'person':
                    # Center of frame is around x=0.5
                    x, w = det['bbox'][0], det['bbox'][2]
                    if 0.25 < x + w/2 < 0.75:  # In center
                        obstacle_in_front = True
                        break

            if obstacle_in_front:
                print("Obstacle detected! Turning...")
                self.motor.set_velocity(0.0, 1.0)  # Turn left
                time.sleep(0.5)
            else:
                print("Moving forward...")
                self.motor.set_velocity(0.3, 0.0)  # Move forward

            # Display frame
            cv2.imshow("Obstacle Avoidance", frame)
            if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
                break

            running_time += time.time() - start

        # Stop
        self.motor.set_velocity(0.0, 0.0)
        cv2.destroyAllWindows()
        print("Done!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    avoider = ObstacleAvoider()
    avoider.run()

import asyncio
from jetbot import Detector, Camera

async def detect_continuously():
    detector = Detector("models/yolov8n.engine")
    camera = Camera()

    while True:
        success, frame = camera.read()
        if success:
            # Non-blocking detection
            detections = await detector.detect_async(frame)
            print(f"Found {len(detections)} objects")

import requests
import json
import base64
from PIL import Image
from io import BytesIO

BASE_URL = "http://jetbot.local:8080/api/v1"
API_KEY = "sk_live_abc123..."

headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

# Move forward
response = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/motor/velocity",
    headers=headers,
    json={"linear_x": 0.5, "angular_z": 0.0}
)
print(response.json())

# Get camera frame
response = requests.get(
    f"{BASE_URL}/camera/frame?format=base64",
    headers=headers
)
data = response.json()
frame_data = base64.b64decode(data['frame'])
image = Image.open(BytesIO(frame_data))
image.show()

# Run detection
response = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/detection/detect",
    headers=headers,
    json={"image_url": f"{BASE_URL}/camera/frame?format=base64"}
)
detections = response.json()['detections']
for det in detections:
    print(f"{det['class_name']}: {det['confidence']:.2f}")

# Set navigation goal
response = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/navigation/goal",
    headers=headers,
    json={"x": 5.0, "y": 5.0, "max_velocity": 0.5}
)
print(response.json())

import rclpy
from jetbot_interfaces.msg import MotorState

def motor_callback(msg):
    print(f"Left velocity: {msg.left_velocity} m/s")
    print(f"Right velocity: {msg.right_velocity} m/s")
    print(f"Left current: {msg.left_current} A")

def main():
    rclpy.init()
    node = rclpy.create_node('motor_listener')

    subscription = node.create_subscription(
        MotorState,
        '/motor/state',
        motor_callback,
        10
    )

    rclpy.spin(node)
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':

docs.title: Example 3: Call Service
docs.text:
Python
import rclpy
from jetbot_interfaces.srv import SetVelocity

def main():
    rclpy.init()
    node = rclpy.create_node('velocity_controller')

    client = node.create_client(SetVelocity, '/motor/set_velocity')

    while not client.wait_for_service(timeout_sec=1.0):
        print('Service not available, waiting again...')

    request = SetVelocity.Request()
    request.linear_x = 0.5
    request.angular_z = 0.0

    future = client.call_async(request)
    rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(node, future)

    result = future.result()
    print(f"Success: {result.success}")
    print(f"Message: {result.message}")

    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist
from jetbot_interfaces.msg import MotorState

class FleetController(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('fleet_controller')

        # Publishers for each robot
        self.robot1_pub = self.create_publisher(Twist, '/jetbot1/cmd_vel', 10)
        self.robot2_pub = self.create_publisher(Twist, '/jetbot2/cmd_vel', 10)

        # Subscribers for status
        self.robot1_sub = self.create_subscription(
            MotorState, '/jetbot1/motor/state', self.robot1_callback, 10)
        self.robot2_sub = self.create_subscription(
            MotorState, '/jetbot2/motor/state', self.robot2_callback, 10)

        # Timer for control loop
        self.timer = self.create_timer(0.1, self.control_loop)

        self.robot1_state = None
        self.robot2_state = None

    def robot1_callback(self, msg):
        self.robot1_state = msg

    def robot2_callback(self, msg):
        self.robot2_state = msg

    def control_loop(self):
        if self.robot1_state and self.robot2_state:
            # Send coordinated commands
            cmd = Twist()
            cmd.linear.x = 0.5

            self.robot1_pub.publish(cmd)
            self.robot2_pub.publish(cmd)

            self.get_logger().info(
                f"Robot1 velocity: {self.robot1_state.left_velocity:.2f}")
            self.get_logger().info(
                f"Robot2 velocity: {self.robot2_state.left_velocity:.2f}")

def main():
    rclpy.init()
    controller = FleetController()
    rclpy.spin(controller)
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

**Environment:**
- Jetson Orin Nano 8GB
- JetPack 5.1.2
- ROS2 Humble
- Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL v1.0.0

**Issue:**
Object detection node crashes with "CUDA out of memory" error after 5 minutes.

**What I've tried:**
- Reduced batch size from 8 to 4
- Lowered model resolution from 640x640 to 320x320
- Monitored GPU memory with nvidia-smi

**Error output:**
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256.00 MiB Text Only
**Question:**

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
What hardware do I need?

Minimum: - NVIDIA Jetson Nano (4GB) - Camera module - MicroSD card (64GB+) - Power supply

Recommended: - Jetson Orin Nano (8GB) - Multiple cameras/sensors - NVMe SSD - See Hardware Setup

Can I use different Jetson models?

Yes! Supported platforms: - ✅ Jetson Nano - ✅ Jetson Xavier NX - ✅ Jetson AGX Xavier - ✅ Jetson Orin Nano - ✅ Jetson AGX Orin

Performance varies by model.

Do I need robotics experience?

No! Our Quick Start Guide is beginner-friendly. However, basic Linux knowledge helps.

What's the fastest way to get started?

Use Docker installation: Bash

git clone https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
docker-compose up -d
See Quick Start

docs.title: 🔧 Installation & Setup
docs.text:
Which installation method should I choose?
  • Docker: Fastest, easiest, recommended for beginners
  • Native: Best performance, for developers
  • Kubernetes: For production/fleet deployment
Installation fails with memory error

Reduce parallel workers or add swap: Bash

colcon build --parallel-workers 1
# Or add 4GB swap
sudo fallocate -l 4G /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
sudo swapon /swapfile

How much disk space do I need?
  • Minimum: 32GB (basic installation)
  • Recommended: 128GB+ (includes models, data)
  • Docker: Additional 10GB for containers

docs.title: 📹 Camera & Sensors
docs.text:
Camera not detected
  1. Check physical connection
  2. Verify permissions: Bash
    sudo usermod -aG video $USER
ls -l /dev/video0
  3. Test camera: Bash
    nvgstcapture-1.0
Which cameras are supported?
  • ✅ CSI cameras (OV5647, IMX219, IMX477)
  • ✅ USB webcams
  • ✅ Thermal cameras
  • ✅ Stereo camera pairs
Low frame rate from camera
  • Reduce resolution: 640x640 instead of 1920x1080
  • Lower framerate parameter
  • Check CPU/GPU usage with tegrastats

docs.title: 🎯 Object Detection
docs.text:
Detection not working
  1. Check model file exists
  2. Verify GPU access: Bash
    python3 -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
  3. Check logs: Bash
    ros2 node info /object_detection
Detection accuracy is low
  • Lower confidence threshold (0.3-0.5)
  • Use better lighting
  • Try larger model (yolov8s vs yolov8n)
  • Calibrate camera
Can I use custom object classes?

Yes! Train custom YOLOv8 model and convert to TensorRT. See Custom Models Tutorial

docs.title: 🗺️ Navigation & SLAM
docs.text:
Robot not building map
  1. Check LIDAR data: Bash
    ros2 topic echo /scan
  2. Ensure LIDAR spinning
  3. Drive slowly during mapping
  4. Check TF tree
Navigation fails to reach goal
  • Ensure clear path in costmap
  • Check robot footprint size
  • Adjust inflation radius
  • Use intermediate waypoints
SLAM drift over time
  • Enable loop closure
  • Add more distinctive features to environment
  • Calibrate IMU
  • Use better odometry

docs.title: ⚡ Performance
docs.text:
System running slow
  1. Check power mode: Bash
    sudo nvpmodel -m 0  # Max performance
sudo jetson_clocks
  2. Monitor resources: Bash
    tegrastats
  3. Reduce workload (lower resolution, simpler model)
What FPS should I expect?

On Jetson Orin Nano (640x640 input): - YOLOv8n: 35-45 FPS - YOLOv8s: 25-30 FPS - YOLOv8m: 15-20 FPS

High latency
  • Use Ethernet instead of WiFi
  • Reduce QoS history depth
  • Enable GPU power mode
  • Check network with ping

docs.title: 🐛 Troubleshooting
docs.text:
ROS2 nodes can't communicate
  1. Check ROS_DOMAIN_ID: Bash
    echo $ROS_DOMAIN_ID
  2. Test multicast: Bash
    ros2 multicast receive
ros2 multicast send  # In another terminal
  3. Check firewall
Build fails

See Troubleshooting Guide

Where are log files? Bash
~/.ros/log/
~/ros2_ws/log/

docs.title: 📦 Docker & Deployment
docs.text:
Docker container won't start
  1. Check Docker daemon: Bash
    sudo systemctl status docker
  2. Verify GPU access: Bash
    docker run --rm --runtime nvidia nvidia/cuda:11.8.0-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi
  3. Check logs: Bash
    docker-compose logs
How to update Docker images? Bash
docker-compose pull
docker-compose up -d

docs.title: Main CI Workflow
docs.text:
.github/workflows/ci.yml:

YAML
name: Continuous Integration

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, master]

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Code Quality Checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'

      - name: Install linters
        run: |
          pip install black flake8 isort
          sudo apt install clang-format -y

      - name: Check Python formatting
        run: |
          black --check src/
          flake8 src/
          isort --check-only src/

      - name: Check C++ formatting
        run: |
          find src/ -name "*.cpp" -o -name "*.hpp" | \
            xargs clang-format --dry-run -Werror

  build:
    name: Build & Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    needs: lint

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Setup ROS2 Humble
        uses: ros-tooling/setup-ros@v0.6
        with:
          required-ros-distributions: humble

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt update
          rosdep update
          rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src -y

      - name: Build
        run: |
          source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
          colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release

      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
          source install/setup.bash
          colcon test --return-code-on-test-failure

      - name: Test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          name: test-results
          path: build/*/test_results/*.xml

  docker:
    name: Docker Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name == 'push'

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v2

      - name: Login to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v4
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          tags: |
            tngblue/jetbot-nanoowl:latest
            tngblue/jetbot-nanoowl:${{ github.sha }}
          cache-from: type=registry,ref=tngblue/jetbot-nanoowl:buildcache
          cache-to: type=registry,ref=tngblue/jetbot-nanoowl:buildcache,mode=max

  docs:
    name: Deploy Documentation
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    needs: build
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'

      - name: Install MkDocs
        run: |
          pip install mkdocs-material mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin

      - name: Build docs
        run: mkdocs build

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          publish_dir: ./site

docs.text:
Docker
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
ARG ROS_DISTRO=humble
ARG BASE_IMAGE=dustynv/ros:${ROS_DISTRO}-pytorch-l4t-r35.4.1

# =============================================================================
# Base Stage: Common dependencies
# =============================================================================
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE} as base

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
WORKDIR /workspace

# Install system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    python3-pip \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install Python dependencies
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# =============================================================================
# Builder Stage: Compile ROS2 packages
# =============================================================================
FROM base as builder

# Copy source code
COPY . /workspace/src/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL

# Install ROS dependencies
RUN . /opt/ros/${ROS_DISTRO}/setup.sh && \
    rosdep update && \
    rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src -y

# Build packages
RUN . /opt/ros/${ROS_DISTRO}/setup.sh && \
    colcon build \
      --symlink-install \
      --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      --parallel-workers 4

# =============================================================================
# Runtime Stage: Minimal runtime image
# =============================================================================
FROM base as runtime

# Copy built packages from builder
COPY --from=builder /workspace/install /workspace/install

# Setup entrypoint
COPY ./docker/entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod +x /entrypoint.sh

ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]
CMD ["ros2", "launch", "jetbot_nanoowl", "bringup.launch.py"]

docs.title: Automated Releases
docs.text:
.github/workflows/release.yml:

YAML
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

jobs:
  release:
    name: Create Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Generate changelog
        id: changelog
        run: |
          # Generate changelog since last tag
          CHANGELOG=$(git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 HEAD^)..HEAD --pretty=format:"- %s (%h)")
          echo "changelog<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "$CHANGELOG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Create Release
        uses: actions/create-release@v1
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ github.ref }}
          release_name: Release ${{ github.ref }}
          body: |
            ## What's Changed
            ${{ steps.changelog.outputs.changelog }}

            ## Docker Images
            ```bash
            docker pull tngblue/jetbot-nanoowl:${{ github.ref_name }}
            ```

          draft: false
          prerelease: false

      - name: Build release artifacts
        run: |
          tar -czf isaac-ros-jetbot-${{ github.ref_name }}.tar.gz src/

      - name: Upload artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-release-asset@v1
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          upload_url: ${{ steps.create_release.outputs.upload_url }}
          asset_path: ./isaac-ros-jetbot-${{ github.ref_name }}.tar.gz
          asset_name: isaac-ros-jetbot-${{ github.ref_name }}.tar.gz
          asset_content_type: application/gzip

docs.text:
Python
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from sensor_msgs.msg import Image
from std_msgs.msg import String


class MyNode(Node):
    """ROS2 node description.

    Subscribes to: /input_topic (Image)
    Publishes to: /output_topic (String)
    """

    def __init__(self):
        """Initialize node."""
        super().__init__('my_node')

        # Declare parameters
        self.declare_parameter('param_name', 'default_value')

        # Create subscribers
        self.subscription = self.create_subscription(
            Image,
            '/input_topic',
            self.callback,
            10
        )

        # Create publishers
        self.publisher = self.create_publisher(
            String,
            '/output_topic',
            10
        )

        # Create timers
        self.timer = self.create_timer(0.1, self.timer_callback)

        self.get_logger().info('Node initialized')

    def callback(self, msg: Image) -> None:
        """Process incoming image message.

        Args:
            msg: Image message from camera
        """
        self.get_logger().debug('Received image')
        # Process message
        result = String()
        result.data = "processed"
        self.publisher.publish(result)

    def timer_callback(self) -> None:
        """Periodic timer callback."""
        pass


def main(args=None):
    """Main entry point."""
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = MyNode()

    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

docs.title: 📋 Release Checklist
docs.text:
Before releasing a new version:

  • All tests passing on main branch

docs.title: 🔢 Version Numbering
docs.text:
We follow Semantic Versioning 2.0.0:

Text Only
MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]

Examples: - 1.0.0 - Initial stable release - 1.1.0 - New feature (backward compatible) - 1.1.1 - Bug fix - 2.0.0 - Breaking change - 2.0.0-beta.1 - Pre-release - 2.0.0+20250126 - Build metadata

docs.title: Incrementing Rules
docs.text:
MAJOR (x.0.0): - Breaking API changes - Incompatible system architecture changes - Major ROS2 version upgrades

MINOR (1.x.0): - New features (backward compatible) - New ROS2 modules - Significant performance improvements - New hardware support

PATCH (1.1.x): - Bug fixes - Documentation updates - Minor performance tweaks - Security patches

# tests/python/test_object_detector.py
import pytest
import numpy as np
from jetbot_detection import ObjectDetector

@pytest.fixture
def detector():
    """Fixture providing detector instance."""
    return ObjectDetector(model_path='models/yolov8n.engine')

@pytest.fixture
def sample_image():
    """Fixture providing test image."""
    return np.random.randint(0, 255, (640, 640, 3), dtype=np.uint8)

class TestObjectDetector:
    """Test suite for ObjectDetector class."""

    def test_initialization(self, detector):
        """Test detector initializes correctly."""
        assert detector is not None
        assert detector.model_path.exists()

    def test_detection_output_format(self, detector, sample_image):
        """Test detection returns correct format."""
        detections = detector.detect(sample_image)

        assert isinstance(detections, list)
        if detections:
            assert 'class' in detections[0]
            assert 'confidence' in detections[0]
            assert 'bbox' in detections[0]

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("confidence", [0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9])
    def test_confidence_thresholds(self, detector, sample_image, confidence):
        """Test different confidence thresholds."""
        detector.confidence_threshold = confidence
        detections = detector.detect(sample_image)

        for det in detections:
            assert det['confidence'] >= confidence

    def test_empty_image_handling(self, detector):
        """Test handling of empty/invalid images."""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            detector.detect(None)

        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            detector.detect(np.array([]))

    @pytest.mark.slow
    def test_performance_benchmark(self, detector, sample_image, benchmark):
        """Benchmark detection performance."""
        result = benchmark(detector.detect, sample_image)
        # Should complete in < 50ms on Jetson Orin Nano
        assert benchmark.stats['mean'] < 0.05

# With coverage

# Specific test

Navigation Test
docs.text:
Python
# tests/e2e/test_autonomous_navigation.py
import pytest
import rclpy
from rclpy.action import ActionClient
from nav2_msgs.action import NavigateToPose
from geometry_msgs.msg import PoseStamped

class TestAutonomousNavigation:
    """E2E test for autonomous navigation."""

    @pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
    def setup(self):
        rclpy.init()
        self.node = rclpy.create_node('test_nav')
        self.nav_client = ActionClient(self.node, NavigateToPose, 'navigate_to_pose')
        yield
        self.node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()

    def test_navigate_to_goal(self):
        """Test robot navigates to goal successfully."""
        # Wait for navigation server
        assert self.nav_client.wait_for_server(timeout_sec=10.0)

        # Create goal
        goal = NavigateToPose.Goal()
        goal.pose.header.frame_id = 'map'
        goal.pose.pose.position.x = 2.0
        goal.pose.pose.position.y = 1.0
        goal.pose.pose.orientation.w = 1.0

        # Send goal
        future = self.nav_client.send_goal_async(goal)
        rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(self.node, future, timeout_sec=60.0)

        goal_handle = future.result()
        assert goal_handle.accepted, "Goal was rejected"

        # Wait for result
        result_future = goal_handle.get_result_async()
        rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(self.node, result_future, timeout_sec=120.0)

        result = result_future.result()
        assert result.status == 4, f"Navigation failed with status {result.status}"

docs.title: Benchmark Suite
docs.text:
Python
# tests/performance/benchmark_detection.py
import time
import numpy as np
import pytest
from jetbot_detection import ObjectDetector

class TestPerformance:
    """Performance benchmarks for detection."""

    @pytest.fixture
    def detector(self):
        return ObjectDetector()

    @pytest.fixture
    def test_images(self):
        """Generate test images of various sizes."""
        sizes = [(416, 416), (640, 640), (1280, 720), (1920, 1080)]
        return {
            f"{w}x{h}": np.random.randint(0, 255, (h, w, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
            for w, h in sizes
        }

    def test_throughput(self, detector, test_images):
        """Measure detection throughput (FPS)."""
        image = test_images['640x640']
        iterations = 100

        start = time.time()
        for _ in range(iterations):
            detector.detect(image)
        duration = time.time() - start

        fps = iterations / duration
        print(f"Throughput: {fps:.2f} FPS")

        # Should achieve 30+ FPS on Jetson Orin Nano
        assert fps >= 30.0, f"Expected >= 30 FPS, got {fps:.2f}"

    def test_latency(self, detector, test_images):
        """Measure detection latency."""
        image = test_images['640x640']
        latencies = []

        # Warm-up
        for _ in range(10):
            detector.detect(image)

        # Measure
        for _ in range(100):
            start = time.perf_counter()
            detector.detect(image)
            latency = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000  # ms
            latencies.append(latency)

        avg_latency = np.mean(latencies)
        p95_latency = np.percentile(latencies, 95)

        print(f"Average latency: {avg_latency:.2f}ms")
        print(f"P95 latency: {p95_latency:.2f}ms")

        assert avg_latency < 35.0, f"Expected < 35ms, got {avg_latency:.2f}ms"
        assert p95_latency < 50.0, f"Expected P95 < 50ms, got {p95_latency:.2f}ms"

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("resolution", ["416x416", "640x640", "1280x720"])
    def test_resolution_scaling(self, detector, test_images, resolution):
        """Test performance across resolutions."""
        image = test_images[resolution]

        start = time.time()
        iterations = 50
        for _ in range(iterations):
            detector.detect(image)
        duration = time.time() - start

        fps = iterations / duration
        print(f"{resolution}: {fps:.2f} FPS")

pytest tests/performance/ -v --benchmark-only

# .github/workflows/test.yml
name: Tests

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Setup ROS2
        uses: ros-tooling/setup-ros@v0.6
        with:
          required-ros-distributions: humble

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          rosdep update
          rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src -y

      - name: Build
        run: colcon build --symlink-install

      - name: Test

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Camera not detected

Problem: Camera node fails to start

Solution: Bash

# Check camera connection
ls /dev/video*

# Test with v4l2
v4l2-ctl --list-devices

# Verify permissions
sudo usermod -aG video $USER

CUDA out of memory

Problem: GPU memory exhausted

Solution: - Reduce batch size in detection config - Lower model resolution - Enable model quantization - See Performance Tuning

ROS2 nodes not communicating

Problem: Nodes can't discover each other

Solution: Bash

# Check ROS_DOMAIN_ID
echo $ROS_DOMAIN_ID

# Verify network
ros2 daemon stop
ros2 daemon start

# Check node graph
ros2 node list
ros2 topic list

More troubleshooting: Getting Started → Troubleshooting

docs.title: 1. ROS2 DDS (Primary)
docs.text:
YAML
Protocol: DDS (Data Distribution Service)
Implementation: FastDDS / CycloneDDS
Transport: UDP Multicast / TCP
Port Range: 7400-7500
QoS Profiles:
  - RELIABLE: Critical data (commands, state)
  - BEST_EFFORT: Sensor data (high frequency)
  - TRANSIENT_LOCAL: Configuration data

Configuration:
  Domain ID: 0-232 (configurable)
  Discovery: Multicast / Simple Discovery Protocol
  Security: DDS Security (optional)

docs.title: ROS2 DDS Configuration
2. WiFi Network
docs.text:
YAML
Standard: IEEE 802.11ac (WiFi 5)
Frequency: 2.4GHz & 5GHz dual-band
Security: WPA3-Personal / WPA2-Enterprise
SSID: jetbot_nanoowl
IP Allocation: DHCP with static reservations

Access Point Settings:
  Channel: Auto (or fixed 36/149 for 5GHz)
  Bandwidth: 40MHz (2.4GHz), 80MHz (5GHz)
  Transmit Power: 20dBm
  Range: 50-100m (indoor), 200m+ (outdoor)

Performance:
  Throughput: 150-300 Mbps (actual)
  Latency: 5-15ms (local network)
  Concurrent Devices: 50+ (depends on AP)

docs.text:

# /etc/netplan/01-network.yaml
network:
  version: 2
  wifis:
    wlan0:
      dhcp4: no
      addresses:
        - 192.168.1.101/24
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 192.168.1.1
      nameservers:
        addresses: [8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4]
      access-points:

docs.title: 4. LoRa Communication
docs.text:
YAML
Frequency: 868 MHz (EU) / 915 MHz (US) / 923 MHz (AS)
Modulation: LoRa CSS (Chirp Spread Spectrum)
Bandwidth: 125 kHz / 250 kHz / 500 kHz
Spreading Factor: SF7-SF12 (configurable)
Coding Rate: 4/5, 4/6, 4/7, 4/8
Max Payload: 255 bytes per packet
Data Rate: 0.3 - 50 kbps (varies with SF)
Range: 1-10 km (urban), up to 20km (line of sight)

Use Cases:
  - Long-range telemetry
  - Emergency communications
  - Image transfer (low-res, compressed)
  - GPS coordinates broadcasting
  - Status updates

docs.title: LoRa Packet Structure
docs.text:
Text Only
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Preamble │ Header │ Payload │ CRC │
│  8 bytes │ 2 bytes│ 0-255 B │ 2 B │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Header Format:
  - Device ID (1 byte)
  - Packet Type (1 byte)
    * 0x01: Telemetry
    * 0x02: Command
    * 0x03: Image Fragment
    * 0x04: ACK/NACK
    * 0x05: Heartbeat

Payload Examples:
  Telemetry:
    - GPS (lat, lon, alt)
    - Battery voltage
    - System status

  Image Transfer:
    - Fragment ID
    - Total fragments
    - Image data (200 bytes)
    - CRC16

Module: Quectel EC25 / Simcom SIM7600

Fallback: 3G HSPA+, 2G EDGE

Use Cases:
  - Internet access in remote areas
  - Cloud connectivity
  - Remote monitoring
  - OTA updates
  - Emergency communications

docs.title: Firewall Configuration
docs.text:
Bash
# iptables rules

# Allow established connections
iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Allow loopback
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT

# Allow SSH (from specific IPs only)
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -s 192.168.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT

# Allow ROS2 DDS ports
iptables -A INPUT -p udp --dport 7400:7500 -s 192.168.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT

# Allow HTTP/HTTPS for API
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

# Allow MQTT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 1883 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 8883 -j ACCEPT

# Drop all other traffic
iptables -A INPUT -j DROP

docs.title: Bandwidth Management
docs.text:
Bash
# Traffic shaping with tc (traffic control)

# Create root qdisc
tc qdisc add dev wlan0 root handle 1: htb default 30

# Add classes with bandwidth limits
tc class add dev wlan0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 100mbit

# High priority: Control commands (30% bandwidth)
tc class add dev wlan0 parent 1:1 classid 1:10 htb rate 30mbit ceil 50mbit prio 1

# Medium priority: Sensor data (50% bandwidth)
tc class add dev wlan0 parent 1:1 classid 1:20 htb rate 50mbit ceil 80mbit prio 2

# Low priority: Other traffic (20% bandwidth)
tc class add dev wlan0 parent 1:1 classid 1:30 htb rate 20mbit ceil 100mbit prio 3

# Add filters to classify traffic
tc filter add dev wlan0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 u32 \
  match ip dport 7400 0xffff flowid 1:10  # ROS2 control
tc filter add dev wlan0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 2 u32 \
  match ip dport 7420 0xffff flowid 1:20  # ROS2 sensors

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: High-level system design and architectural philosophy.

docs.title: 🎯 Design Philosophy
docs.text: The Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL architecture follows these core principles:

docs.title: 1. Layered Architecture
docs.text:
The system is organized into distinct layers, each with specific responsibilities:

graph TB
    Layer1["Application Layer(Web UI, REST API, CLI)"]
    Layer2["ROS2 Middleware Layer(Nodes, Topics, Services)"]
    Layer3["Hardware Abstraction Layer(CUDA, Drivers, Comms)"]
    Layer4["Hardware Layer(Jetson, Sensors, Motors)"]

    Layer1 --> Layer2
    Layer2 --> Layer3
    Layer3 --> Layer4

Benefits: - ✅ Clear separation of concerns - ✅ Easy to test and maintain - ✅ Reusable components - ✅ Scalable design

docs.title: 2. Publish-Subscribe Messaging
docs.text:
ROS2 topics enable loose coupling between components:

graph LR
    CamNode["📷 CameraNode"]
    DetNode["🎯 DetectionNode"]
    NavNode["🗺️ NavigationNode"]

    CamNode -->|"image_raw"| ImageTopic[" "]
    ImageTopic -->|"image_raw"| DetNode
    ImageTopic -->|"image_raw"| NavNode
    DetNode -->|"detections"| DetTopic[" "]
    DetTopic -->|"detections"| NavNode

Advantages: - Components can be developed independently - Easy to add new subscribers/publishers - Asynchronous communication - Scalable to multiple robots

docs.title: 3. Hardware Abstraction
docs.text:
CUDA library provides unified GPU access:

Text Only
ROS2 Nodes
    ↓
CUDA Vision Library
    ↓
NVIDIA Hardware (GPU)

This allows: - Same code on different GPU architectures - Easy optimization without API changes - Fallback to CPU when needed

# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: Continuous Integration

jobs:
  build-and-test:

      - name: Coverage

          lcov --remove coverage.info '/usr/*' --output-file coverage.info

docs.title: Optimization Strategies
docs.text:
YAML
CPU Optimization:
  - Use -O3 optimization flag
  - Enable link-time optimization (LTO)
  - Use march=native for CPU-specific instructions
  - Minimize memory allocations
  - Use memory pools for frequent allocations

GPU Optimization:
  - Batch operations when possible
  - Minimize CPU-GPU transfers
  - Use pinned memory for transfers
  - Optimize kernel launch parameters
  - Use shared memory in kernels

Memory Optimization:
  - Use zero-copy when possible
  - Pre-allocate buffers
  - Reuse memory buffers
  - Use memory-mapped files for large data

I/O Optimization:
  - Use async I/O operations
  - Buffer network data
  - Compress data before transmission
  - Use efficient serialization (e.g., msgpack)

docs.title: C++ Example
docs.text:
Convert image to grayscale and apply Gaussian blur.

C++
#include <jetbot_cuda_vision/cuda_processor.hpp>
#include <jetbot_cuda_vision/image_processing.hpp>
#include <iostream>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

int main() {
    const int WIDTH = 1280;
    const int HEIGHT = 720;
    const size_t IMAGE_SIZE = WIDTH * HEIGHT * 4; // RGBA

    // Allocate GPU memory
    uint8_t *input_gpu, *grayscale_gpu, *blurred_gpu;
    cudaMalloc(&input_gpu, IMAGE_SIZE);
    cudaMalloc(&grayscale_gpu, WIDTH * HEIGHT);
    cudaMalloc(&blurred_gpu, WIDTH * HEIGHT);

    // Load image (pseudocode)
    uint8_t *host_image = new uint8_t[IMAGE_SIZE];
    // ... load image data ...
    cudaMemcpy(input_gpu, host_image, IMAGE_SIZE, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

    // Create processor
    jetbot::CUDAProcessor processor(0, {WIDTH, HEIGHT});

    // Convert to grayscale
    jetbot::grayscaleConvert(input_gpu, grayscale_gpu, WIDTH, HEIGHT,
                             jetbot::ImageFormat::RGBA);

    // Apply Gaussian blur
    jetbot::gaussianBlur(grayscale_gpu, blurred_gpu, WIDTH, HEIGHT, 
                         5, 1.5f);

    // Copy result back
    uint8_t *host_output = new uint8_t[WIDTH * HEIGHT];
    cudaMemcpy(host_output, blurred_gpu, WIDTH * HEIGHT, 
               cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

    std::cout << "✅ Processing complete\n";

    // Cleanup
    cudaFree(input_gpu);
    cudaFree(grayscale_gpu);
    cudaFree(blurred_gpu);
    delete[] host_image;
    delete[] host_output;

    return 0;
}

docs.title: ROS2 Node Implementation
Python ROS2 Node
docs.text:
Python
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from sensor_msgs.msg import Image
from cv_bridge import CvBridge
import jetbot_cuda_vision as jcv
import numpy as np

class CUDAVisionNode(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('cuda_vision_node')

        # Create processor
        self.processor = jcv.CUDAProcessor(gpu_id=0, width=1280, height=720)
        self.bridge = CvBridge()

        # Subscribe to camera
        self.subscription = self.create_subscription(
            Image, '/camera/image_raw', self.image_callback, 10)

        # Publish processed image
        self.publisher = self.create_publisher(Image, '/cuda_vision/processed', 10)

        self.get_logger().info('CUDA Vision Node initialized')

    def image_callback(self, msg):
        # Convert ROS image to OpenCV
        cv_image = self.bridge.imgmsg_to_cv2(msg, desired_encoding='rgba8')

        # Process with CUDA
        gray = jcv.grayscale_convert(cv_image)

        # Convert back to ROS message
        output_msg = self.bridge.cv2_to_imgmsg(gray, encoding='mono8')
        output_msg.header = msg.header

        self.publisher.publish(output_msg)

def main(args=None):
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = CUDAVisionNode()
    rclpy.spin(node)
    node.destroy_node()
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

docs.title: 📌 Example 5: Multi-Stream Processing
docs.text:
Process multiple frames in parallel.

C++
#include <jetbot_cuda_vision/cuda_processor.hpp>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <chrono>

int main() {
    const int WIDTH = 640;
    const int HEIGHT = 480;
    const int NUM_STREAMS = 4;
    const int NUM_FRAMES = 100;

    // Create processor with streaming enabled
    jetbot::CUDAProcessor processor(0, {WIDTH, HEIGHT});
    processor.enableStreaming(NUM_STREAMS);

    // Allocate memory for multiple frames
    std::vector<uint8_t*> input_frames(NUM_STREAMS);
    std::vector<uint8_t*> output_frames(NUM_STREAMS);

    for (int i = 0; i < NUM_STREAMS; i++) {
        cudaMalloc(&input_frames[i], WIDTH * HEIGHT * 4);
        cudaMalloc(&output_frames[i], WIDTH * HEIGHT);
    }

    // Host memory for results
    std::vector<uint8_t*> host_results(NUM_STREAMS);
    for (int i = 0; i < NUM_STREAMS; i++) {
        cudaMallocHost(&host_results[i], WIDTH * HEIGHT);
    }

    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();

    // Process frames
    for (int f = 0; f < NUM_FRAMES; f++) {
        int stream_idx = f % NUM_STREAMS;

        // Simulate input data
        // In real usage, load actual frame data

        // Enqueue processing
        jetbot::grayscaleConvert(input_frames[stream_idx], 
                                output_frames[stream_idx],
                                WIDTH, HEIGHT, jetbot::ImageFormat::RGBA);

        // Copy result (async)
        cudaMemcpyAsync(host_results[stream_idx], 
                       output_frames[stream_idx],
                       WIDTH * HEIGHT,
                       cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
    }

    // Synchronize all streams
    cudaDeviceSynchronize();

    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>
                   (end - start).count();

    double fps = (NUM_FRAMES * 1000.0) / duration;
    std::cout << "Processed " << NUM_FRAMES << " frames in " 
              << duration << "ms\n";
    std::cout << "Throughput: " << fps << " FPS\n";

    // Cleanup
    for (int i = 0; i < NUM_STREAMS; i++) {
        cudaFree(input_frames[i]);
        cudaFree(output_frames[i]);
        cudaFreeHost(host_results[i]);
    }

    return 0;
}

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy) for Jetson Orin Nano
  • CUDA: CUDA 12.2+ (pre-installed on Jetson)
  • cuDNN: 8.6+
  • TensorRT: 8.6+
  • CMake: 3.22+
  • GCC: 11.0+

docs.title: Verify NVIDIA Stack
docs.text:
Bash
# Check CUDA version
nvcc --version

# Verify GPU
nvidia-smi

# Check cuDNN
dpkg -l | grep cudnn

# Verify TensorRT
dpkg -l | grep tensorrt

Expected output: Text Only

CUDA Version: 12.2
GPU: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano
Driver Version: 560.35

docs.title: 1. Clone Repository
docs.text:
Bash
cd ~/ros2_ws/src
git clone https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/CUDA

docs.title: 2. Install Dependencies
docs.text:
Bash
# Update system packages
sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade -y

# Install build tools
sudo apt install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    pkg-config

# Install CUDA development headers
sudo apt install -y \
    cuda-toolkit-12-2 \
    libcudnn8-dev \
    tensorrt \
    tensorrt-dev

# Install ROS2 dependencies
sudo apt install -y \
    ros-humble-ros-core \
    ros-humble-geometry2 \
    ros-humble-sensor-msgs

# Install Python development
sudo apt install -y \
    python3-dev \
    python3-pip \
    pybind11-dev

docs.title: 3. Configure CMake
docs.text:
Bash
cd ~/ros2_ws/src/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/CUDA

# Create build directory
mkdir -p build
cd build

# Configure with CMake
cmake .. \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DCUDA_ARCH_BIN="87" \
    -DENABLE_PYTHON_BINDINGS=ON \
    -DENABLE_TENSORRT=ON

CMake Options:

Option Default Description CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release Build type (Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo) CUDA_ARCH_BIN 87 CUDA architecture for Orin Nano ENABLE_PYTHON_BINDINGS ON Build Python bindings ENABLE_TENSORRT ON Enable TensorRT integration ENABLE_TESTS ON Build unit tests ENABLE_EXAMPLES ON Build example applications

docs.title: 4. Build and Install
docs.text:
Bash
# Build
cmake --build . --config Release -j$(nproc)

# Run tests (optional)
ctest --output-on-failure

# Install
sudo cmake --install . --prefix /usr/local

# Build ROS2 package (if in workspace)
cd ~/ros2_ws
colcon build --packages-select jetbot_cuda_vision --symlink-install
source install/setup.bash

docs.title: Install Python Bindings
docs.text:
Bash
# Option 1: From system install
python3 -m pip install /usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/jetbot_cuda_vision

# Option 2: From development source
cd ~/ros2_ws/src/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/CUDA
python3 -m pip install -e .

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Python
# Python verification script
python3 << 'EOF'
import jetbot_cuda_vision as jcv

# Check library version
print(f"CUDA Vision Version: {jcv.__version__}")

# Verify GPU availability
print(f"GPU Available: {jcv.is_cuda_available()}")
print(f"CUDA Devices: {jcv.get_device_count()}")

# Test basic functionality
processor = jcv.CUDAProcessor(gpu_id=0)
print(f"Processor initialized: {processor}")
EOF

Bash
cmake .. -DENABLE_PYTHON_BINDINGS=OFF

docs.title: Debug Build with Symbols
docs.text:
Bash
cmake .. \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -DCUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION=ON

docs.title: Enable NCCL for Multi-GPU (future)
docs.text:
Bash
cmake .. -DENABLE_NCCL=ON

docs.title: Optimize for Jetson Orin NX
docs.text:
Bash

cmake .. -DCUDA_ARCH_BIN="87"

docs.title: Optimize for Jetson Orin AGX
docs.text:
Bash

cmake .. -DCUDA_ARCH_BIN="87"

docs.title: Issue: CUDA Not Found
docs.text:
Bash
# Verify CUDA installation
ls /usr/local/cuda-12.2/

# Set CUDA_PATH if needed
export CUDA_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.2
cmake ..

docs.title: Issue: cuDNN Library Not Found
docs.text:
Bash
# Check cuDNN installation
find /usr -name "libcudnn*" 2>/dev/null

# Install cuDNN if missing
sudo apt install -y libcudnn8-dev

docs.title: Issue: CMake Configuration Error
docs.text:
Bash
# Clean build directory
cd build
rm -rf *

# Reconfigure with verbose output
cmake .. -DCMAKE_VERBOSE_MAKEFILE=ON

# Check for specific errors
cmake .. 2>&1 | grep "error"

docs.title: Issue: Out of Memory During Build
docs.text:
Bash
# Reduce parallel build jobs
cmake --build . -j2

# Or use monolithic build
make -j1

docs.title: Issue: Python Binding Import Error
docs.text:
Bash
# Check Python version compatibility
python3 --version

# Verify binding location
python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.path)"
find /usr/local -name "*jetbot_cuda_vision*"

# Reinstall bindings
sudo python3 -m pip install --force-reinstall .

docs.title: C++ Verification
System Integration Check
docs.text:
Bash
# Check environment
echo "CUDA_PATH: $CUDA_PATH"
echo "LD_LIBRARY_PATH: $LD_LIBRARY_PATH"

# Verify ROS2 integration
ros2 pkg list | grep jetbot_cuda_vision

# Check system libraries
ldconfig -p | grep cuda

docs.title: Update to Latest Version
docs.text:
Bash
cd ~/ros2_ws/src/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
git pull origin master

cd CUDA/build
cmake ..
cmake --build . -j$(nproc)
sudo cmake --install .

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Bash
# Remove system installation
sudo rm -rf /usr/local/include/jetbot_cuda_vision
sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/*cuda_vision*

# Remove Python bindings
python3 -m pip uninstall jetbot_cuda_vision -y

# Clean build directory
cd ~/ros2_ws/src/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/CUDA
rm -rf build

docs.title: CUDA Vision Overview
docs.text: High-performance GPU-accelerated computer vision library for NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose and Goals
docs.text: The CUDA Vision Library provides optimized, GPU-accelerated computer vision components tailored for the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano platform.

docs.title: Primary Objectives
docs.text:
1. Performance: Maximize throughput with GPU acceleration
  2. Efficiency: Minimize power consumption and latency
  3. Flexibility: Support multiple vision algorithms
  4. Integration: Seamless ROS2 integration
  5. Scalability: Handle multiple inference streams

docs.title: 🚀 Performance Acceleration
docs.text:
• CUDA Kernels: Custom-optimized image processing kernels
  • TensorRT Integration: FP16/INT8 quantization support
  • Multi-threading: Parallel processing pipeline
  • Zero-copy Memory: GPU-pinned memory for efficiency
  • Stream Processing: Async kernel execution
graph TB
    Input["Input ImageCPU Memory"]
    PinMem["GPU-PinnedMemory"]
    Process["CUDAProcessing"]
    TensorRT["TensorRTInference"]
    Output["OutputGPU Memory"]

    Input -->|"DMA Transfer"| PinMem
    PinMem -->|"Zero-copy"| Process
    Process --> TensorRT
    TensorRT --> Output

docs.title: Image Processing
docs.text:
• Grayscale conversion (optimized kernels)
  • Gaussian blur and edge detection
  • Histogram equalization
  • Color space conversion (RGB/HSV/YUV)
  • Image resizing and warping
  • Morphological operations

docs.title: Feature Extraction
docs.text:
• SIFT/SURF acceleration
  • ORB feature detection
  • Harris corner detection
  • Hough transform for line/circle detection

docs.title: Video Processing
docs.text:
• Frame rate conversion
  • Motion detection
  • Temporal filtering
  • Multi-stream processing

docs.title: 🔌 API Design
docs.text:
The CUDA Vision Library offers multiple interfaces:

C++
// High-level C++ API
CUDAProcessor processor(GPU_ID, IMAGE_SIZE);
processor.processFrame(input_gpu_buffer, output_gpu_buffer);

// Low-level CUDA kernels
cuda_grayscale_kernel(input, output, width, height);
cuda_gaussian_blur_kernel(input, output, kernel_size, sigma);

// Python bindings
from jetbot_cuda_vision import CUDAProcessor
processor = CUDAProcessor(gpu_id=0, image_size=(1280, 720))
output = processor.process_frame(input_array)

docs.title: 🎯 Optimization Checklist
docs.text:
• Use pinned memory for host-device transfers
  • Pre-allocate GPU memory outside loops
  • Enable streaming for multi-frame processing
  • Use appropriate kernel sizes (start with 3×3)
  • Profile with nsys/ncu to identify bottlenecks
  • Fuse kernels when processing same data
  • Monitor GPU power consumption
  • Use double buffering for continuous streams
  • Keep memory alignment (32 bytes minimum)
  • Batch operations when possible

docs.title: Block and Thread Configuration
Memory Coalescing
docs.text:
Ensure global memory accesses are coalesced:

CUDA
// Good: Memory coalescing
__global__ void good_kernel(const uint8_t* input, uint8_t* output) {
    int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    output[idx] = process(input[idx]);  // Sequential memory access
}

// Bad: Non-coalesced access
__global__ void bad_kernel(const uint8_t* input, uint8_t* output) {
    int idx = (blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x) * stride;
    output[idx] = process(input[idx]);  // Strided access
}

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Bash
# Build container
docker build -t jetbot:latest -f Dockerfile .

# Run container
docker run --gpus all \
  --privileged \
  -v /dev:/dev \
  -it jetbot:latest

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
YAML
version: '3.8'

services:
  ros2:
    image: jetbot:ros2
    environment:
      ROS_DOMAIN_ID: 0
    volumes:
      - /dev:/dev
    devices:
      - /dev/nvidia0:/dev/nvidia0
    privileged: true

  api:
    image: jetbot:api
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    depends_on:
      - ros2

docs.title: Deployment Manifest
docs.text:
YAML
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: jetbot-ros2
  namespace: jetbot
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: jetbot
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: jetbot
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ros2
        image: jetbot:ros2
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
        volumeMounts:
        - name: dev
          mountPath: /dev
      volumes:
      - name: dev
        hostPath:
          path: /dev

# File: aws-deployment.yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL - AWS CloudFormation Stack'

Parameters:
  InstanceType:
    Type: String
    Default: t3.medium
  DBInstanceClass:
    Type: String
    Default: db.t3.micro

Resources:
  # VPC
  JetbotVPC:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      EnableDnsSupport: true

  # Subnet
  JetbotSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref JetbotVPC
      CidrBlock: 10.0.1.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: us-east-1a

  # EC2 Instance
  JetbotControlPlane:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Instance
    Properties:
      ImageId: ami-0c55b159cbfafe1f0
      InstanceType: !Ref InstanceType
      SubnetId: !Ref JetbotSubnet
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: jetbot-control

  # RDS Database
  JetbotDatabase:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties:
      DBInstanceIdentifier: jetbot-db
      DBInstanceClass: !Ref DBInstanceClass
      Engine: mysql
      MasterUsername: admin
      MasterUserPassword: !Sub '{{resolve:secretsmanager:jetbot-db-password:SecretString:password}}'
      AllocatedStorage: 20
      BackupRetentionPeriod: 7

  # S3 Bucket
  JetbotBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub 'jetbot-fleet-data-${AWS::AccountId}'
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled

Outputs:
  ControlPlaneIP:
    Value: !GetAtt JetbotControlPlane.PublicIp
  DatabaseEndpoint:
    Value: !GetAtt JetbotDatabase.Endpoint.Address
  S3BucketName:
    Value: !Ref JetbotBucket

docs.title: AWS Kinesis Streaming
docs.text:
Python
# File: ~/ros2_ws/src/jetbot_cloud/cloud_sync.py
import boto3
import json
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from sensor_msgs.msg import Imu

class CloudSync(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('cloud_sync')

        # Initialize AWS clients
        self.kinesis_client = boto3.client('kinesis', region_name='us-east-1')
        self.s3_client = boto3.client('s3')

        # Subscribe to sensor data
        self.imu_sub = self.create_subscription(
            Imu, '/imu/data', self.imu_callback, 10)

        self.robot_id = 'jetbot-1'
        self.stream_name = 'jetbot-telemetry'

    def imu_callback(self, msg):
        """Stream IMU data to Kinesis"""
        data = {
            'robot_id': self.robot_id,
            'timestamp': self.get_clock().now().to_msg().sec,
            'imu': {
                'acceleration_x': float(msg.linear_acceleration.x),
                'acceleration_y': float(msg.linear_acceleration.y),
                'acceleration_z': float(msg.linear_acceleration.z),
                'angular_velocity_x': float(msg.angular_velocity.x),
                'angular_velocity_y': float(msg.angular_velocity.y),
                'angular_velocity_z': float(msg.angular_velocity.z),
            }
        }

        try:
            self.kinesis_client.put_record(
                StreamName=self.stream_name,
                Data=json.dumps(data),
                PartitionKey=self.robot_id
            )
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Failed to sync data: {e}")

docs.title: Google Pub/Sub Integration
docs.text:
Python
# File: pubsub_sync.py
from google.cloud import pubsub_v1
import json

class PubSubSync:
    def __init__(self, project_id, topic_name):
        self.publisher = pubsub_v1.PublisherClient()
        self.topic_path = self.publisher.topic_path(project_id, topic_name)

    def publish_telemetry(self, data):
        """Publish telemetry to Pub/Sub"""
        message_json = json.dumps(data)
        message_bytes = message_json.encode('utf-8')

        publish_future = self.publisher.publish(
            self.topic_path, message_bytes)

        message_id = publish_future.result()
        print(f"Published message ID: {message_id}")

COPY . .

RUN apt-get update && \

RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y ros-humble-desktop

COPY --from=builder /build/install /opt/ros/jetbot/install

docs.title: Full Stack Deployment
docs.text:
YAML
# File: Docker/compose/docker-compose.yml
version: '3.8'

services:
  # Motor Controller
  motor_controller:
    image: jetbot_nanoowl:latest
    container_name: motor_controller
    runtime: nvidia
    environment:
      - NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all
      - ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
    devices:
      - /dev/ttyUSB0:/dev/ttyUSB0  # Serial port
      - /dev/video0:/dev/video0     # Camera
    volumes:
      - ./data:/home/jetbot/data
      - ./config:/home/jetbot/config
    networks:
      - jetbot_network
    command: ros2 launch jetbot_control motor_controller.launch.py

  # Object Detection
  detection:
    image: object_detection_isaac_ros:latest
    container_name: detection
    runtime: nvidia
    environment:
      - NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all
      - ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
    depends_on:
      - motor_controller
    volumes:
      - ./models:/home/jetbot/models
      - ./data:/home/jetbot/data
    networks:
      - jetbot_network
    command: ros2 launch jetbot_detection detection.launch.py

  # SLAM & Navigation
  slam:
    image: lidar_slam:latest
    container_name: slam
    runtime: nvidia
    environment:
      - NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all
      - ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
    depends_on:
      - motor_controller
    volumes:
      - ./maps:/home/jetbot/maps
      - ./data:/home/jetbot/data
    networks:
      - jetbot_network
    command: ros2 launch jetbot_slam slam.launch.py

  # OTA Update Server
  ota_server:
    image: server_ota:latest
    container_name: ota_server
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./updates:/app/updates
      - ./logs:/app/logs
    networks:
      - jetbot_network
    environment:
      - PORT=8080
      - UPDATE_DIR=/app/updates

  # Monitoring
  monitoring:
    image: jetbot_nanoowl:latest
    container_name: monitoring
    environment:
      - ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
    depends_on:
      - motor_controller
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    networks:
      - jetbot_network
    command: bash -c "source install/setup.bash && ros2 run jetbot_monitoring monitoring_node"

  # OLED Display (optional)
  oled:
    image: oled:latest
    container_name: oled
    devices:
      - /dev/i2c-1:/dev/i2c-1
    environment:
      - ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
    depends_on:
      - motor_controller
    networks:
      - jetbot_network
    command: ros2 run jetbot_display oled_node

networks:
  jetbot_network:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  data:
    driver: local
  models:
    driver: local
  maps:
    driver: local

# File: Helm/charts/jetbot-nanoowl/Chart.yaml
apiVersion: v2
name: jetbot-nanoowl
description: |
  Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Helm Chart

type: application

keywords:

sources:

maintainers:
  - name: TNG Blue Team
    email: contact@tngblue.com

dependencies:
  - name: prometheus
    version: "15.x"
    repository: https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts

docs.title: values.yaml
docs.text:
YAML
# File: Helm/charts/jetbot-nanoowl/values.yaml

# Global settings
global:
  namespace: jetbot
  environment: production

# Motor Controller Deployment
motorController:
  enabled: true
  replicaCount: 1
  image:
    repository: tngblue/jetbot_nanoowl
    tag: "2.0.0"
    pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  resources:
    requests:
      memory: "1Gi"
      cpu: "500m"
      nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    limits:
      memory: "2Gi"
      cpu: "1000m"
      nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  nodeSelector:
    jetbot: "true"
  env:
    ROS_DOMAIN_ID: "0"
    ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY: "0"

# Object Detection Deployment
detection:
  enabled: true
  replicaCount: 1
  image:
    repository: tngblue/object_detection_isaac_ros
    tag: "2.0.0"
    pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  resources:
    requests:
      memory: "2Gi"
      cpu: "1000m"
      nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    limits:
      memory: "4Gi"
      cpu: "2000m"
      nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  modelPath: /home/jetbot/models
  confidenceThreshold: 0.5

# SLAM Deployment
slam:
  enabled: true
  replicaCount: 1
  image:
    repository: tngblue/lidar_slam
    tag: "2.0.0"
  resources:
    requests:
      memory: "2Gi"
      cpu: "1000m"
    limits:
      memory: "3Gi"
      cpu: "1500m"

# Storage
storage:
  enabled: true
  className: fast-ssd
  size: 10Gi
  mountPath: /home/jetbot/data

# Service configuration
service:
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    ros2: 11311
    rest: 8080
    metrics: 9090

# Networking
networking:
  podNetworkPolicy:
    enabled: true
  ingress:
    enabled: false
    hosts:
      - jetbot.example.com

# Monitoring
monitoring:
  enabled: true
  prometheus:
    enabled: true
    retention: 15d
    scrapeInterval: 30s

# Logging
logging:
  enabled: true
  elasticsearch:
    enabled: true
  kibana:
    enabled: true

# Security
security:
  rbac:
    enabled: true
  networkPolicy:
    enabled: true
  podSecurityPolicy:
    enabled: true

# High Availability
ha:
  enabled: false
  replicaCount: 3
  antiAffinity: soft

# Multi-robot support
multiRobot:
  enabled: true
  robotCount: 1
  robots: []
    # - name: jetbot-1
    #   nodeSelector: jetbot-1
    #   robotId: 1

docs.title: Deployment Template
docs.text:
YAML
# File: Helm/charts/jetbot-nanoowl/templates/deployment.yaml
{{- if .Values.motorController.enabled }}
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ include "jetbot-nanoowl.fullname" . }}-motor-controller
  namespace: {{ .Values.global.namespace }}
  labels:
    {{- include "jetbot-nanoowl.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.motorController.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "jetbot-nanoowl.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
      component: motor-controller
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "jetbot-nanoowl.selectorLabels" . | nindent 8 }}
        component: motor-controller
    spec:
      {{- with .Values.motorController.nodeSelector }}
      nodeSelector:
        {{- toYaml . | nindent 8 }}
      {{- end }}
      containers:
      - name: motor-controller
        image: "{{ .Values.motorController.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.motorController.image.tag }}"
        imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.motorController.image.pullPolicy }}
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: {{ include "jetbot-nanoowl.fullname" . }}-config
        resources:
          {{- toYaml .Values.motorController.resources | nindent 12 }}
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: {{ .Values.storage.mountPath }}
        - name: serial
          mountPath: /dev/ttyUSB0
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: {{ include "jetbot-nanoowl.fullname" . }}-pvc
      - name: serial
        hostPath:
          path: /dev/ttyUSB0
          type: CharDevice
{{- end }}

  {{- end }}

docs.title: Kubernetes Deployment
docs.text: Deploy Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL on Kubernetes clusters.

docs.title: 📚 Overview
docs.text:
Kubernetes enables scalable, automated container orchestration for Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL systems, supporting multiple robots and edge deployments.

Benefits: - ✅ Automated scaling - ✅ Self-healing - ✅ Rolling updates - ✅ Multi-robot coordination - ✅ High availability - ✅ Resource management

docs.title: Cluster Components
docs.text:
YAML
Kubernetes Cluster:
├── Control Plane
│   ├── API Server
│   ├── Scheduler
│   ├── Controller Manager
│   └── etcd (data store)
├── Worker Nodes
│   ├── Robot 1 (Jetson Orin Nano)
│   ├── Robot 2 (Jetson Orin Nano)
│   └── Robot N
└── Add-ons
    ├── DNS
    ├── Networking (CNI)
    ├── Monitoring (Prometheus)
    └── Logging (ELK)

docs.title: Deployment Topology
docs.text:
graph TB
    subgraph "Kubernetes Control Plane"
        API["API Server"]
        Scheduler["Scheduler"]
        Controller["Controller Manager"]
    end

    subgraph "Worker Nodes"
        subgraph "Node 1: Jetbot-1"
            Motor1["Motor Controller"]
            Detect1["Detection"]
            SLAM1["SLAM"]
        end

        subgraph "Node 2: Jetbot-2"
            Motor2["Motor Controller"]
            Detect2["Detection"]
            SLAM2["SLAM"]
        end
    end

    subgraph "Services"
        OTA["OTA Server"]
        Monitor["Monitoring"]
    end

    API --> Scheduler

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Bash
# Install kubectl
curl -LO "https://dl.k8s.io/release/$(curl -L -s https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl"
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0755 kubectl /usr/local/bin/kubectl

# Verify installation
kubectl version --client

# Install kubeadm & kubelet
sudo apt-get install -y kubeadm kubelet kubernetes-cni

# Start kubelet service
sudo systemctl start kubelet
sudo systemctl enable kubelet

docs.title: Initialize Kubernetes Cluster
docs.text:
Bash
# Initialize control plane (on master node)
sudo kubeadm init \
  --pod-network-cidr=10.244.0.0/16 \
  --kubernetes-version=stable

# Configure kubectl
mkdir -p $HOME/.kube
sudo cp -i /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf $HOME/.kube/config
sudo chown $(id -u):$(id -g) $HOME/.kube/config

# Install networking addon (Flannel)
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreos/flannel/master/Documentation/kube-flannel.yml

# Verify cluster
kubectl get nodes
kubectl get pods -A
