docs.title: Client Configuration
OTA Client Implementation
docs.text:
Python
# File: ~/ros2_ws/src/jetbot_ota/ota_client.py
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
import requests
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path

class OTAClient(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('ota_client')

        self.config = OTAConfig('/home/jetbot/.jetbot/ota-config.yaml')
        self.robot_id = self.get_robot_id()
        self.current_version = self.get_current_version()

        # Timer for checking updates
        self.timer = self.create_timer(
            self.config.check_interval,
            self.check_for_updates
        )

        self.get_logger().info(f"OTA Client initialized. Robot: {self.robot_id}")

    def check_for_updates(self):
        """Check update server for new versions"""
        try:
            response = requests.get(
                f"{self.config.update_server}/api/v1/latest-update",
                params={"robot_id": self.robot_id},
                timeout=10
            )

            if response.status_code == 200:
                update_info = response.json()

                if update_info['version'] > self.current_version:
                    self.get_logger().info(
                        f"Update available: {update_info['version']}"
                    )

                    if self.config.auto_update:
                        self.download_and_install(update_info)
                    else:
                        self.notify_update_available(update_info)

        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Failed to check updates: {e}")

    def download_and_install(self, update_info):
        """Download and install update"""
        try:
            # Download
            self.get_logger().info(f"Downloading update {update_info['version']}")
            self.download_update(update_info)

            # Verify
            if not self.verify_update(update_info):
                raise Exception("Checksum verification failed")

            # Backup current
            self.backup_current_version()

            # Install
            self.get_logger().info("Installing update...")
            self.install_update(update_info)

            # Verify installation
            if self.verify_installation(update_info):
                self.get_logger().info("Update installed successfully")
                self.current_version = update_info['version']
                self.report_update_status("completed", update_info)
            else:
                raise Exception("Installation verification failed")

        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Update failed: {e}")
            self.rollback_update()
            self.report_update_status("failed", update_info)

    def download_update(self, update_info):
        """Download update file"""
        url = update_info['download_url']
        output_file = Path(f"/tmp/{update_info['filename']}")

        response = requests.get(url, stream=True)
        total_size = int(response.headers.get('content-length', 0))

        with open(output_file, 'wb') as f:
            downloaded = 0
            for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=8192):
                f.write(chunk)
                downloaded += len(chunk)
                progress = (downloaded / total_size) * 100
                self.get_logger().debug(f"Download progress: {progress:.1f}%")

    def verify_update(self, update_info):
        """Verify update checksum"""
        import hashlib

        file_path = Path(f"/tmp/{update_info['filename']}")
        sha256_hash = hashlib.sha256()

        with open(file_path, 'rb') as f:
            for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(4096), b''):
                sha256_hash.update(chunk)

        actual_checksum = sha256_hash.hexdigest()
        expected_checksum = update_info['checksum'].replace('sha256:', '')

        return actual_checksum == expected_checksum

    def install_update(self, update_info):
        """Install update"""
        subprocess.run([
            'sudo', 'systemctl', 'stop', 'jetbot-ros2'
        ])

        # Install logic depends on update type
        if update_info['type'] == 'firmware':
            self.install_firmware(update_info)
        elif update_info['type'] == 'software':
            self.install_software(update_info)

        subprocess.run([
            'sudo', 'systemctl', 'start', 'jetbot-ros2'
        ])

    def rollback_update(self):
        """Rollback to previous version"""
        self.get_logger().warn("Rolling back update...")
        subprocess.run(['sudo', '/usr/local/bin/rollback-update.sh'])

    def report_update_status(self, status, update_info):
        """Report update status to server"""
        try:
            requests.post(
                f"{self.config.update_server}/api/v1/update-status",
                json={
                    "robot_id": self.robot_id,
                    "update_id": update_info['id'],
                    "status": status,
                    "timestamp": time.time()
                }
            )
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Failed to report status: {e}")

def main():
    rclpy.init()
    client = OTAClient()
    rclpy.spin(client)
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

docs.text:
Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
import board
import busio
import digitalio
from adafruit_rfm9x import RFM9x

class LoRaNode(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('lora_node')

        # Configure LoRa
        spi = busio.SPI(board.SCK, MOSI=board.MOSI, MISO=board.MISO)
        cs = digitalio.DigitalInOut(board.CE0)
        reset = digitalio.DigitalInOut(board.D24)

        self.rfm9x = RFM9x(spi, cs, reset, 915.0)
        self.rfm9x.tx_power = 23  # Max power

        # Subscribe to telemetry
        self.subscription = self.create_subscription(
            String,
            '/telemetry',
            self.telemetry_callback,
            10
        )

    def telemetry_callback(self, msg):
        # Send via LoRa
        self.rfm9x.send(bytes(msg.data, 'utf-8'))
        self.get_logger().info(f'Sent: {msg.data}')

def transmit_image(image_data):
    # Compress image
    import cv2
    _, buffer = cv2.imencode('.jpg', image_data, [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, 20])
    compressed = buffer.tobytes()

    # Split into chunks (256 bytes max per LoRa packet)
    chunk_size = 256
    chunks = [compressed[i:i+chunk_size] for i in range(0, len(compressed), chunk_size)]

    # Transmit with acknowledgment
    for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks):
        packet = f"{i}/{len(chunks)}:".encode() + chunk
        rfm9x.send(packet)
        time.sleep(0.5)  # Wait for transmission

docs.title: ROS2 Bridge Node
docs.text:
Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
ROS2 node for communicating with Arduino Portenta H7
"""

import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist
from nav_msgs.msg import Odometry
from sensor_msgs.msg import JointState
import serial
import threading

class PortentaBridgeNode(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('portenta_bridge_node')

        # Parameters
        self.declare_parameter('serial_port', '/dev/ttyACM0')
        self.declare_parameter('baud_rate', 115200)
        self.declare_parameter('wheel_separation', 0.15)  # meters
        self.declare_parameter('wheel_radius', 0.033)    # meters

        port = self.get_parameter('serial_port').value
        baud = self.get_parameter('baud_rate').value

        # Serial connection
        self.serial = serial.Serial(port, baud, timeout=0.1)
        self.serial.reset_input_buffer()

        # ROS2 subscriptions
        self.cmd_vel_sub = self.create_subscription(
            Twist,
            '/cmd_vel',
            self.cmd_vel_callback,
            10
        )

        # ROS2 publishers
        self.odom_pub = self.create_publisher(Odometry, '/odom', 10)
        self.joint_state_pub = self.create_publisher(JointState, '/joint_states', 10)

        # Start serial read thread
        self.read_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.read_serial, daemon=True)
        self.read_thread.start()

        self.get_logger().info('Portenta bridge node started')

    def cmd_vel_callback(self, msg):
        """Convert Twist message to differential drive velocities"""
        linear = msg.linear.x
        angular = msg.angular.z

        wheel_sep = self.get_parameter('wheel_separation').value

        # Differential drive kinematics
        left_vel = linear - (angular * wheel_sep / 2.0)
        right_vel = linear + (angular * wheel_sep / 2.0)

        # Send command to Portenta
        cmd = f"VEL {left_vel:.4f} {right_vel:.4f}\n"
        self.serial.write(cmd.encode())

    def read_serial(self):
        """Thread for reading serial data from Portenta"""
        while rclpy.ok():
            try:
                if self.serial.in_waiting:
                    line = self.serial.readline().decode('utf-8').strip()
                    self.process_telemetry(line)
            except Exception as e:
                self.get_logger().error(f'Serial read error: {e}')

    def process_telemetry(self, line):
        """Process telemetry data from Portenta"""
        parts = line.split()

        if parts[0] == 'TEL' and len(parts) == 5:
            # Parse telemetry: TEL vel_l vel_r enc_l enc_r
            vel_left = float(parts[1])
            vel_right = float(parts[2])
            enc_left = int(parts[3])
            enc_right = int(parts[4])

            # Publish odometry
            self.publish_odometry(vel_left, vel_right)

            # Publish joint states
            self.publish_joint_states(vel_left, vel_right)

        elif parts[0] == 'STATUS' and len(parts) == 4:
            # Parse status: STATUS battery temp current
            battery = float(parts[1])
            temp = float(parts[2])
            current = float(parts[3])

            self.get_logger().info(
                f'Status - Battery: {battery}V, Temp: {temp}°C, Current: {current}A'
            )

        elif parts[0] == 'ERR':
            # Error message
            self.get_logger().error(f'Portenta error: {" ".join(parts[1:])}')

    def publish_odometry(self, vel_left, vel_right):
        """Publish odometry message"""
        # Calculate linear and angular velocities
        wheel_sep = self.get_parameter('wheel_separation').value

        linear = (vel_left + vel_right) / 2.0
        angular = (vel_right - vel_left) / wheel_sep

        # Create and publish Odometry message
        msg = Odometry()
        msg.header.stamp = self.get_clock().now().to_msg()
        msg.header.frame_id = 'odom'
        msg.child_frame_id = 'base_link'

        msg.twist.twist.linear.x = linear
        msg.twist.twist.angular.z = angular

        self.odom_pub.publish(msg)

    def publish_joint_states(self, vel_left, vel_right):
        """Publish joint states message"""
        msg = JointState()
        msg.header.stamp = self.get_clock().now().to_msg()
        msg.name = ['left_wheel_joint', 'right_wheel_joint']
        msg.velocity = [vel_left, vel_right]

        self.joint_state_pub.publish(msg)

def main(args=None):
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = PortentaBridgeNode()

    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        node.serial.close()
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""
OpenMV RT1062 - QR Code Scanner
Streams QR code data to Jetson via UART
"""

import sensor
import image
import time
import pyb

# Initialize camera
sensor.reset()
sensor.set_pixformat(sensor.RGB565)
sensor.set_framesize(sensor.QVGA)  # 320x240
sensor.skip_frames(time=2000)
sensor.set_auto_gain(False)
sensor.set_auto_whitebal(False)

# Initialize UART for Jetson communication
uart = pyb.UART(3, 115200, timeout_char=1000)

# LED indicator
led = pyb.LED(1)  # Red LED

print("OpenMV RT1062 - QR Code Scanner")
print("Streaming to Jetson via UART3...")

clock = time.clock()

while True:
    clock.tick()
    img = sensor.snapshot()

    # Detect QR codes
    qr_codes = img.find_qrcodes()

    if qr_codes:
        for qr in qr_codes:
            # Draw rectangle around QR code
            img.draw_rectangle(qr.rect(), color=(255, 0, 0))

            # Send data to Jetson
            data = qr.payload()
            uart.write(f"QR:{data}\n")

            # Blink LED
            led.on()
            pyb.delay(100)
            led.off()

            print(f"QR Code detected: {data}")

    # Display FPS
    fps = clock.fps()
    img.draw_string(5, 5, f"FPS: {fps:.1f}", color=(255, 255, 255), scale=2)

"""
OpenMV RT1062 - Color Blob Detection
Tracks colored objects and sends centroid to Jetson
"""

import sensor
import image
import time
import pyb

# Color thresholds (L, A, B)
# Use Tools -> Machine Vision -> Threshold Editor in OpenMV IDE
red_threshold = (30, 100, 15, 127, 15, 127)
green_threshold = (30, 100, -64, -8, -32, 32)
blue_threshold = (0, 30, 0, 64, -128, 0)

# Initialize
sensor.reset()
sensor.set_pixformat(sensor.RGB565)
sensor.set_framesize(sensor.QVGA)
sensor.skip_frames(time=2000)
sensor.set_auto_gain(False)
sensor.set_auto_whitebal(False)

uart = pyb.UART(3, 115200)

clock = time.clock()

while True:
    clock.tick()
    img = sensor.snapshot()

    # Find red blobs
    blobs = img.find_blobs(
        [red_threshold],
        pixels_threshold=200,
        area_threshold=200,
        merge=True
    )

    if blobs:
        # Find largest blob
        largest = max(blobs, key=lambda b: b.pixels())

        # Draw crosshair
        img.draw_rectangle(largest.rect(), color=(255, 0, 0))
        img.draw_cross(largest.cx(), largest.cy(), color=(255, 0, 0))

        # Send centroid to Jetson
        cx = largest.cx()
        cy = largest.cy()
        area = largest.pixels()

        uart.write(f"BLOB:{cx},{cy},{area}\n")

        print(f"Blob at ({cx}, {cy}), area={area}")

    fps = clock.fps()
    img.draw_string(5, 5, f"FPS: {fps:.1f}", color=(255, 255, 255))

"""
OpenMV RT1062 - Line Following
Detects line and calculates steering angle
"""

import sensor
import image
import time
import pyb
import math

# Initialize
sensor.reset()
sensor.set_pixformat(sensor.GRAYSCALE)
sensor.set_framesize(sensor.QQVGA)  # 160x120 for speed
sensor.skip_frames(time=2000)

uart = pyb.UART(3, 115200)

# Region of interest (ROI)
ROI = (0, 100, 160, 20)  # Bottom 20 rows

clock = time.clock()

while True:
    clock.tick()
    img = sensor.snapshot()

    # Find line
    line = img.get_regression(
        [(100, 100)],  # Black threshold
        roi=ROI,
        robust=True
    )

    if line:
        # Draw line
        img.draw_line(line.line(), color=127)

        # Calculate steering angle
        # line.theta() returns angle in degrees (0-180)
        # 90° = straight ahead
        angle = line.theta()

        # Convert to steering command (-1.0 to 1.0)
        # Negative = turn left, Positive = turn right
        steering = (angle - 90) / 90.0

        # Send to Jetson
        uart.write(f"LINE:{steering:.3f}\n")

        print(f"Line angle: {angle:.1f}°, Steering: {steering:.3f}")
    else:
        # No line detected
        uart.write("LINE:LOST\n")

    fps = clock.fps()
    img.draw_string(5, 5, f"FPS: {fps:.1f}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
ROS2 node for OpenMV RT1062 communication
"""

import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from geometry_msgs.msg import Point
from std_msgs.msg import String
import serial

class OpenMVBridgeNode(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('openmv_bridge_node')

        # Parameters
        self.declare_parameter('serial_port', '/dev/ttyACM1')
        self.declare_parameter('baud_rate', 115200)

        port = self.get_parameter('serial_port').value
        baud = self.get_parameter('baud_rate').value

        # Serial connection
        self.serial = serial.Serial(port, baud, timeout=0.1)

        # Publishers
        self.qr_pub = self.create_publisher(String, '/openmv/qr_code', 10)
        self.blob_pub = self.create_publisher(Point, '/openmv/blob_centroid', 10)
        self.line_pub = self.create_publisher(String, '/openmv/line_steering', 10)

        # Timer for reading serial
        self.create_timer(0.01, self.read_serial)  # 100 Hz

        self.get_logger().info('OpenMV bridge node started')

    def read_serial(self):
        """Read and process data from OpenMV"""
        if self.serial.in_waiting:
            try:
                line = self.serial.readline().decode('utf-8').strip()
                self.process_data(line)
            except Exception as e:
                self.get_logger().error(f'Serial error: {e}')

    def process_data(self, line):
        """Process data from OpenMV"""
        parts = line.split(':')

        if len(parts) == 2:
            msg_type, data = parts

            if msg_type == 'QR':
                # QR code detected
                msg = String()
                msg.data = data
                self.qr_pub.publish(msg)
                self.get_logger().info(f'QR Code: {data}')

            elif msg_type == 'BLOB':
                # Blob centroid: cx,cy,area
                coords = data.split(',')
                if len(coords) == 3:
                    msg = Point()
                    msg.x = float(coords[0])
                    msg.y = float(coords[1])
                    msg.z = float(coords[2])  # area
                    self.blob_pub.publish(msg)

            elif msg_type == 'LINE':
                # Line steering angle
                msg = String()
                msg.data = data
                self.line_pub.publish(msg)

def main(args=None):
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = OpenMVBridgeNode()

    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        node.serial.close()
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Power monitoring node - Publishes battery and power consumption data
"""

import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from sensor_msgs.msg import BatteryState
from std_msgs.msg import Float32
import smbus2
import time

# INA260 I2C address
INA260_ADDR = 0x40

# Register addresses
REG_VOLTAGE = 0x02
REG_CURRENT = 0x01
REG_POWER = 0x03

class PowerMonitorNode(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('power_monitor_node')

        # I2C bus
        self.bus = smbus2.SMBus(1)

        # Publishers
        self.battery_pub = self.create_publisher(
            BatteryState,
            '/battery/state',
            10
        )

        self.power_pub = self.create_publisher(
            Float32,
            '/battery/power',
            10
        )

        # Battery parameters
        self.declare_parameter('capacity_ah', 5.0)
        self.declare_parameter('voltage_min', 9.0)
        self.declare_parameter('voltage_max', 12.6)
        self.declare_parameter('voltage_nominal', 11.1)

        # State tracking
        self.total_charge = 0.0  # Coulomb counting
        self.last_time = time.time()

        # Timer for periodic monitoring
        self.create_timer(0.1, self.monitor_callback)  # 10 Hz

        self.get_logger().info('Power monitor node started')

    def read_ina260(self, register):
        """Read 16-bit value from INA260"""
        data = self.bus.read_i2c_block_data(INA260_ADDR, register, 2)
        value = (data[0] << 8) | data[1]

        # Convert to signed if needed
        if value & 0x8000:
            value = -((value ^ 0xFFFF) + 1)

        return value

    def monitor_callback(self):
        """Monitor battery and publish state"""
        try:
            # Read voltage (LSB = 1.25 mV)
            voltage_raw = self.read_ina260(REG_VOLTAGE)
            voltage = voltage_raw * 1.25 / 1000.0  # Convert to Volts

            # Read current (LSB = 1.25 mA)
            current_raw = self.read_ina260(REG_CURRENT)
            current = current_raw * 1.25 / 1000.0  # Convert to Amps

            # Read power (LSB = 10 mW)
            power_raw = self.read_ina260(REG_POWER)
            power = power_raw * 10 / 1000.0  # Convert to Watts

            # Coulomb counting for charge estimation
            current_time = time.time()
            dt = current_time - self.last_time
            self.total_charge += current * dt / 3600.0  # Convert to Ah
            self.last_time = current_time

            # Estimate state of charge (SOC)
            capacity = self.get_parameter('capacity_ah').value
            soc = max(0.0, min(1.0, 1.0 - (self.total_charge / capacity)))

            # Adjust SOC based on voltage (voltage-based estimation)
            v_min = self.get_parameter('voltage_min').value
            v_max = self.get_parameter('voltage_max').value
            voltage_soc = (voltage - v_min) / (v_max - v_min)
            voltage_soc = max(0.0, min(1.0, voltage_soc))

            # Blend coulomb counting and voltage estimation
            soc_blended = 0.7 * soc + 0.3 * voltage_soc

            # Create BatteryState message
            battery_msg = BatteryState()
            battery_msg.header.stamp = self.get_clock().now().to_msg()
            battery_msg.voltage = voltage
            battery_msg.current = -current  # Negative = discharging
            battery_msg.charge = soc_blended * capacity
            battery_msg.capacity = capacity
            battery_msg.design_capacity = capacity
            battery_msg.percentage = soc_blended
            battery_msg.power_supply_status = BatteryState.POWER_SUPPLY_STATUS_DISCHARGING
            battery_msg.power_supply_health = self.get_health_status(voltage)
            battery_msg.power_supply_technology = BatteryState.POWER_SUPPLY_TECHNOLOGY_LIPO
            battery_msg.present = True

            # Publish
            self.battery_pub.publish(battery_msg)

            # Publish power consumption
            power_msg = Float32()
            power_msg.data = power
            self.power_pub.publish(power_msg)

            # Log warnings
            if voltage < v_min + 0.5:
                self.get_logger().warn(
                    f'Low battery: {voltage:.2f}V ({soc_blended*100:.0f}%)'
                )

        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f'Power monitoring error: {e}')

    def get_health_status(self, voltage):
        """Determine battery health based on voltage"""
        v_min = self.get_parameter('voltage_min').value
        v_max = self.get_parameter('voltage_max').value

        if voltage > v_max + 0.5:
            return BatteryState.POWER_SUPPLY_HEALTH_OVERVOLTAGE
        elif voltage < v_min:
            return BatteryState.POWER_SUPPLY_HEALTH_DEAD
        elif voltage < v_min + 1.0:
            return BatteryState.POWER_SUPPLY_HEALTH_COLD  # Repurposed as "low"
        else:
            return BatteryState.POWER_SUPPLY_HEALTH_GOOD

def main(args=None):
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = PowerMonitorNode()

    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Safety monitor - Automatic shutdown on critical conditions
"""

import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from sensor_msgs.msg import BatteryState
from std_msgs.msg import Bool
import subprocess

class SafetyMonitorNode(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('safety_monitor_node')

        # Thresholds
        self.declare_parameter('voltage_critical', 9.0)
        self.declare_parameter('voltage_warning', 9.5)
        self.declare_parameter('temp_warning', 50.0)
        self.declare_parameter('temp_critical', 60.0)

        # Subscribers
        self.create_subscription(
            BatteryState,
            '/battery/state',
            self.battery_callback,
            10
        )

        # Publishers
        self.emergency_stop_pub = self.create_publisher(
            Bool,
            '/emergency_stop',
            10
        )

        # State
        self.warning_count = 0
        self.shutdown_initiated = False

        self.get_logger().info('Safety monitor node started')

    def battery_callback(self, msg):
        """Monitor battery and take action if needed"""
        voltage = msg.voltage
        v_critical = self.get_parameter('voltage_critical').value
        v_warning = self.get_parameter('voltage_warning').value

        # Critical voltage - immediate shutdown
        if voltage < v_critical and not self.shutdown_initiated:
            self.get_logger().error(
                f'CRITICAL: Battery voltage {voltage:.2f}V < {v_critical}V'
            )
            self.initiate_emergency_shutdown()

        # Warning voltage - alert user
        elif voltage < v_warning:
            self.warning_count += 1
            if self.warning_count % 10 == 0:  # Every second at 10Hz
                self.get_logger().warn(
                    f'WARNING: Low battery {voltage:.2f}V'
                )
                # Publish emergency stop signal
                stop_msg = Bool()
                stop_msg.data = True
                self.emergency_stop_pub.publish(stop_msg)

    def initiate_emergency_shutdown(self):
        """Emergency system shutdown"""
        self.shutdown_initiated = True

        self.get_logger().error('Initiating emergency shutdown!')

        # Stop all motors
        stop_msg = Bool()
        stop_msg.data = True
        self.emergency_stop_pub.publish(stop_msg)

        # Wait for motors to stop
        time.sleep(2)

        # Shutdown system
        subprocess.call(['sudo', 'shutdown', '-h', 'now'])

def main(args=None):
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = SafetyMonitorNode()

    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

docs.title: Battery Care
docs.text:
YAML
Storage Guidelines:
  Short-term (<2 weeks):
    - Charge to 50-70%
    - Store at room temperature (20-25°C)
    - Check voltage monthly

  Long-term (>2 weeks):
    - Charge to storage voltage (3.85V/cell = 11.55V)
    - Store in cool, dry place (15-20°C)
    - Check voltage every 2-3 months
    - Recharge if below 11.0V

Operating Guidelines:
  - Never discharge below 3.0V/cell (9.0V total)
  - Avoid continuous high-current discharge (>20A)
  - Let battery cool before recharging
  - Monitor temperature during use
  - Balance charge every 10 cycles

Lifespan:
  Typical: 300-500 cycles
  Factors: Charge/discharge rate, temperature, storage
  Signs of aging: Reduced capacity, longer charge time, swelling
  Replacement: When capacity < 80% or physical damage

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
YAML
Issue: Battery won't charge
  Check:
    - Charger settings (3S LiPo mode)
    - Balance lead connection
    - Fuse continuity
    - Cell voltages (should be similar)
  Solution:
    - Verify charger output voltage
    - Check for internal BMS fault
    - Replace if cells imbalanced (>0.3V difference)

Issue: Rapid discharge
  Check:
    - Power consumption (use power monitor)
    - Short circuits
    - BMS bypass
  Solution:
    - Identify high-current loads
    - Check wiring for shorts
    - Test with known-good battery

Issue: Battery swelling
  Action:
    - STOP using immediately
    - Discharge to 0V in safe location
    - Dispose at proper recycling facility
    - NEVER puncture or disassemble

docs.title: Ultrasonic Sensors (HC-SR04)
docs.text:
Specifications: YAML

Model: HC-SR04 (set of 4-8 sensors)
Range: 2cm - 400cm
Accuracy: ±3mm
Beam Angle: 15°
Frequency: 40 kHz
Measurement Cycle: 60ms minimum

Interface: GPIO (Trigger + Echo pins)
Power: 5V / 15mA
Response Time: <1ms

Wiring (per sensor):

Text Only
HC-SR04 → Jetson Orin Nano
───────────────────────────
VCC     → Pin 2 (5V)
TRIG    → GPIO pin (e.g., Pin 11)
ECHO    → GPIO pin (e.g., Pin 13) + voltage divider
GND     → Pin 6 (GND)

⚠️ IMPORTANT: Echo pin outputs 5V, but Jetson GPIO is 3.3V tolerant
Use voltage divider: 1kΩ and 2kΩ resistors

Driver Code:

Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from sensor_msgs.msg import Range
import RPi.GPIO as GPIO
import time

class UltrasonicNode(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('ultrasonic_node')

        self.declare_parameter('trigger_pin', 11)
        self.declare_parameter('echo_pin', 13)
        self.declare_parameter('frame_id', 'ultrasonic_link')
        self.declare_parameter('rate', 10.0)  # Hz

        self.trigger = self.get_parameter('trigger_pin').value
        self.echo = self.get_parameter('echo_pin').value
        self.frame_id = self.get_parameter('frame_id').value

        GPIO.setmode(GPIO.BOARD)
        GPIO.setup(self.trigger, GPIO.OUT)
        GPIO.setup(self.echo, GPIO.IN)
        GPIO.output(self.trigger, False)

        self.publisher = self.create_publisher(Range, 'ultrasonic/range', 10)

        rate = self.get_parameter('rate').value
        self.timer = self.create_timer(1.0 / rate, self.measure_distance)

        self.get_logger().info('Ultrasonic sensor node started')

    def measure_distance(self):
        # Send trigger pulse
        GPIO.output(self.trigger, True)
        time.sleep(0.00001)  # 10μs pulse
        GPIO.output(self.trigger, False)

        # Wait for echo
        timeout = time.time() + 0.1  # 100ms timeout
        while GPIO.input(self.echo) == 0:
            pulse_start = time.time()
            if pulse_start > timeout:
                self.get_logger().warn('Ultrasonic timeout (no echo start)')
                return

        while GPIO.input(self.echo) == 1:
            pulse_end = time.time()
            if pulse_end > timeout:
                self.get_logger().warn('Ultrasonic timeout (no echo end)')
                return

        # Calculate distance
        pulse_duration = pulse_end - pulse_start
        distance = pulse_duration * 17150  # Speed of sound / 2
        distance = distance / 100  # Convert to meters

        # Publish Range message
        msg = Range()
        msg.header.stamp = self.get_clock().now().to_msg()
        msg.header.frame_id = self.frame_id
        msg.radiation_type = Range.ULTRASOUND
        msg.field_of_view = 0.26  # 15° in radians
        msg.min_range = 0.02
        msg.max_range = 4.0
        msg.range = distance

        self.publisher.publish(msg)

def main(args=None):
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = UltrasonicNode()
    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        GPIO.cleanup()
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

docs.title: Magnetometer / Compass (HMC5883L)
docs.text:
Specifications: YAML

Model: Honeywell HMC5883L
Range: ±1.3 to ±8.1 Gauss (selectable)
Resolution: 1° to 2°
Accuracy: 1-2° heading accuracy
Sample Rate: Up to 160 Hz

Interface: I2C
I2C Address: 0x1E
Power: 3.3V / 100μA (active)

Calibration (Critical for Accuracy):

Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Magnetometer calibration script
import smbus2
import time
import numpy as np

bus = smbus2.SMBus(1)
MAG_ADDR = 0x1E

# Initialize magnetometer
bus.write_byte_data(MAG_ADDR, 0x00, 0x70)  # 8-average, 15 Hz
bus.write_byte_data(MAG_ADDR, 0x01, 0xA0)  # Gain = 5
bus.write_byte_data(MAG_ADDR, 0x02, 0x00)  # Continuous mode

print("Rotate magnetometer in all directions for 30 seconds...")
print("Make figure-8 patterns in 3D space")

samples = []
start_time = time.time()

while time.time() - start_time < 30:
    # Read raw data
    data = bus.read_i2c_block_data(MAG_ADDR, 0x03, 6)
    x = np.int16((data[0] << 8) | data[1])
    y = np.int16((data[4] << 8) | data[5])
    z = np.int16((data[2] << 8) | data[3])

    samples.append([x, y, z])
    time.sleep(0.01)

samples = np.array(samples)

# Calculate hard-iron offset (center of sphere)
offset = np.mean(samples, axis=0)

# Calculate soft-iron scale (ellipsoid to sphere)
centered = samples - offset
scale = np.std(centered, axis=0)
scale = scale / np.min(scale)

print(f"\nCalibration Results:")
print(f"Offset: {offset}")
print(f"Scale: {scale}")
print(f"\nAdd to imu_params.yaml:")
print(f"mag_offset: [{offset[0]:.1f}, {offset[1]:.1f}, {offset[2]:.1f}]")
print(f"mag_scale: [{scale[0]:.3f}, {scale[1]:.3f}, {scale[2]:.3f}]")

docs.title: Multi-Sensor Kalman Filter
docs.text:
Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from sensor_msgs.msg import Imu, NavSatFix
from geometry_msgs.msg import PoseWithCovarianceStamped
from nav_msgs.msg import Odometry
import numpy as np
from filterpy.kalman import ExtendedKalmanFilter

class SensorFusionNode(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('sensor_fusion_node')

        # Initialize EKF
        self.ekf = ExtendedKalmanFilter(dim_x=9, dim_z=6)
        # State: [x, y, z, vx, vy, vz, roll, pitch, yaw]

        # Subscribers
        self.create_subscription(Imu, '/imu/data', self.imu_callback, 10)
        self.create_subscription(NavSatFix, '/gps/fix', self.gps_callback, 10)
        self.create_subscription(Odometry, '/odom', self.odom_callback, 10)

        # Publisher
        self.pose_pub = self.create_publisher(
            PoseWithCovarianceStamped,
            '/fused_pose',
            10
        )

        # Timer for prediction step
        self.create_timer(0.01, self.prediction_step)  # 100 Hz

        self.get_logger().info('Sensor fusion node started')

    def prediction_step(self):
        # EKF prediction using motion model
        dt = 0.01
        self.ekf.predict(dt=dt)

        # Publish fused pose
        msg = PoseWithCovarianceStamped()
        msg.header.stamp = self.get_clock().now().to_msg()
        msg.header.frame_id = 'map'

        # Extract state estimate
        x, y, z = self.ekf.x[0:3]
        roll, pitch, yaw = self.ekf.x[6:9]

        # Fill pose
        msg.pose.pose.position.x = x
        msg.pose.pose.position.y = y
        msg.pose.pose.position.z = z

        # Convert RPY to quaternion
        from tf_transformations import quaternion_from_euler
        q = quaternion_from_euler(roll, pitch, yaw)
        msg.pose.pose.orientation.x = q[0]
        msg.pose.pose.orientation.y = q[1]
        msg.pose.pose.orientation.z = q[2]
        msg.pose.pose.orientation.w = q[3]

        # Fill covariance
        P = self.ekf.P
        msg.pose.covariance[0] = P[0, 0]   # x
        msg.pose.covariance[7] = P[1, 1]   # y
        msg.pose.covariance[14] = P[2, 2]  # z
        msg.pose.covariance[21] = P[6, 6]  # roll
        msg.pose.covariance[28] = P[7, 7]  # pitch
        msg.pose.covariance[35] = P[8, 8]  # yaw

        self.pose_pub.publish(msg)

    def imu_callback(self, msg):
        # EKF update with IMU data (acceleration & angular velocity)
        # Measurement: [ax, ay, az, wx, wy, wz]
        z = np.array([
            msg.linear_acceleration.x,
            msg.linear_acceleration.y,
            msg.linear_acceleration.z,
            msg.angular_velocity.x,
            msg.angular_velocity.y,
            msg.angular_velocity.z
        ])

        self.ekf.update(z, self.imu_measurement_model)

    def gps_callback(self, msg):
        # EKF update with GPS position
        # Convert lat/lon to local x/y (simplified)
        x, y = self.latlon_to_xy(msg.latitude, msg.longitude)
        z = msg.altitude

        # Measurement: [x, y, z]
        measurement = np.array([x, y, z])
        self.ekf.update(measurement, self.gps_measurement_model)

    def odom_callback(self, msg):
        # EKF update with wheel odometry
        # Measurement: [vx, vy, vz]
        z = np.array([
            msg.twist.twist.linear.x,
            msg.twist.twist.linear.y,
            msg.twist.twist.linear.z
        ])

        self.ekf.update(z, self.odom_measurement_model)

    def imu_measurement_model(self, x):
        # Measurement model for IMU
        # Returns expected measurement given state
        pass

    def gps_measurement_model(self, x):
        # Measurement model for GPS
        pass

    def odom_measurement_model(self, x):
        # Measurement model for odometry
        pass

    def latlon_to_xy(self, lat, lon):
        # Convert GPS lat/lon to local XY
        # (Simplified; use proper projection in production)
        return lat * 111000, lon * 111000 * np.cos(np.radians(lat))

docs.title: Control System
docs.text: Motor control, servo management, and actuation system.

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text:
The Control System module provides real-time motor control, servo management, and actuation for the Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL platform.

Key Features: - Dual DC motor PWM control (0-100%) - Servo control with pulse width modulation (0.5-2.5ms) - PID velocity tracking (linear and angular) - Odometry feedback integration - Emergency stop safety mechanism - Motor current monitoring - Acceleration/deceleration profiles - Multi-motor coordination

docs.title: Motor Control Parameters
docs.text:
YAML
# config/motor_config.yaml
motor_controller:
  ros__parameters:
    # Motor specifications
    left_motor_pin: 17
    right_motor_pin: 27
    left_pwm_pin: 12
    right_pwm_pin: 13

    # Motor characteristics
    max_speed: 1.0  # m/s
    motor_constants:
      kp: 0.5
      ki: 0.1
      kd: 0.05
      max_integral: 1.0

    # Speed control
    acceleration_limit: 2.0  # m/s²
    deceleration_limit: 3.0  # m/s²

    # Feedback
    enable_odometry_feedback: true
    odometry_topic: "/odom"

    # Safety
    max_current: 2.0  # Amperes
    emergency_stop_timeout: 0.5  # seconds

    # PWM
    pwm_frequency: 1000  # Hz
    pwm_range: [0, 255]

docs.title: Servo Control Parameters
docs.text:
YAML
# config/servo_config.yaml
servo_controller:
  ros__parameters:
    # Servo channels (I2C based)
    i2c_bus: 1
    i2c_address: 0x40

    # Servo specifications
    num_servos: 4
    servos:
      - id: 0
        name: "pan"
        min_angle: -90
        max_angle: 90
        min_pulse: 0.5   # milliseconds
        max_pulse: 2.5
        center_pulse: 1.5

      - id: 1
        name: "tilt"
        min_angle: -45
        max_angle: 45
        min_pulse: 0.5
        max_pulse: 2.5
        center_pulse: 1.5

      - id: 2
        name: "gripper"
        min_angle: 0
        max_angle: 180
        min_pulse: 0.5
        max_pulse: 2.5
        center_pulse: 1.5

      - id: 3
        name: "lift"
        min_angle: 0
        max_angle: 90
        min_pulse: 0.5
        max_pulse: 2.5
        center_pulse: 1.5

    # Frequency
    pwm_frequency: 50  # Hz (standard servo frequency)

    # Speed profile
    speed_limit: 60  # degrees per second

docs.text:
Check: - Power supply connected and sufficient voltage - PWM pins configured correctly - Motor driver IC enabled - Safety limits not triggered

docs.title: Unsmooth Motion
docs.text: Solutions: - Tune PID gains (start with lower kp, increase gradually) - Check encoder connections - Verify motor power supply stability - Reduce acceleration limits temporarily

docs.title: Servo Jitter
docs.text: Solutions: - Verify servo signal line shielding - Check PWM frequency (50Hz for servos) - Increase servo power supply capacity - Reduce number of servos updated simultaneously

docs.title: Microcontroller Integration
docs.text: ARM Cortex-M7 microcontroller for real-time I/O and low-level control.

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text:
The Microcontroller Integration module provides real-time low-level control and I/O interfacing through an ARM Cortex-M7 MCU, enabling precise sensor reading and actuator control.

Key Features: - ARM Cortex-M7 (600 MHz) processor - Real-time operating system (RTOS) support - Analog/digital I/O (16 ADC channels, 12 DAC channels) - PWM generation (6+ independent PWM outputs) - CAN bus interface (2x) - I2C/SPI communication - Interrupt-driven real-time control - Wireless bootloader support - 256KB RAM, 512KB Flash

docs.text:

# config/mcu_config.yaml
mcu_interface:
  ros__parameters:
    # Serial communication
    port: "/dev/ttyUSB0"
    baudrate: 921600
    timeout: 1.0  # seconds

    # Protocol
    protocol_version: 1
    checksum_type: "crc32"

    # Update rates
    adc_update_rate: 100  # Hz
    pwm_update_rate: 500  # Hz
    can_update_rate: 100  # Hz
    gpio_update_rate: 10  # Hz

    # Watchdog
    enable_watchdog: true
    watchdog_timeout: 2  # seconds

    # Motor configuration
    motor_channels: [0, 1]  # PWM channels for motors
    motor_frequency: 1000  # Hz
    motor_resolution: 255  # 8-bit

    # Servo configuration
    servo_channels: [2, 3, 4, 5]  # PWM channels for servos
    servo_frequency: 50  # Hz (standard servo)

    # ADC channels
    adc_channels:
      battery_voltage: 0
      current_sense: 1
      temperature: 2
      light_sensor: 3

    # Output
    publish_diagnostics: true
    diagnostics_frequency: 1  # Hz

docs.title: Real-time Task Scheduling
docs.text:
YAML
FreeRTOS Tasks:

Task 1: ADC Reading
  Priority: High (3)
  Frequency: 100 Hz (10ms period)
  Duration: <2ms
  Function: Read all ADC channels, publish data

Task 2: PWM Control
  Priority: High (3)
  Frequency: 500 Hz (2ms period)
  Duration: <1ms
  Function: Update PWM duty cycles

Task 3: CAN Communication
  Priority: Medium (2)
  Frequency: 100 Hz (10ms period)
  Duration: <3ms
  Function: Send/receive CAN messages

Task 4: UART Communication
  Priority: Medium (2)
  Frequency: Event-driven
  Duration: <5ms
  Function: Serialize/deserialize messages to Jetson

Task 5: Watchdog
  Priority: Low (1)
  Frequency: 10 Hz (100ms period)
  Duration: <1ms
  Function: Monitor system health, kick watchdog

Idle Task:
  Sleep state, lowest power

docs.title: ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter)
docs.text:
YAML
Specifications:
  Resolution: 12-bit (0-4095 digital units)
  Channels: 16 multiplexed
  Sampling: Up to 100 kHz per channel
  Reference: Internal 3.3V
  Input Range: 0 - 3.3V
  Accuracy: ±1 LSB typical (±0.8mV)

Connected Sensors:
  Channel 0: Battery Voltage (via divider)
    Range: 0-12V (attenuated to 0-3.3V)
    Scaling: ADC_value * 12 / 4095

  Channel 1: Current Sense (via INA219)
    Range: ±3.2A
    Scaling: Via I2C interface

  Channel 2: Temperature (NTC thermistor)
    Range: -40 to +85°C
    Scaling: Steinhart-Hart equation

  Channel 3: Light Sensor (LDR)
    Range: 0-100kΩ
    Scaling: Logarithmic response

docs.title: PWM (Pulse Width Modulation)
docs.text:
YAML
Specifications:
  Channels: 6 independent outputs
  Frequency: Programmable 1 Hz - 1 MHz
  Resolution: 8-16 bit (software programmable)
  Duty Cycle: 0-100%
  Output Voltage: 3.3V (logic level)
  Output Current: 25mA per pin

Motor Control:
  Channel 0: Left Motor (1kHz, 8-bit)
  Channel 1: Right Motor (1kHz, 8-bit)

  Servo Control:
  Channel 2: Pan Servo (50Hz, 16-bit)
    Pulse Width: 1000μs (0°) - 2000μs (180°)

  Channel 3: Tilt Servo (50Hz, 16-bit)
  Channel 4: Gripper Servo (50Hz, 16-bit)
  Channel 5: Lift Servo (50Hz, 16-bit)

docs.title: CAN Bus Interface
docs.text:
YAML
Specifications:
  Protocol: CAN 2.0B
  Bitrate: 250 kbps, 500 kbps, 1 Mbps
  Interfaces: 2x CAN ports
  Max Devices: 127 nodes per bus

CAN Node ID Assignment:
  0x100: Motor Controller 1
  0x101: Motor Controller 2
  0x110: IMU Sensor
  0x111: Temperature Sensor
  0x120: Battery Monitor
  0x130: Diagnostics

Message Format:
  Standard ID (11-bit)
  Data Length: 0-8 bytes
  Priority: Via arbitration ID

Example Message:
  ID: 0x120 (Battery Monitor)
  Data: [V_high, V_low, I_high, I_low, T, ...]
  Frequency: 10 Hz

docs.title: Serial Communication with Jetson
docs.text:
YAML
Protocol: Custom binary protocol

Frame Format:
  Header: 0xAA 0xBB (2 bytes)
  Length: uint16 (2 bytes)
  Command: uint8 (1 byte)
  Payload: variable length
  Checksum: CRC32 (4 bytes)
  Footer: 0xCC 0xDD (2 bytes)

Baudrate: 921600 (High-speed)
Timeout: 100ms (watchdog timeout)
Max Retries: 3

Commands:
  0x01: Read ADC
  0x02: Set PWM
  0x03: GPIO Control
  0x04: CAN Send
  0x05: System Status
  0x06: Calibration
  ...

docs.title: System Monitoring
docs.text: Real-time system diagnostics, logging, and performance monitoring.

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text:
The Monitoring module provides comprehensive system diagnostics, real-time performance tracking, and fault detection for the Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL platform.

Key Features: - Real-time system metrics (CPU, memory, disk) - Temperature monitoring and thermal management - Battery health tracking - Network diagnostics - ROS2 node health monitoring - Performance profiling - Automated fault detection - Historical data logging

docs.title: Monitoring Parameters
docs.text:
YAML
# config/monitoring_config.yaml
monitoring_node:
  ros__parameters:
    # Update frequency
    system_update_rate: 5  # Hz
    battery_update_rate: 1  # Hz
    thermal_update_rate: 10  # Hz
    network_update_rate: 2  # Hz

    # Sensor configuration
    enable_cpu_monitoring: true
    enable_memory_monitoring: true
    enable_disk_monitoring: true
    enable_temperature_monitoring: true
    enable_battery_monitoring: true
    enable_network_monitoring: true
    enable_ros2_monitoring: true

    # Thermal sensors
    thermal_zone: "/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0"
    thermal_sensors:
      - name: "cpu"
        path: "/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon0/temp1_input"
      - name: "gpu"
        path: "/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon0/temp2_input"
      - name: "ambient"
        path: "/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon0/temp3_input"

    # Battery configuration
    battery_path: "/sys/class/power_supply/battery"
    battery_type: "Li-Po"  # Li-Po, Li-Ion, NiMH
    battery_cells: 2
    battery_nominal_voltage: 7.4  # Volts
    battery_capacity: 5000  # mAh

    # Network interfaces
    network_interfaces:
      - "eth0"
      - "wlan0"

    # Performance profiling
    enable_profiling: true
    profile_update_rate: 1  # Hz

    # Logging
    enable_logging: true
    log_directory: "/var/log/jetbot"
    log_max_size: 100  # MB
    log_retention_days: 30

    # Publishing
    diagnostics_topic: "/diagnostics"
    metrics_topic: "/monitoring/metrics"

docs.title: CPU Performance
docs.text:
YAML
Metrics:
  - Usage percentage: 0-100%
  - Per-core load: Individual core activity
  - Average load (1/5/15 min): System load average
  - Context switches: Per second
  - Interrupts: Hardware + software

Calculation:
  CPU Usage = (total_time - idle_time) / total_time * 100
  Load Average = (sum of running tasks) / cpu_count

docs.title: Memory Usage
docs.text:
YAML
Metrics:
  - Total memory: Fixed at 8GB
  - Used memory: Currently allocated
  - Available memory: Free + reclaimable
  - Buffers: Disk cache
  - Swap usage: Virtual memory

Breakdown:
  - System: Linux kernel, drivers
  - ROS2: Node processes, middleware
  - Applications: User programs
  - Cache: Recoverable memory

docs.title: Disk I/O
docs.text:
YAML
Metrics:
  - Read/write throughput: MB/s
  - IOPS: Operations per second
  - Queue depth: Pending requests
  - Latency: Operation time

Thresholds:
  - Warning: > 500 MB/s sustained
  - Critical: > 800 MB/s sustained
  - Latency warning: > 50ms average

docs.title: Network Statistics
docs.text:
YAML
Per-Interface:
  - RX bytes: Data received
  - TX bytes: Data transmitted
  - RX packets: Packet count
  - TX packets: Packet count
  - Errors: Transmission errors
  - Dropped: Lost packets

Calculations:
  - Bandwidth: (bytes * 8) / time
  - Packet loss rate: dropped / total * 100
  - Error rate: errors / total * 100

docs.title: Battery State Estimation
Battery Health Analysis
docs.text:
YAML
Health Indicators:
  - Internal resistance: Measured from voltage drop under load
  - Cycle count: Number of charge/discharge cycles
  - Capacity fade: Actual vs nominal capacity
  - Age: Days in service
  - Temperature history: Thermal stress

Estimation:
  Health% = (Cycles / Max_Cycles) * 100
         + (Temp_Peak / Max_Temp) * 100
         - (Age_Days / Life_Days) * 50

docs.title: Discharge Profile
docs.text:
YAML
Typical Li-Po 2S (7.4V nominal):

Discharge Curve:
  100%: 8.40V (fully charged)
   75%: 7.80V
   50%: 7.30V
   25%: 6.80V
    0%: 6.00V (fully discharged)

Safe Operating Range:
  Min Voltage: 6.0V (stop use)
  Recommended Min: 6.5V (extend life)
  Max Voltage: 8.4V (fully charged)
  Continuous Current: 10A max

docs.title: Temperature Sensors
docs.text:
YAML
Jetson Orin Nano Thermal Zones:

CPU Package:
  - Path: /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0
  - Normal: 40-60°C
  - Warning: 70°C
  - Throttle: 80°C
  - Shutdown: 95°C

GPU:
  - Normal: 35-60°C
  - Same thresholds as CPU

Memory/SoC:
  - Normal: 30-50°C
  - Warning: 70°C

Ambient:
  - Typical: 20-35°C
  - Consideration: ΔT = (Die - Ambient)

docs.title: Cooling Strategies
docs.text:
YAML
Strategy 1: Passive (No Fan)
  - Heatsink only
  - Air circulation
  - Performance: Limited at high load
  - Power: 0W (none needed)

Strategy 2: Active (Fan)
  - Variable speed fan
  - Thermostat control
  - Temperature setpoint: 65°C
  - Fan speed: PWM-controlled
  - Power: ~1W

Strategy 3: Throttling
  - Reduce CPU frequency
  - Reduce GPU frequency
  - Maintain thermal limit
  - Performance: Reduced by 20-40%

Strategy 4: Shutdown (Safety)
  - Graceful shutdown if > 95°C
  - Prevents hardware damage
  - Alert user
  - Automatic recovery when cooled

docs.title: Network Bridge
docs.text: Wireless communication, remote control, and distributed computing.

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text:
The Network Bridge module enables wireless communication, remote teleoperation, and distributed computing for the Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL platform.

Key Features: - 5GHz WiFi connectivity (802.11ac) - LoRa long-range communication (10km range) - 4G/LTE cellular backup (optional) - ROS2 bridge for remote nodes - Video streaming (H.264, H.265) - Command and telemetry UDP/TCP - Multi-robot mesh networking - Network load balancing

docs.title: Network Configuration
docs.text:
YAML
# config/network_config.yaml
network_bridge:
  ros__parameters:
    # Primary network
    primary_network: "wifi"  # wifi, lora, cellular

    # WiFi configuration
    wifi:
      enabled: true
      ssid: "jetbot-network"
      password: "secure_password"
      frequency: 5000  # 5GHz
      channel: 149
      tx_power: 30  # dBm
      bandwidth: 80  # MHz

    # LoRa configuration
    lora:
      enabled: true
      frequency: 915.0  # MHz (US ISM band)
      bandwidth: 125  # kHz
      spreading_factor: 7
      coding_rate: 4/5
      tx_power: 20  # dBm
      range_estimate: 10000  # meters

    # Cellular (optional)
    cellular:
      enabled: false
      provider: "verizon"
      apn: "verizon.com"

    # ROS2 bridge
    ros2_bridge:
      enabled: true
      middleware: "CycloneDDS"
      domain_id: 0
      dds_config: "config/dds_config.xml"

    # Network failover
    failover:
      enabled: true
      fallback_network: "lora"
      timeout: 5  # seconds
      retry_count: 3

    # Monitoring
    monitoring_interval: 1  # seconds
    log_network_stats: true

docs.title: Bitrate Adaptation
docs.text:
YAML
Adaptive Bitrate Scheme:
  Measurement: Packet loss rate, RTT (round trip time)

  Excellent (>95% delivery): 4000 kbps
  Good (90-95% delivery):    2500 kbps
  Fair (80-90% delivery):    1500 kbps
  Poor (<80% delivery):      800 kbps

  Update Frequency: Every 3 seconds
  Hysteresis: ±10% to prevent oscillation

docs.title: Command Packet Format
docs.text:
YAML
UDP Command Packet:
  Header: 0xDEADBEEF (4 bytes)
  Sequence: uint16 (2 bytes)
  Command Type: uint8 (1 byte)

  Data:
    - Linear velocity: float (4 bytes)
    - Angular velocity: float (4 bytes)
    - Aux command: uint32 (4 bytes)

  Checksum: CRC32 (4 bytes)
  Total: 23 bytes

Latency: <20ms typical

docs.title: Telemetry Packet Format
docs.text:
YAML
UDP Telemetry Packet:
  Header: 0xBEEFDEAD (4 bytes)
  Sequence: uint16 (2 bytes)
  Timestamp: uint64 (8 bytes)

  Data:
    - Position: float[3] (12 bytes)
    - Orientation: float[4] quaternion (16 bytes)
    - Velocity: float[3] (12 bytes)
    - Battery: float (4 bytes)
    - Status flags: uint32 (4 bytes)

  Checksum: CRC32 (4 bytes)
  Total: 66 bytes

Rate: 10-30 Hz typical

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text:
YAML
AES-256-GCM Encryption:
  Key Exchange: Diffie-Hellman
  Key Size: 256 bits
  Authentication: 16-byte GCM tag
  Nonce: 12 bytes, random

Applied to:
  - ROS2 messages
  - Video stream metadata
  - Control commands
  - Telemetry packets

docs.title: WiFi Connection Drops
docs.text:
Check: - Signal strength: iwconfig wlan0 - Channel interference: Use WiFi analyzer app - Thermal interference: Check temperature

Solutions: - Reduce TX power to 20dBm - Switch to less congested channel - Enable 5GHz (less interference)

docs.title: High Video Latency
docs.text:
Check: - Network ping: ping -c 10 gateway.local - Packet loss: iperf3 -c server -u -b 2M

Solutions: - Reduce video resolution - Enable low-latency mode (shorter buffers) - Increase keyframe interval

docs.title: LoRa Not Connecting

docs.title: Temperature Measurement
docs.text:
YAML
Thermal Radiation:
  Planck's Law: L(λ,T) = (2hc²/λ⁵) / [exp(hc/λkT) - 1]

  Stefan-Boltzmann: P = εσAT⁴
    ε = Emissivity (0.95 for most objects)
    σ = Stefan-Boltzmann constant
    A = Surface area
    T = Absolute temperature (K)

  Radiometric Accuracy:
    - Typical: ±2°C over -40 to +80°C range
    - After calibration: ±1°C possible
    - Depends on emissivity accuracy

docs.title: Weighted Blending
Laplacian Pyramid Fusion
docs.text:
YAML
Process:
  1. Create Laplacian pyramids for both images
  2. At each scale: Select regions from higher-contrast image
  3. Reconstruct from fused pyramids

Advantages:
  - Preserves detail from both images
  - Natural-looking fusion
  - Good for object detection

Disadvantages:
  - Higher computational cost
  - Requires careful weight selection

docs.title: Guided Filter Fusion
docs.text:

Process:
  1. Use RGB as guidance image
  2. Filter thermal data through RGB structure
  3. Enhance edges from thermal where RGB is uncertain

Advantages:
  - Respects object boundaries
  - Good edge preservation
  - Efficient computation

Causes: - Lens misalignment - Dirt on lens - Temperature out of range

docs.title: Fusion Registration Error

Causes: - RGB and thermal sensors not aligned - Different image resolutions

Causes: - Thermal resolution too low - Object temperature too close to background - Attenuation by rain/fog

docs.title: Detector Interface
YOLOv8 Example
🐍 Python API
docs.text:
Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from sensor_msgs.msg import Image
from vision_msgs.msg import Detection2DArray
from cv_bridge import CvBridge

class DetectionSubscriber(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('detection_subscriber')

        self.subscription = self.create_subscription(
            Detection2DArray,
            '/detection/objects',
            self.detection_callback,
            10
        )

        self.image_subscription = self.create_subscription(
            Image,
            '/detection/annotated_image',
            self.image_callback,
            10
        )

        self.bridge = CvBridge()

    def detection_callback(self, msg):
        self.get_logger().info(f'Received {len(msg.detections)} detections')

        for detection in msg.detections:
            for result in detection.results:
                class_id = result.hypothesis.class_id
                score = result.hypothesis.score
                bbox = detection.bbox

                self.get_logger().info(
                    f'  {class_id}: {score:.2f} at '
                    f'[{bbox.center.position.x:.0f}, '
                    f'{bbox.center.position.y:.0f}]'
                )

    def image_callback(self, msg):
        # Convert to OpenCV image
        cv_image = self.bridge.imgmsg_to_cv2(msg, desired_encoding='bgr8')

        # Display or save
        # cv2.imshow('Detections', cv_image)
        # cv2.waitKey(1)

def main():
    rclpy.init()
    node = DetectionSubscriber()

    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass

    node.destroy_node()
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

  13: 2472 MHz (non-overlapping)

Non-overlapping Channels: 1, 6, 11 (recommended)
Typical Bandwidth: 20 MHz per channel
Overlap Penalty: 25 dB adjacent, 5 dB overlapping

Common Interference:
  - Bluetooth: 2.402 - 2.480 GHz
  - Microwaves: 2.45 GHz
  - Cordless phones: 2.4 GHz

docs.title: 5 GHz WiFi Band (UNII)
docs.text:
YAML
Band: 5.15 - 5.85 GHz
Technology: 802.11a/n/ac/ax
Channel Bandwidth: 20/40/80/160 MHz

Bands:
  UNII-1 (5.15-5.25 GHz):
    Channels: 36, 40, 44, 48
    Power Limit: 17 dBm
    Use Case: Indoor/Outdoor

  UNII-2 (5.25-5.35 GHz):
    Channels: 52, 56, 60, 64
    Power Limit: 24 dBm
    Use Case: Outdoor, radar sensing

  UNII-3 (5.65-5.85 GHz):
    Channels: 149, 153, 157, 161, 165
    Power Limit: 30 dBm
    Use Case: Outdoor

Advantages over 2.4 GHz:
  - More channels available
  - Less interference (unlicensed)
  - Higher data rates (20/40/80/160 MHz)
  - Lower latency

Disadvantages:
  - Shorter range (higher frequency = more attenuation)
  - Lower wall penetration
  - Higher power consumption

docs.title: 915 MHz LoRa Band (ISM)
docs.text:
YAML
Band: 902 - 928 MHz (North America)
Band: 863 - 870 MHz (Europe)
Technology: LoRaWAN, LoRa point-to-point
Bandwidth: 125 kHz (standard), 250 kHz, 500 kHz

Channels (US):
  Uplink: 902.3 - 914.9 MHz (64 channels @ 200 kHz spacing)
  Downlink: 923.3 - 927.5 MHz (8 channels @ 600 kHz spacing)

Configuration:
  Spreading Factor: 7-12
  Coding Rate: 4/5, 4/6, 4/7, 4/8
  Bandwidth: 125/250/500 kHz

Lower interference than 2.4 GHz:
  - 15 MHz band is large
  - Fewer devices typically
  - Better long-range performance

docs.title: FFT-based Analysis
docs.text:
YAML
Process:
  1. Apply windowing function (Hann, Hamming)
  2. Compute FFT (Fast Fourier Transform)
  3. Calculate magnitude spectrum
  4. Accumulate multiple spectra (averaging)
  5. Convert to dBm

Advantages:
  - Fast computation
  - Good frequency resolution
  - Well-established technique

Disadvantages:
  - Spectral leakage (side lobes)
  - Picket fence effect
  - Limited dynamic range

docs.title: Welch Method (Averaging)
docs.text:
YAML
Process:
  1. Divide signal into overlapping segments
  2. Apply window to each segment
  3. Compute FFT for each segment
  4. Average the power spectra
  5. Result: Smoother, less noisy spectrum

Parameters:
  - Segment length: 256-1024 samples
  - Overlap: 50%
  - Window: Hann or Hamming

Benefits:
  - Reduced variance in spectrum estimate
  - Better for noise reduction
  - More stable measurements

docs.title: Spectrogram (Time-Frequency)
docs.text:
YAML
Matrix of:
  - Time (x-axis): seconds
  - Frequency (y-axis): MHz/GHz
  - Color intensity: Signal power (dBm)

Use Cases:
  - Transient signal detection

docs.title: Automatic Detection Algorithm
Noise Floor Estimation
Signal Quality Assessment
docs.text:
YAML
WiFi Channel Quality:
  RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator):
    Excellent: -30 to -50 dBm
    Good:      -50 to -60 dBm
    Fair:      -60 to -70 dBm
    Poor:      -70 to -80 dBm
    Very Poor: < -80 dBm

  SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio):
    Excellent: > 40 dB
    Good:      30-40 dB
    Fair:      20-30 dB
    Poor:      10-20 dB
    Very Poor: < 10 dB

  Throughput Estimate (20MHz channel):
    -30 dBm + 40dB SNR: ~150 Mbps (802.11ac)
    -50 dBm + 30dB SNR: ~100 Mbps
    -70 dBm + 20dB SNR: ~50 Mbps
    -80 dBm + 10dB SNR: ~11 Mbps (802.11g)

docs.title: Channel Recommendations
docs.text:
YAML
Algorithm: Select least congested channel

For 2.4GHz:
  1. Measure RSSI on channels 1, 6, 11
  2. Calculate interference (count signals > -70dBm)
  3. Select channel with lowest interference
  4. Example:
     Ch1: 4 interferers → Avoid
     Ch6: 1 interferer  → Recommended
     Ch11: 2 interferers → Moderate

For 5GHz:
  1. Measure all available channels
  2. Prefer UNII-3 (149-165) for best throughput
  3. Check for radar interference (DFS)
  4. Recommend channel with > 30 dB SNR

docs.title: Sensor Fusion
docs.text: Multi-sensor integration and Kalman filtering for robust state estimation.

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text:
The Sensor Fusion module integrates data from multiple sensors (camera, IMU, odometry) using Kalman filtering to provide robust state estimation and localization.

Key Features: - Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) fusion - IMU integration for drift correction - Odometry fusion with pose correction - GPS/GNSS integration (optional) - Compass/magnetometer calibration - Real-time covariance estimation - Sensor health monitoring - Automatic outlier rejection

docs.title: EKF Fusion Parameters
docs.text:
YAML
# config/fusion_params.yaml
ekf_fusion:
  ros__parameters:
    # Filter configuration
    filter_type: "ekf"  # ekf, ukf, particle
    state_dimension: 9  # x, y, yaw, vx, vy, wx, ax, ay, wyaw
    measurement_dimension: 6

    # Process noise (how much we trust model)
    process_noise:
      position: 0.01      # m²
      orientation: 0.001  # rad²
      velocity: 0.05      # (m/s)²
      angular_vel: 0.01   # (rad/s)²

    # Measurement noise (how much we trust sensors)
    measurement_noise:
      odometry_position: 0.05     # m²
      odometry_orientation: 0.01  # rad²
      imu_acceleration: 0.1       # (m/s²)²
      imu_angular_vel: 0.05       # (rad/s)²
      gps_position: 1.0           # m² (if available)

    # Update frequency
    fusion_frequency: 50  # Hz

    # Sensor topics
    odometry_topic: "/odom"
    imu_topic: "/imu/data"
    gps_topic: "/gps/fix"  # optional
    compass_topic: "/compass/heading"  # optional

    # Output
    fused_state_topic: "/fusion/state"
    covariance_topic: "/fusion/covariance"
    tf_frame_id: "map"
    tf_child_frame_id: "base_link"

docs.title: EKF State Vector
docs.text:
YAML
State = [x, y, yaw, vx, vy, wx, ax, ay, wyaw]
         ├─ Position (x, y)
         ├─ Orientation (yaw)
         ├─ Velocity (vx, vy)
         ├─ Angular velocity (wx)
         ├─ Acceleration (ax, ay)
         └─ Angular acceleration (wyaw)

docs.title: Fusion Pipeline
docs.text:
graph TB
    Odom["OdometryInput"]
    IMU["IMUData"]
    GPS["GPSInput"]

    Odom --> Predict["PredictionStep"]
    IMU --> Predict
    GPS --> Predict

    Predict --> Update["UpdateStep"]

    Update --> State["StateEstimate"]
    Update --> Cov["CovarianceMatrix"]

    State --> Output["OutputTransform"]
    Cov --> Output

docs.title: Kalman Filter Equations
docs.text:
Text Only
Prediction:
  x̂⁻ = f(x̂⁺, u, Δt)
  P⁻ = FP⁺Fᵀ + Q

Update:
  K = P⁻Hᵀ(HP⁻Hᵀ + R)⁻¹
  x̂⁺ = x̂⁻ + K(z - Hx̂⁻)
  P⁺ = (I - KH)P⁻

Where:
  F = State transition matrix
  Q = Process noise covariance
  H = Measurement matrix
  R = Measurement noise covariance
  K = Kalman gain

docs.title: Fault Handling
Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF)
docs.text:
YAML
Advantages over EKF:
  - No Jacobian matrix required
  - Better for highly nonlinear systems
  - Same computational complexity
  - Better accuracy for small sample times

Configuration:

docs.title: Multi-hypothesis Tracking
docs.text:

Handles ambiguous situations:

  - Sensor fusion conflicts

Number of hypotheses: 4

  - Covariance indicates uncertainty
  - Hypotheses merge when confident

docs.title: Tuning Process
docs.text:
1. Estimate process noise (Q):
  2. Start with typical sensor errors
  3. Increase if filter lags reality

  4. Decrease if filter is too jittery

  5. Estimate measurement noise (R):

  6. Use manufacturer specifications
  7. Verify empirically

  8. Scale by actual sensor quality

  9. Test configuration:

  10. Static test: Verify no drift
  11. Motion test: Check tracking accuracy
  12. Stress test: Rapid acceleration/rotation

docs.title: Tuning Parameters
docs.text:
YAML
Tuning Workflow:
  1. Set Q = 0.1 × Process model uncertainty
  2. Set R = Sensor manufacturer spec
  3. Test and observe:
     - Filter lag: Increase Q
     - Filter noise: Increase R
  4. Iterate until satisfactory

docs.title: SLAM & Navigation
docs.text: Real-time Simultaneous Localization and Mapping with visual-inertial odometry.

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text:
The SLAM & Navigation module provides visual-inertial simultaneous localization and mapping (VI-SLAM) capabilities optimized for real-time autonomous navigation on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano.

Key Features: - Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) at 30+ FPS - Real-time feature tracking and mapping - Loop closure detection - IMU fusion for drift reduction - Path planning and trajectory optimization - Obstacle avoidance - Particle filter localization - Map persistence and reuse

Symptoms: Pose estimates drift rapidly

Solutions: - Check camera calibration accuracy - Ensure sufficient lighting (avoid backlit scenes) - Verify IMU is properly calibrated - Reduce feature threshold to detect more features - Increase keyframe threshold for slower updates

docs.title: Incorrect Loop Closure
docs.text:

Solutions: - Increase loop closure similarity threshold - Verify camera has visited same location - Check feature descriptor quality - Reduce descriptor distance threshold - Enable loop closure only after sufficient exploration

docs.title: High CPU Usage
docs.text:
Symptoms: Real-time performance degradation

Solutions: - Reduce image resolution - Decrease number of features tracked - Increase keyframe interval - Disable unnecessary output topics - Profile with ros2_tracing

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text:
The Stereo Vision module provides 3D perception capabilities through stereo image pairs, enabling depth estimation, 3D object detection, and 3D scene reconstruction.

docs.title: Stereo Camera Setup
docs.text:
YAML
# config/stereo_params.yaml
stereo_processor:
  ros__parameters:
    # Camera configuration
    left_camera_topic: "/camera_left/image_raw"
    right_camera_topic: "/camera_right/image_raw"
    left_camera_info_topic: "/camera_left/camera_info"
    right_camera_info_topic: "/camera_right/camera_info"

    # Calibration
    calibration_file: "config/stereo_calibration.yaml"
    rectify_images: true

    # Stereo matching algorithm
    matcher_type: "semi_global"  # bm, sgbm, semi_global

    # Block matching parameters
    block_size: 11              # Odd number (5-31)
    num_disparities: 192        # Multiple of 16
    min_disparity: 0
    max_disparity: 192

    # Matching cost
    cost_function: "census"     # sad, ssd, census
    p1: 100                     # Penalty for disparity change
    p2: 400                     # Penalty for larger changes

    # Uniqueness check
    uniqueness_ratio: 15        # percent
    texture_threshold: 10
    speckle_size: 100           # pixels
    speckle_range: 16           # disparity units

    # Sub-pixel refinement
    enable_subpixel: true

    # Processing
    median_filter_size: 3
    bilateral_filter: true

    # Output
    publish_depth: true
    publish_point_cloud: true
    publish_disparity: true
    depth_scale: 1000           # mm per unit

docs.title: Stereo Calibration
docs.text:
YAML
# config/stereo_calibration.yaml
stereo_calibration:
  # Left camera intrinsics
  left_camera_matrix:
    rows: 3
    cols: 3
    data: [
      919.8, 0.0, 640.0,
      0.0, 919.8, 360.0,
      0.0, 0.0, 1.0
    ]

  left_distortion:
    rows: 1
    cols: 5
    data: [0.05, -0.1, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

  left_image_size: [1280, 720]

  # Right camera intrinsics
  right_camera_matrix:
    rows: 3
    cols: 3
    data: [
      919.8, 0.0, 640.0,
      0.0, 919.8, 360.0,
      0.0, 0.0, 1.0
    ]

  right_distortion:
    rows: 1
    cols: 5
    data: [0.05, -0.1, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

  right_image_size: [1280, 720]

  # Stereo extrinsics
  R: # Rotation matrix (left to right)
    rows: 3
    cols: 3
    data: [
      0.9999, -0.0015, 0.0045,
      0.0015, 0.9999, -0.0020,
      -0.0045, 0.0020, 0.9999
    ]

  T: # Translation (left to right) in mm
    rows: 3
    cols: 1
    data: [120.0, 2.0, -1.0]  # Baseline = 120mm

  F: # Fundamental matrix
    rows: 3
    cols: 3
    data: [
      0.0, -1.5e-6, -0.4,
      1.5e-6, 0.0, 0.0,
      0.4, 0.0, 1.0
    ]

  # Rectification (if needed)
  Q: # Disparity to depth matrix
    rows: 4
    cols: 4
    data: [
      1.0, 0.0, 0.0, -640.0,
      0.0, 1.0, 0.0, -360.0,
      0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 919.8,
      0.0, 0.0, 1.0/120.0, 0.0
    ]

docs.title: Stereo Processing Pipeline
docs.text:
graph TB
    A["Left Image"]
    B["Right Image"]

    A --> Rect1["Rectification"]
    B --> Rect1

    Rect1 --> Undist["Undistortion"]

    Undist --> Match["StereoMatching"]

    Match --> Disp["DisparityMap"]

    Disp --> DepthEst["DepthEstimation"]

    DepthEst --> PointCloud["Point CloudGeneration"]

    PointCloud --> Output["3D SceneOutput"]

docs.title: Stereo Matching Algorithm
docs.text:
graph TB
    A["Rectified Images"]

    A --> Feature["FeatureExtraction"]

    Feature --> Cost["Cost VolumeComputation"]

    Cost --> Aggr["CostAggregation"]

    Aggr --> Winner["Winner-Take-AllLabeling"]

    Winner --> LR["Left-RightConsistency"]

    LR --> Refine["Sub-pixelRefinement"]

    Refine --> Disp["Final DisparityMap"]

docs.title: Epipolar Geometry Basics
docs.text:
YAML
Fundamental Equation:
  q' · F · p = 0

  Where:
    p = point in left image
    q = corresponding point in right image
    F = Fundamental matrix (3×3)

Interpretation:
  - For point p in left image
  - Its epipolar line in right image is: l' = F·p
  - Matching point q must lie on this line
  - Reduces search space from 2D to 1D

docs.title: Disparity to Depth Conversion
docs.text:
YAML
Process:
  1. Extract disparity from stereo matching
  2. Convert to depth using camera calibration
  3. Format as depth image or point cloud

Formula:
  depth = (baseline × focal_length) / disparity

  Where:
    baseline = distance between cameras (120mm)
    focal_length = camera focal length (919.8 pixels)
    disparity = left_x - right_x (pixels)

Example:
  If disparity = 60 pixels:
    depth = (120mm × 919.8) / 60 = 1840mm = 1.84m

docs.title: Depth Accuracy
docs.text:
YAML
Depth Resolution:
  Close range (2m):   ±50-100mm
  Mid range (5m):     ±100-200mm
  Far range (10m):    ±200-500mm

  Typical formula:
    depth_error = (baseline² / focal_length) / disparity²

Factors affecting accuracy:
  - Baseline length (wider = better accuracy)
  - Camera resolution
  - Texture richness (more texture = better matching)
  - Lighting conditions
  - Occlusions

docs.title: Point Cloud Generation
Point Cloud Processing
docs.text:
YAML
Operations:
  - Filtering: Remove outliers (radius outlier, statistical)
  - Downsampling: Reduce point density for speed
  - Segmentation: Cluster nearby points into objects
  - Normal estimation: Surface normal calculation
  - Feature detection: Keypoint extraction

Applications:
  - Obstacle detection
  - 3D object recognition
  - Scene reconstruction
  - Navigation planning

docs.title: Real-time Obstacle Detection
Ground Plane Segmentation
docs.text:
YAML
Algorithm: RANSAC (Random Sample Consensus)

Process:
  1. Randomly select 3 points
  2. Estimate plane parameters
  3. Count inliers (points close to plane)
  4. Repeat N iterations
  5. Keep plane with most inliers

Ground Plane Characteristics:
  - Normal vector: Approximately [0, 0, 1]
  - Distance from sensor: Varies with robot height
  - Points below: Obstacles
  - Points above: Free space

docs.title: Poor Depth Quality
docs.text:
Causes: - Uncalibrated cameras - Low texture regions (blank walls) - Insufficient baseline - Incorrect disparity range

Solutions: - Recalibrate stereo cameras - Increase lighting on scene - Use wider baseline if possible - Adjust num_disparities parameter

docs.title: Noisy Disparity Map
docs.text:
Causes: - Reflective surfaces (mirrors, glass) - Occlusions - Poor matching parameters

Solutions: - Enable median filtering - Increase speckle filter parameters - Adjust cost aggregation parameters - Apply bilateral filter

docs.title: Slow Processing
docs.text:
Causes: - High resolution input - Complex matching algorithm - Insufficient GPU acceleration

Solutions: - Reduce image resolution (e.g., 640×480) - Use faster matching (BM instead of SGBM) - Reduce number of disparities - Enable GPU processing if available

docs.title: 📋 Installation Paths
docs.text:
We offer multiple installation methods:

🐳 Docker (Recommended)🔨 Native Installation☸️ Kubernetes

Best for: Quick setup, isolated environment, easy updates

Bash
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL

# Run with Docker Compose
docker-compose up -d

✅ Advantages: - Fastest setup time (~30 minutes) - No dependency conflicts - Easy rollback and updates - Consistent environment

⚠️ Considerations: - Requires ~10GB disk space - Slight performance overhead

Best for: Maximum performance, development work, custom modifications

Bash
# Install ROS2 Humble
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y ros-humble-desktop

# Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
colcon build --symlink-install

✅ Advantages: - Best performance - Full system access - Easier debugging - No containerization overhead

⚠️ Considerations: - Longer setup time (~2 hours) - Potential dependency conflicts - Manual updates required

Best for: Multi-robot fleets, production deployments, scalability

Bash
# Add Helm repository
helm repo add tng-blue https://tng-blue.github.io/charts

# Install with Helm
helm install jetbot-nanoowl tng-blue/jetbot-nanoowl \
  --namespace robotics --create-namespace

✅ Advantages: - Production-ready orchestration - Easy scaling and updates - Built-in monitoring - High availability

⚠️ Considerations: - Complex initial setup - Requires K8s knowledge - Resource overhead

docs.title: ❓ Common Questions
docs.text:
What if I don't have all the hardware?

You can start with minimal hardware (Jetson + one camera) and add sensors gradually. Many features work with reduced sensor sets.

Can I use a different Jetson model?

Yes! The platform supports Jetson Nano, Xavier NX, and AGX Xavier. Performance will vary.

Do I need robotics experience?

Not required! Our tutorials start from basics. However, Linux familiarity is helpful.

What if I get stuck?

Check our Troubleshooting Guide or ask in GitHub Discussions.

docs.title: What is ROS2?
docs.text:
ROS2 (Robot Operating System 2) is a framework for robot software development providing:

  • Nodes: Independent processes that perform specific tasks
  • Topics: Channels for asynchronous data streaming
  • Services: Request/response communication
  • Actions: Long-running tasks with feedback
graph LR
    Camera[Camera Node] -->|Image Topic| Detection[Detection Node]
    Detection -->|Objects Topic| Navigation[Nav Node]
    Navigation -->|Velocity| Control[Motor Controller]

    style Camera fill:#4A90E2
    style Detection fill:#F5A623
    style Navigation fill:#7ED321
    style Control fill:#BD10E0

docs.title: Essential ROS2 Commands
docs.text:
Bash
# List all active nodes
ros2 node list

# List all topics
ros2 topic list

# View topic data
ros2 topic echo /camera/image_raw

# Check topic frequency
ros2 topic hz /camera/image_raw

# View node information
ros2 node info /object_detection

# List all services
ros2 service list

# Call a service
ros2 service call /reset_pose std_srvs/srv/Empty

Command Shortcuts

Use Tab for auto-completion in ROS2 commands!

docs.title: Start Teleop Control
docs.text:
Control your robot with keyboard or joystick:

KeyboardJoystick Bash
# Launch keyboard teleop
ros2 run teleop_twist_keyboard teleop_twist_keyboard

Controls: Text Only

Moving around:
   u    i    o
   j    k    l
   m    ,    .

u/o : rotate left/right while moving forward
j/l : rotate left/right
m/. : rotate left/right while moving backward
k   : stop

q/z : increase/decrease max speeds by 10%
w/x : increase/decrease only linear speed by 10%
e/c : increase/decrease only angular speed by 10%

Bash
# Install joystick support
sudo apt install ros-humble-joy -y

# Launch joy node
ros2 run joy joy_node

# Launch teleop
ros2 launch jetbot_teleop joystick.launch.py

Controls (Xbox/PS4): Text Only

Left Stick : Forward/Backward
Right Stick : Rotate Left/Right
A/X Button : Turbo mode
B/Circle : Emergency stop
