docs.title: Complete Installation Guide
docs.text: Comprehensive installation instructions for Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL on NVIDIA Jetson platforms.

docs.title: Minimum Requirements
docs.text: Component Specification Platform NVIDIA Jetson Nano (4GB) Storage 64GB microSD (Class 10) Power 5V/2A USB-C Memory 4GB RAM OS Ubuntu 20.04 + JetPack 4.6+

docs.title: Recommended Requirements
docs.text:
Component Specification Platform NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super (8GB) Storage 128GB NVMe SSD or microSD (UHS-I) Power 5V/4A USB-C or barrel jack Memory 8GB RAM OS Ubuntu 22.04 + JetPack 5.1.2+

Hardware Compatibility

Also supports: Jetson Xavier NX, Xavier AGX, AGX Orin. Performance scales with hardware capabilities.

docs.title: 🔧 Method 1: Docker Installation (Recommended)
docs.text: Docker provides the fastest and most reliable installation with zero dependency conflicts.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Bash
# Update system
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

# Install Docker (if not present)
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com -o get-docker.sh
sudo sh get-docker.sh

# Add user to docker group
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
newgrp docker

# Install Docker Compose
sudo apt install docker-compose -y

docs.title: Install Isaac ROS Jetbot
docs.text:
Bash
# Clone repository
cd ~
git clone --recursive https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL

# Build and start containers
docker-compose up -d --build

# Verify containers are running
docker-compose ps

docs.title: Container Architecture
docs.text:
The Docker setup includes multiple containers:

graph TB
    subgraph "Docker Containers"
        ROS2[ROS2 Base ContainerHumble Hawksbill]
        ISAAC[Isaac ROS ContainerGPU Acceleration]
        DETECT[Detection ContainerYOLOv8 + TensorRT]
        NAV[Navigation ContainerSLAM + Planning]
        WEB[Web InterfaceDashboard + API]
    end

    ROS2 --> ISAAC
    ISAAC --> DETECT
    ISAAC --> NAV
    ROS2 --> WEB

    style ISAAC fill:#76B900
    style DETECT fill:#FF6B35
    style NAV fill:#004E89

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Edit docker-compose.yml to customize:

YAML
# docker-compose.yml
version: '3.8'

services:
  jetbot-core:
    image: tngblue/jetbot-nanoowl:latest
    runtime: nvidia  # GPU access
    privileged: true
    network_mode: host
    volumes:
      - ./config:/app/config
      - ./models:/app/models
      - /dev:/dev  # Hardware access
    environment:
      - ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
      - DISPLAY=${DISPLAY}
      - NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all
      - NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all

docs.title: 🛠️ Method 2: Native Installation
docs.text: Full native installation for maximum performance and development flexibility.

docs.title: Step 1: Install JetPack
docs.text:
Bash
# For Jetson Orin Nano (JetPack 5.1.2)
# Use NVIDIA SDK Manager from host PC
# Or flash with pre-built image from:
# https://developer.nvidia.com/embedded/jetpack

# Verify installation
cat /etc/nv_tegra_release
# Expected: R35 (release), REVISION: 4.1

docs.title: Step 2: Install ROS2 Humble
docs.text:
Bash
# Set locale
sudo apt update && sudo apt install locales
sudo locale-gen en_US en_US.UTF-8
sudo update-locale LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 LANG=en_US.UTF-8
export LANG=en_US.UTF-8

# Add ROS2 repository
sudo apt install software-properties-common
sudo add-apt-repository universe
sudo apt update && sudo apt install curl -y

sudo curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ros/rosdistro/master/ros.key \
  -o /usr/share/keyrings/ros-archive-keyring.gpg

echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/ros-archive-keyring.gpg] \
  http://packages.ros.org/ros2/ubuntu $(. /etc/os-release && echo $UBUNTU_CODENAME) main" | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ros2.list > /dev/null

# Install ROS2 Humble
sudo apt update
sudo apt install ros-humble-desktop -y

# Install development tools
sudo apt install \
  python3-colcon-common-extensions \
  python3-rosdep \
  python3-vcstool \
  build-essential \
  -y

# Initialize rosdep
sudo rosdep init
rosdep update

docs.title: Step 3: Install Isaac ROS
docs.text:
Bash
# Install Isaac ROS dependencies
sudo apt install \
  ros-humble-isaac-ros-nitros \
  ros-humble-isaac-ros-common \
  ros-humble-isaac-ros-dnn-inference \
  -y

# Install CUDA dependencies
sudo apt install \
  cuda-toolkit-11-8 \
  nvidia-tensorrt \
  python3-libnvinfer \
  python3-libnvinfer-dev \
  -y

docs.title: Step 4: Build Workspace
docs.text:
Bash
# Create workspace
mkdir -p ~/ros2_ws/src
cd ~/ros2_ws/src

# Clone main repository
git clone --recursive https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git

# Clone additional dependencies
vcs import < Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/dependencies.repos

# Install Python dependencies
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
pip3 install -r requirements.txt

# Install ROS dependencies
cd ~/ros2_ws
rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src -r -y

# Build packages
colcon build --symlink-install --parallel-workers 2 \
  --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release

# This takes 20-30 minutes on Jetson Orin Nano

docs.title: Step 5: Setup Environment
docs.text:
Bash
# Source workspace
source ~/ros2_ws/install/setup.bash

# Add to bashrc
echo "source ~/ros2_ws/install/setup.bash" >> ~/.bashrc
echo "export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0" >> ~/.bashrc

# Setup GPU environment
echo "export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda" >> ~/.bashrc
echo "export PATH=\$CUDA_HOME/bin:\$PATH" >> ~/.bashrc
echo "export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=\$CUDA_HOME/lib64:\$LD_LIBRARY_PATH" >> ~/.bashrc

source ~/.bashrc

docs.title: ☸️ Method 3: Kubernetes Deployment
docs.text: Production-ready deployment with Kubernetes orchestration.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Bash
# Install K3s (lightweight Kubernetes)
curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | sh -

# Verify installation
sudo k3s kubectl get nodes

# Install Helm
curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash

docs.title: Deploy with Helm
docs.text:
Bash
# Add Helm repository
helm repo add tng-blue https://tng-blue.github.io/charts
helm repo update

# Create namespace
kubectl create namespace robotics

# Install Jetbot chart
helm install jetbot-nanoowl tng-blue/jetbot-nanoowl \
  --namespace robotics \
  --set image.tag=latest \
  --set nodeSelector.nvidia\.com/gpu=true \
  --set resources.limits.nvidia\.com/gpu=1

docs.title: Custom Configuration
docs.text:
Create values.yaml:

YAML
# values.yaml
replicaCount: 1

image:
  repository: tngblue/jetbot-nanoowl
  tag: "latest"
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent

resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    memory: 4Gi
  requests:
    memory: 2Gi

nodeSelector:
  nvidia.com/gpu: "true"

config:
  ros:
    domainId: 0
  detection:
    modelPath: /models/yolov8n.engine
    confidenceThreshold: 0.5
  navigation:
    maxSpeed: 0.5
    safetyDistance: 0.5

Install with custom values:

Bash
helm install jetbot-nanoowl tng-blue/jetbot-nanoowl \
  --namespace robotics \
  -f values.yaml

docs.title: Setup Firewall

docs.title: 🔍 Quick Diagnostics
docs.text:
Start with our automated diagnostic tool:

Bash
cd ~/ros2_ws/src/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL

This checks: - ✅ ROS2 environment - ✅ Hardware detection - ✅ GPU acceleration - ✅ Network configuration - ✅ Model files - ✅ Node status

docs.title: Problem: colcon build fails with memory error
docs.text:
Symptoms: Text Only

c++: fatal error: Killed signal terminated program cc1plus

Solutions:

Solution 1: Reduce WorkersSolution 2: Increase SwapSolution 3: Build Sequentially Bash
# Use only 1 parallel worker
colcon build --symlink-install --parallel-workers 1
Bash
# Create 4GB swap file
sudo fallocate -l 4G /swapfile
sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
sudo swapon /swapfile

# Make permanent
echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab

# Verify
free -h
Bash
# Build one package at a time
colcon build --packages-select jetbot_core
colcon build --packages-select jetbot_detection
# ... and so on

docs.title: Problem: CUDA not found during build
docs.text:
Symptoms: Text Only

CMake Error: Could not find CUDA
nvcc: command not found

Solution: Bash

# Check CUDA installation
ls /usr/local/cuda

# Add to PATH
echo 'export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda' >> ~/.bashrc
echo 'export PATH=$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH' >> ~/.bashrc
echo 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH' >> ~/.bashrc

source ~/.bashrc

# Verify
nvcc --version

docs.title: Problem: ROS2 packages not found
docs.text:
Symptoms: Text Only

Package 'ros-humble-desktop' has no installation candidate

Solution: Bash

# Re-add ROS2 repository
sudo rm /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ros2.list
sudo curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ros/rosdistro/master/ros.key \
  -o /usr/share/keyrings/ros-archive-keyring.gpg

echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/ros-archive-keyring.gpg] \
  http://packages.ros.org/ros2/ubuntu $(. /etc/os-release && echo $UBUNTU_CODENAME) main" | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ros2.list > /dev/null

sudo apt update
sudo apt install ros-humble-desktop

docs.title: Problem: Camera not detected
docs.text:
Diagnostics: Bash

# List video devices
ls -l /dev/video*

# Check kernel messages
dmesg | grep -i camera

# Test with GStreamer
gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video0 ! xvimagesink

Solutions:

CSI Camera Not Detected
  1. Check physical connection:
  2. Lift black latch on CSI port
  3. Ensure cable contacts face PCB

  4. Press latch firmly closed

  5. Verify camera is enabled: Bash

    # Edit boot config
sudo nano /boot/config.txt

# Ensure line is present:
camera_auto_detect=1

# Reboot
sudo reboot

  6. Test with nvgstcapture: Bash

    nvgstcapture-1.0

USB Camera Not Detected

  1. Check USB connection: Bash

    lsusb
# Should show camera device

  2. Verify permissions: Bash

    sudo usermod -aG video $USER
newgrp video

# Check device permissions
ls -l /dev/video0
# Should show: crw-rw---- 1 root video

  3. Try different USB port:

  4. USB 3.0 ports for high bandwidth
  5. Check power requirements

docs.text:
Solution: Bash

# Reduce resolution
ros2 param set /camera_node image_width 640
ros2 param set /camera_node image_height 480

# Reduce framerate
ros2 param set /camera_node framerate 15.0

docs.title: Problem: Object detection not working
docs.text:
Diagnostics: Bash

# Check if model file exists
ls ~/ros2_ws/src/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/models/*.engine

# Check GPU usage
tegrastats

# View detection node logs
ros2 node list
ros2 node info /object_detection

Solutions:

Model file not found Bash
# Download models
cd ~/ros2_ws/src/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
./scripts/download_models.sh

# Or manually download
wget https://github.com/TNG-Blue/models/releases/download/v1.0/yolov8n.engine
mv yolov8n.engine models/
TensorRT engine incompatible Bash
# Rebuild engine for your platform
cd ~/ros2_ws/src/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
python3 scripts/export_tensorrt.py \
  --weights models/yolov8n.pt \
  --device 0 \
  --include engine \
  --dynamic
Low detection accuracy YAML
# Edit config/detection_params.yaml
detection:
  confidence_threshold: 0.3  # Lower for more detections
  nms_threshold: 0.45        # Non-max suppression
  input_size: [640, 640]     # Higher resolution

docs.title: Problem: Detection too slow (<10 FPS)
docs.text:
Solutions:

  1. Use smaller model: YAML

    # config/detection_params.yaml
model_path: "models/yolov8n.engine"  # Nano (fastest)
# vs yolov8s.engine (small)
# vs yolov8m.engine (medium)

  2. Reduce input resolution: YAML

    input_size: [416, 416]  # Instead of [640, 640]

  3. Enable power mode: Bash

    sudo nvpmodel -m 0  # Maximum performance
sudo jetson_clocks

docs.title: Problem: SLAM not building map
docs.text:
Diagnostics: Bash

# Check LIDAR data
ros2 topic echo /scan --once

# Check TF tree
ros2 run tf2_tools view_frames
evince frames.pdf

# Check SLAM node
ros2 node info /slam_toolbox

Solutions:

LIDAR not publishing Bash
# Check LIDAR connection
ls /dev/ttyUSB*

# Set permissions
sudo chmod 666 /dev/ttyUSB0

# Or permanent fix
sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER
newgrp dialout

# Restart LIDAR node
ros2 launch rplidar_ros rplidar_a2_launch.py
Robot moving too fast YAML
# config/slam_params.yaml
minimum_travel_distance: 0.1  # Increase for slower mapping
minimum_travel_heading: 0.15
Poor loop closure YAML
# config/slam_params.yaml
loop_search_maximum_distance: 5.0  # Increase search radius
do_loop_closing: true
loop_match_minimum_chain_size: 10

docs.title: Problem: Robot not navigating to goal
docs.text:
Diagnostics: Bash

# Check navigation status
ros2 topic echo /navigate_to_pose/_action/status

# View costmaps
ros2 run rqt_image_view rqt_image_view /global_costmap/costmap
ros2 run rqt_image_view rqt_image_view /local_costmap/costmap

# Check planned path
ros2 topic echo /plan

Solutions:

Robot stuck / won't move

  1. Check footprint: YAML

    # config/nav_params.yaml
robot_radius: 0.2  # Increase if getting stuck

  2. Adjust costmap inflation: YAML

    inflation_layer:
  inflation_radius: 0.55
  cost_scaling_factor: 3.0

  3. Enable recovery behaviors: YAML

    enable_rotate_recovery: true
enable_backup_recovery: true

Goal unreachable
  • Ensure goal is not in obstacle
  • Check if path exists in global costmap
  • Try setting intermediate waypoints

docs.title: Problem: Motors not responding
docs.text:
Diagnostics: Bash

# Check motor controller communication
ros2 topic list | grep cmd_vel

# Echo velocity commands
ros2 topic echo /cmd_vel

# Test motor controller directly
ros2 run jetbot_control motor_test.py

Solutions:

I2C motor controller Bash
# Check I2C devices
i2cdetect -y -r 1

# Should show address (typically 0x60)
# If not visible, check wiring

# Test I2C communication
i2cget -y 1 0x60 0x00
Ethernet motor controller Bash
# Check network connection
ping 192.168.1.103  # Portenta H7

# Check ROS2 communication
ros2 topic list | grep motor
ros2 topic echo /motor/status

docs.title: Problem: IMU data erratic
docs.text:
Solution: Bash

# Calibrate IMU
ros2 run jetbot_imu calibrate_imu.py

# Place robot on level surface
# Follow prompts for 6-axis calibration

# Verify after calibration
ros2 topic echo /imu/data

docs.title: Problem: GPS not acquiring satellites
docs.text:
Solution: Bash

# Ensure outdoor location
# Wait 2-5 minutes for cold start

# Check GPS status
cgps -s

# If no satellites after 5 minutes:
# - Check antenna connection
# - Verify power supply (5V)
# - Try different location (away from buildings)

docs.title: Problem: ROS2 nodes can't communicate
docs.text:
Diagnostics: Bash

# Check ROS domain
echo $ROS_DOMAIN_ID

# Check multicast
ros2 multicast receive
# In another terminal:
ros2 multicast send

# Check firewall
sudo ufw status

Solutions:

Set ROS domain ID Bash
echo 'export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

# Verify
echo $ROS_DOMAIN_ID
Configure firewall Bash
# Allow ROS2 DDS ports
sudo ufw allow 7400:7500/udp
sudo ufw allow 7400:7500/tcp

# Or disable firewall (not recommended for production)
sudo ufw disable
Use Cyclone DDS Bash
# Install Cyclone DDS
sudo apt install ros-humble-rmw-cyclonedds-cpp

# Set as middleware
echo 'export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

docs.title: Problem: High latency on WiFi
docs.text:
Solution: Bash

# Use 5GHz band if available
sudo iwconfig wlan0 channel 36

# Reduce WiFi power saving
sudo iw dev wlan0 set power_save off

# Use Ethernet for critical data

docs.title: Problem: System running slow
docs.text:
Diagnostics: Bash

# Check CPU usage
htop

# Check GPU usage
tegrastats

# Check disk I/O
iotop

# Check memory
free -h

Solutions:

High CPU usage Bash
# Set power mode (Jetson)
sudo nvpmodel -m 0  # Maximum performance
sudo jetson_clocks

# Reduce node load
# - Lower camera framerate
# - Use smaller detection model
# - Disable unused sensors
High memory usage Bash
# Check memory per process
ps aux --sort=-%mem | head

# Add swap space (see above)
# Or close unused processes
Thermal throttling Bash
# Check temperature
tegrastats | grep temp

# If over 70°C:
# - Add active cooling (fan)
# - Improve chassis ventilation
# - Reduce power mode temporarily
sudo nvpmodel -m 2  # Lower power mode

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL is built on a modular, scalable architecture designed for real-world robotics deployments.

docs.title: 1. Perception Stack
docs.text:
• Object Detection (YOLOv8/v5, MobileNet)
  • Stereo Vision & Depth Estimation
  • Night Vision (Infrared)
  • Sensor Fusion (IMU, Compass)

docs.title: 2. Navigation Stack
docs.text:
• SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping)
  • Path Planning (RRT*, Dijkstra)
  • Obstacle Avoidance
  • GPS Integration

docs.title: 3. Control Stack
docs.text:
• Motion Control (PID, MPC)
  • Servo Management
  • Motor Control
  • Safety Systems

docs.title: 4. Communication Stack
docs.text:
• ROS2 Middleware
  • Network Bridge
  • Sensor Streaming
  • Command Interface

docs.title: Main Processor
docs.text:
• Jetson Orin Nano Super: Quad-core ARM64 @ 2.1 GHz
  • GPU: 128 CUDA cores + 40-core Tensor Engine
  • Memory: 8GB LPDDR5
  • Storage: 128GB eMMC

docs.title: Sensor Suite
docs.text:
• Cameras:
  • RGB/Stereo camera (USB/CSI)
  • Night vision (IR)
  • Fish-eye lens options
  • IMU: 9-DoF accelerometer + gyroscope + magnetometer
  • Depth Sensor: Stereo matching or ToF
  • GPS: Optional GNSS receiver

docs.title: Actuators
docs.text:
• Motors: 2-4 DC/servo motors
  • Servos: Pan-tilt mechanism (up to 16 channels)
  • Power System: Battery management, voltage regulation

docs.title: Communication
docs.text:
• Gigabit Ethernet
  • WiFi 6 (802.11ax)
  • Optional: 4G/5G module, LoRa

docs.title: Operating System
docs.text:
• Base OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
  • Kernel: NVIDIA Jetpack 6.0 (Linux 5.15)
  • Real-time: Optional RT_PREEMPT kernel patch

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
• ROS2: Humble Distribution
  • DDS: RTI Connext or CycloneDDS
  • Message Protocol: Protobuf, JSON, YAML

docs.title: AI/ML Framework
docs.text:
• Inference Engine: TensorRT 8.6+
  • CUDA: 12.2+
  • Deep Learning: PyTorch, TensorFlow Lite

docs.title: Additional Libraries
docs.text:
• OpenCV: 4.8+ (with CUDA support)
  • PCL: Point Cloud Library 1.13+
  • Eigen: Linear algebra
  • Boost: C++ utilities

docs.title: Perception Pipeline
docs.text:
Text Only
Camera Input → Image Preprocessing → Object Detection 
           → Post-processing → ROS2 Topic (Detections)

docs.title: Navigation Pipeline
docs.text:
Text Only
Sensor Fusion → SLAM → Map Generation → Path Planning 
            → Motion Control → Motor Commands

docs.title: Communication Pipeline
docs.text:
Text Only
Local Sensors → ROS2 Nodes → Network Bridge 
            → Remote System → Feedback Loop

docs.title: 🏆 Design Principles
docs.text:
1. Modularity: Independent, reusable components
  2. Scalability: From single robot to multi-robot systems
  3. Real-time: Deterministic timing for safety-critical tasks
  4. Efficiency: Optimized power and computational usage
  5. Robustness: Fault tolerance and error recovery
  6. Security: Encrypted communication and access control

docs.title: Custom Models
docs.text: Train custom YOLOv8 detection models for your specific use case.

docs.title: 🎯 Learning Objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this tutorial, you will: - ✅ Prepare custom dataset for training - ✅ Train YOLOv8 model on your data - ✅ Quantize model for edge deployment - ✅ Deploy and test on Jetbot - ✅ Measure performance metrics

Estimated Time: 2-3 hours Difficulty Level: Advanced Prerequisites: Sensor Setup completed

docs.title: Step 1: Collect Images
docs.text:
Bash
# Create dataset directory
mkdir -p ~/custom_dataset/{images,labels}

# Option A: Record with ROS2
ros2 bag record /camera/image_raw -o ~/camera_recording

# Extract images from bag
python3 << 'EOF'
import rosbag2
import cv2
from cv_bridge import CvBridge
import os

bridge = CvBridge()
bag_path = os.path.expanduser('~/camera_recording')
output_dir = os.path.expanduser('~/custom_dataset/images')

reader = rosbag2.SequentialReader()
reader.open(bag_path)

counter = 0
while reader.has_next():
    msg_type, data, _ = reader.read_next()
    if msg_type == 'sensor_msgs/Image':
        cv_image = bridge.imgmsg_to_cv2(data, desired_encoding='bgr8')
        filename = os.path.join(output_dir, f'image_{counter:06d}.jpg')
        cv2.imwrite(filename, cv_image)
        counter += 1

print(f"Extracted {counter} images")
EOF

# Option B: Manual capture
python3 << 'EOF'
import cv2
cap = cv2.VideoCapture(0)
counter = 0
output_dir = os.path.expanduser('~/custom_dataset/images')

while True:
    ret, frame = cap.read()
    if not ret:
        break

    cv2.imshow('Press SPACE to capture, Q to quit', frame)
    key = cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF

    if key == ord(' '):
        filename = os.path.join(output_dir, f'image_{counter:06d}.jpg')
        cv2.imwrite(filename, frame)
        counter += 1
        print(f"Captured: {counter}")

    elif key == ord('q'):
        break

cap.release()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()
print(f"Total captured: {counter}")
EOF

docs.title: Step 3: Create Dataset Structure
docs.text:
Bash
# Organize into train/val/test splits
mkdir -p ~/custom_dataset/{train,val,test}/{images,labels}

# Split dataset (80% train, 10% val, 10% test)
python3 << 'EOF'
import os
import shutil
import random

source_images = os.path.expanduser('~/custom_dataset/images')
source_labels = os.path.expanduser('~/custom_dataset/labels')

# Get all images
images = sorted([f for f in os.listdir(source_images) if f.endswith('.jpg')])
random.shuffle(images)

# Calculate split
total = len(images)
train_count = int(total * 0.8)
val_count = int(total * 0.1)

print(f"Total: {total}, Train: {train_count}, Val: {val_count}, Test: {total-train_count-val_count}")

# Train split
for i, img in enumerate(images[:train_count]):
    shutil.copy(
        os.path.join(source_images, img),
        os.path.expanduser(f'~/custom_dataset/train/images/{img}')
    )
    label_file = img.replace('.jpg', '.txt')
    shutil.copy(
        os.path.join(source_labels, label_file),
        os.path.expanduser(f'~/custom_dataset/train/labels/{label_file}')
    )

# Val split
for img in images[train_count:train_count+val_count]:
    shutil.copy(
        os.path.join(source_images, img),
        os.path.expanduser(f'~/custom_dataset/val/images/{img}')
    )
    label_file = img.replace('.jpg', '.txt')
    shutil.copy(
        os.path.join(source_labels, label_file),
        os.path.expanduser(f'~/custom_dataset/val/labels/{label_file}')
    )

# Test split
for img in images[train_count+val_count:]:
    shutil.copy(
        os.path.join(source_images, img),
        os.path.expanduser(f'~/custom_dataset/test/images/{img}')
    )

print("✓ Dataset split complete")
EOF

docs.title: Step 2: Create Training Script
docs.text:
Bash
# Create training script
python3 << 'EOF'
from ultralytics import YOLO
import os

# Create dataset.yaml
dataset_yaml = """
path: /home/jetbot/custom_dataset
train: train/images
val: val/images
test: test/images

nc: 2  # Number of classes (change as needed)
names: ['object1', 'object2']  # Class names
"""

yaml_path = os.path.expanduser('~/custom_dataset/dataset.yaml')
with open(yaml_path, 'w') as f:
    f.write(dataset_yaml)

# Load model (nano for Jetbot)
model = YOLO('yolov8n.pt')

# Train
results = model.train(
    data=yaml_path,
    epochs=100,
    imgsz=640,
    patience=20,  # Early stopping
    device=0,  # GPU device
    batch=16,
    optimizer='SGD',
    lr0=0.01,
    lrf=0.01,
    momentum=0.937,
    weight_decay=0.0005,
    warmup_epochs=3,
    warmup_momentum=0.8,
    warmup_bias_lr=0.1,
    close_mosaic=10,
    project=os.path.expanduser('~/yolov8_training'),
    name='custom_model_v1',
    exist_ok=False,
    pretrained=True,
    amp=True,  # Mixed precision
    mosaic=1.0,
    flipud=0.5,
    fliplr=0.5,
    hsv_h=0.015,
    hsv_s=0.7,
    hsv_v=0.4,
)

print("\n✓ Training complete!")
print(f"Best model: {results.save_dir}/weights/best.pt")
EOF

# Run training
python3 train_model.py

docs.title: Step 1: Export Model
docs.text:
Bash
# Export to ONNX
python3 << 'EOF'
from ultralytics import YOLO
import os

model_path = os.path.expanduser('~/yolov8_training/custom_model_v1/weights/best.pt')
model = YOLO(model_path)

# Export to ONNX
export_path = model.export(format='onnx', half=False, imgsz=640)
print(f"✓ Exported to: {export_path}")

# Export to TensorRT (for GPU optimization)
export_path_trt = model.export(format='engine', half=True, imgsz=640, device=0)
print(f"✓ Exported TensorRT: {export_path_trt}")
EOF

docs.title: Step 2: Quantize for Edge
docs.text:
Bash
# Quantize to INT8 using TensorRT
python3 << 'EOF'
from ultralytics import YOLO
import os

model_path = os.path.expanduser('~/yolov8_training/custom_model_v1/weights/best.pt')
model = YOLO(model_path)

# Export to INT8 quantized model
export_path = model.export(
    format='engine',
    half=True,  # FP16
    int8=True,  # INT8 quantization
    imgsz=640,
    device=0,
    data=os.path.expanduser('~/custom_dataset/dataset.yaml')
)

print(f"✓ Quantized model: {export_path}")

# Check model size
original_size = os.path.getsize(model_path) / (1024**2)
quantized_size = os.path.getsize(export_path) / (1024**2)

print(f"\nModel Size:")
print(f"  Original: {original_size:.2f} MB")
print(f"  Quantized: {quantized_size:.2f} MB")
print(f"  Reduction: {(1-quantized_size/original_size)*100:.1f}%")
EOF

docs.title: Step 1: Evaluate Model
docs.text:
Bash
# Test model performance
python3 << 'EOF'
from ultralytics import YOLO
import os

model_path = os.path.expanduser('~/yolov8_training/custom_model_v1/weights/best.pt')
model = YOLO(model_path)

# Validate
metrics = model.val(
    data=os.path.expanduser('~/custom_dataset/dataset.yaml'),
    imgsz=640,
    conf=0.5,
    device=0
)

print("\n=== Validation Metrics ===")
print(f"mAP50: {metrics.box.map50:.3f}")
print(f"mAP50-95: {metrics.box.map:.3f}")
print(f"Precision: {metrics.box.p.mean():.3f}")
print(f"Recall: {metrics.box.r.mean():.3f}")
EOF

docs.text:
Bash
# Test on single image
python3 << 'EOF'
from ultralytics import YOLO
import cv2

model_path = os.path.expanduser('~/yolov8_training/custom_model_v1/weights/best.pt')
model = YOLO(model_path)

# Run inference
results = model.predict(
    source='/path/to/test/image.jpg',
    conf=0.5,
    device=0,
    visualize=True
)

# Display results
for result in results:
    print(f"Detections: {len(result.boxes)}")
    for box in result.boxes:
        print(f"  Class: {result.names[int(box.cls)]}, Conf: {box.conf:.2f}")

    # Save result
    result.save(filename='prediction.jpg')
EOF

docs.title: 3.1 Create Fleet Communication Node
docs.text:
Bash
# Create coordinator
cat > ~/ros2_ws/src/jetbot_bringup/src/fleet_coordinator.py << 'EOF'
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from geometry_msgs.msg import Pose, PoseArray
from std_msgs.msg import String
import json

class FleetCoordinator(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('fleet_coordinator')

        # Subscribers for each robot pose
        self.pose_sub1 = self.create_subscription(
            Pose, '/jetbot1/pose', self.pose_callback1, 10)
        self.pose_sub2 = self.create_subscription(
            Pose, '/jetbot2/pose', self.pose_callback2, 10)

        # Publisher for fleet state
        self.fleet_state_pub = self.create_publisher(
            String, '/fleet/state', 10)

        # Robot positions
        self.robot_poses = {
            'jetbot1': None,
            'jetbot2': None
        }

        # Timer for periodic updates
        self.timer = self.create_timer(1.0, self.update_fleet_state)

    def pose_callback1(self, msg):
        self.robot_poses['jetbot1'] = msg

    def pose_callback2(self, msg):
        self.robot_poses['jetbot2'] = msg

    def update_fleet_state(self):
        # Create fleet state message
        fleet_state = {
            'timestamp': self.get_clock().now().to_msg(),
            'robots': {}
        }

        for name, pose in self.robot_poses.items():
            if pose:
                fleet_state['robots'][name] = {
                    'x': float(pose.position.x),
                    'y': float(pose.position.y),
                    'z': float(pose.position.z),
                }

        # Publish
        msg = String()
        msg.data = json.dumps(fleet_state, default=str)
        self.fleet_state_pub.publish(msg)

        self.get_logger().debug(f"Fleet state: {fleet_state}")

def main():
    rclpy.init()
    coordinator = FleetCoordinator()
    rclpy.spin(coordinator)
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
EOF

# Make executable
chmod +x ~/ros2_ws/src/jetbot_bringup/src/fleet_coordinator.py

docs.title: 4.1 Create Multi-Robot Mission
docs.text:
Bash
# Create mission planner
cat > ~/multi_robot_mission.py << 'EOF'
import rclpy
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist
import time

class MultiRobotMission:
    def __init__(self):
        rclpy.init()
        self.node = rclpy.create_node('multi_robot_mission')

        # Publishers for each robot
        self.pub1 = self.node.create_publisher(Twist, '/jetbot1/cmd_vel', 10)
        self.pub2 = self.node.create_publisher(Twist, '/jetbot2/cmd_vel', 10)

    def move_robot(self, pub, linear_x, angular_z, duration):
        """Move robot for specified duration"""
        twist = Twist()
        twist.linear.x = linear_x
        twist.angular.z = angular_z

        for _ in range(int(duration * 10)):
            pub.publish(twist)
            time.sleep(0.1)

        # Stop
        twist.linear.x = 0.0
        twist.angular.z = 0.0
        pub.publish(twist)

    def parallel_patrol(self):
        """Both robots patrol in parallel"""
        print("Starting parallel patrol mission...")

        # Robot 1 moves forward
        self.move_robot(self.pub1, 0.2, 0.0, 3.0)

        # Robot 2 moves forward
        self.move_robot(self.pub2, 0.2, 0.0, 3.0)

        print("✓ Parallel patrol complete")

    def formation_movement(self):
        """Robots maintain formation"""
        print("Formation movement: Line formation...")

        # Start simultaneously
        for i in range(30):
            twist1 = Twist()
            twist1.linear.x = 0.2
            self.pub1.publish(twist1)

            twist2 = Twist()
            twist2.linear.x = 0.2
            self.pub2.publish(twist2)

            time.sleep(0.1)

        # Stop
        twist = Twist()
        self.pub1.publish(twist)
        self.pub2.publish(twist)

        print("✓ Formation complete")

    def leapfrog_pattern(self):
        """Robots alternate movement"""
        print("Leapfrog pattern...")

        # Robot 1 moves
        self.move_robot(self.pub1, 0.2, 0.0, 2.0)

        # Robot 2 moves
        self.move_robot(self.pub2, 0.2, 0.0, 2.0)

        # Robot 1 moves again
        self.move_robot(self.pub1, 0.2, 0.0, 2.0)

        print("✓ Leapfrog pattern complete")

def main():
    mission = MultiRobotMission()

    # Run missions
    mission.parallel_patrol()
    time.sleep(1.0)

    mission.formation_movement()
    time.sleep(1.0)

    mission.leapfrog_pattern()

    print("\n✓ All missions complete!")
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
EOF

# Run mission
python3 multi_robot_mission.py

docs.title: SLAM Configuration
docs.text: Advanced SLAM tuning for optimal navigation and mapping.

docs.title: 🎯 Learning Objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this tutorial, you will: - ✅ Understand VI-SLAM theory and parameters - ✅ Tune SLAM for your environment - ✅ Configure loop closure detection - ✅ Optimize map quality - ✅ Troubleshoot SLAM issues

Estimated Time: 1.5-2 hours Difficulty Level: Advanced Prerequisites: Sensor Setup + Custom Models completed

docs.title: 🏗️ SLAM Architecture
docs.text:
YAML
Visual-Inertial SLAM Pipeline:

Input:
  ├─ Camera frames (30 Hz)
  └─ IMU data (200 Hz)

Processing:
  ├─ Feature extraction (ORB/SIFT)
  ├─ Feature matching
  ├─ Pose estimation
  ├─ IMU fusion (EKF)
  ├─ Map building
  └─ Loop closure detection

Output:
  ├─ Robot pose (x, y, yaw)
  ├─ Occupancy grid map
  ├─ 3D point cloud
  └─ Trajectory history

docs.title: Step 1: Access SLAM Configuration
docs.text:
Bash
# Location of SLAM config
vim ~/ros2_ws/src/jetbot_slam/config/slam_params.yaml

# Key parameters:
# 1. Feature detection
# 2. Feature matching
# 3. Pose estimation
# 4. Map management
# 5. Loop closure

docs.title: Step 2: Feature Detection Tuning
docs.text:
YAML
# config/slam_params.yaml

feature_detector:
  type: "orb"  # Options: orb, sift, akaze

  # ORB parameters
  n_features: 500        # Number of features to detect (increase for texture-rich environments)
  scale_factor: 1.2      # Pyramid decimation ratio
  n_levels: 8            # Number of pyramid levels
  first_frame: 0         # First frame scale level
  edge_threshold: 19     # Edge response threshold
  patch_size: 31         # Patch size
  fast_threshold: 10     # FAST keypoint detector threshold

  # Tuning guide:
  # - Low texture environment: Increase n_features to 1000
  # - High texture environment: Can use 200-300
  # - Few features detected: Lower fast_threshold (8-10)
  # - Too many features: Raise fast_threshold (15-20)

docs.title: Step 3: Feature Matching Configuration
docs.text:
YAML
matcher:
  type: "BruteForce"  # Options: BruteForce, FLANN, FastHeuristic

  # Matching parameters
  norm_type: "HAMMING"    # For ORB features
  max_distance: 100       # Max descriptor distance
  ratio_test: 0.75        # Lowe's ratio test threshold

  # Good matches per frame
  min_matches: 10         # Minimum matches required
  max_matches: 1000       # Maximum to process

  # Tuning tips:
  # - Few matches: Increase max_distance (100->150)
  # - Too many matches: Lower ratio_test (0.75->0.6)
  # - Unstable tracking: Require more matches (min_matches++)

docs.title: Step 4: Pose Estimation
docs.text:
YAML
pose_estimator:
  algorithm: "epnp"  # Options: epnp, iterative, ransac

  # RANSAC parameters (if using RANSAC)
  ransac_threshold: 8.0     # Pixel distance threshold
  ransac_prob: 0.99         # Confidence probability
  ransac_max_iters: 100     # Maximum iterations

  # Refinement
  refine_iterations: 5      # Bundle adjustment refinement

  # Tuning guide:
  # - Many outliers: Lower ransac_threshold (8->5)
  # - Unstable poses: Increase ransac_max_iters
  # - Slow processing: Reduce ransac_prob (0.99->0.95)

docs.title: Step 1: Map Parameters
docs.text:
YAML
mapping:
  # Map representation
  type: "occupancy_grid"  # Options: grid, point_cloud, feature_map

  # Grid parameters
  grid_size: 100          # Grid cells in each direction
  cell_size: 0.1          # Size of each cell (meters)
  origin: [-5.0, -5.0]    # Map origin (meters)

  # Memory management
  max_memory_mb: 500      # Maximum map memory
  keyframe_interval: 0.5  # Distance between keyframes (meters)
  max_keyframes: 1000     # Maximum keyframes to keep

  # Optimization frequency
  local_window: 20        # Keyframes in local window
  global_window: 200      # Keyframes in global window

  # Tuning:
  # - Map growing too large: Increase cell_size or reduce grid_size
  # - Poor map quality: Decrease keyframe_interval
  # - Memory issues: Reduce max_keyframes or local_window

docs.title: Step 2: Keyframe Selection
docs.text:
YAML
keyframe_selector:
  # Criteria for adding keyframes
  translation_threshold: 0.3   # meters
  rotation_threshold: 0.1      # radians (5.7°)
  time_threshold: 0.5          # seconds

  # Additional criteria
  feature_threshold: 100       # Min tracked features
  velocity_threshold: 2.0      # Max velocity for keyframe

  # Tuning:
  # - Too many keyframes: Increase translation_threshold
  # - Sparse map: Decrease translation_threshold
  # - Slow mapping: Increase thresholds
  # - Poor localization: Decrease thresholds

docs.title: Step 1: Configure Loop Closure
docs.text:
YAML
loop_closure:
  enabled: true

  # Loop detection
  min_keyframes_between: 50     # Min keyframes between loops
  similarity_threshold: 0.7     # Descriptor similarity (0-1)
  geometric_threshold: 0.8      # Geometric consistency (0-1)

  # Candidate pool
  max_candidates: 50            # Max loop closure candidates
  covisibility_min: 10          # Min co-visible frames

  # Verification
  verification_inliers: 30      # Min inliers to accept loop
  verification_iterations: 100  # RANSAC iterations

  # Optimization
  local_ba_window: 20           # Local bundle adjustment window
  global_ba_frequency: 50       # Global BA every N loops

  # Tuning:
  # - Few loop closures detected:
  #   - Lower similarity_threshold (0.7->0.6)
  #   - Reduce min_keyframes_between (50->30)
  # - False loop closures:
  #   - Increase geometric_threshold (0.8->0.9)
  #   - Increase verification_inliers (30->50)

docs.title: Step 2: Enable Place Recognition

Bash

pip3 install place-recognition

# Or use pre-trained vocabulary
mkdir -p ~/ros2_ws/src/jetbot_slam/vocabulary

docs.title: Step 4: Analyze Results
docs.text:
Bash
# Check mapping quality
python3 << 'EOF'
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import os

# Load map
map_file = '/home/jetbot/slam_test_output/map.pgm'
map_img = Image.open(map_file)
map_array = np.array(map_img)

# Analyze
print("Map Statistics:")
print(f"  Size: {map_array.shape}")
print(f"  Unknown cells: {np.sum(map_array == 205)}")
print(f"  Free cells: {np.sum(map_array == 254)}")
print(f"  Occupied cells: {np.sum(map_array < 50)}")
print(f"  Occupancy: {np.sum(map_array < 50) / map_array.size * 100:.1f}%")

# Check for loop closures
trajectory_file = '/home/jetbot/slam_test_output/trajectory.txt'
if os.path.exists(trajectory_file):
    traj = np.loadtxt(trajectory_file)
    # First pose
    start = traj[0, :2]
    # Last pose
    end = traj[-1, :2]
    # Distance
    dist = np.linalg.norm(end - start)
    print(f"\nLoop Closure:")
    print(f"  Start pose: {start}")
    print(f"  End pose: {end}")
    print(f"  Distance: {dist:.3f} m")
    print(f"  Loop closed: {'✓' if dist < 0.5 else '✗'}")
EOF

docs.title: Issue: Features Not Detected
docs.text:
YAML
Symptoms: Frame count shows 0 features

Solutions:
  1. Check lighting - need well-lit environment
  2. Lower fast_threshold (10 -> 8)
  3. Increase n_features (500 -> 1000)
  4. Check camera focus - may be blurry
  5. Try different feature detector (ORB -> SIFT)

docs.title: Issue: Unstable Tracking
docs.text:
YAML
Symptoms: Pose jumps around, map distorted

Solutions:
  1. Verify IMU calibration - run sensor_setup tutorial
  2. Reduce movement speed (0.3 m/s -> 0.1 m/s)
  3. Increase RANSAC threshold (8 -> 10)
  4. Reduce feature matching ratio (0.75 -> 0.8)
  5. Check for fast rotations - SLAM struggles with >180°/s

docs.title: Issue: No Loop Closures
docs.text:
YAML
Symptoms: Map grows unbounded, no optimization

Solutions:
  1. Lower loop closure similarity (0.7 -> 0.6)
  2. Reduce min_keyframes_between (50 -> 30)
  3. Enable place recognition vocabulary
  4. Record longer trajectory (>5 minutes)
  5. Check environment has recognizable features

docs.title: Metric 1: Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE)
docs.text:
Bash
# Calculate ATE
python3 << 'EOF'
import numpy as np

# Ground truth (if available)
gt = np.loadtxt('ground_truth.txt')  # [x, y, z]

# SLAM trajectory
slam_traj = np.loadtxt('slam_trajectory.txt')  # [x, y, z]

# Calculate error
errors = np.linalg.norm(slam_traj - gt, axis=1)
print(f"ATE Mean: {np.mean(errors):.3f} m")
print(f"ATE RMSE: {np.sqrt(np.mean(errors**2)):.3f} m")
print(f"ATE Max: {np.max(errors):.3f} m")

# Good ATE: < 0.1m for small environments
# Acceptable ATE: < 0.5m for large environments
EOF

docs.title: Metric 2: Map Quality
docs.text:
YAML
Good Map Indicators:
  ✓ Straight walls appear straight
  ✓ Closed loops properly aligned
  ✓ No "ghosts" or double walls
  ✓ Reasonable map size
  ✓ Occupancy makes sense

docs.text:

  • Pose estimates stable (< 0.1m drift per meter traveled)
  • Map building smoothly
  • Loop closures detected when expected
  • ATE < 0.5m over test trajectory
  • Processing time < 100ms per frame

docs.title: Camera Calibration
docs.text: Calibrate your camera for accurate vision-based perception.

docs.title: 🎯 Learning Objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this tutorial, you will: - ✅ Understand camera calibration concepts - ✅ Capture calibration images - ✅ Run OpenCV calibration process - ✅ Verify calibration accuracy - ✅ Save calibration for future use

Estimated Time: 30-40 minutes Difficulty Level: Beginner Prerequisites: First Mission completed

docs.title: Why Calibrate?
docs.text:
Cameras introduce distortions that affect: - Object detection accuracy - Depth estimation - SLAM performance - 3D reconstruction quality

Calibration removes these distortions by computing: - Camera matrix (K): Internal camera parameters - Distortion coefficients: Lens distortion parameters

docs.title: Before vs After
docs.text:
YAML
Before Calibration:
  ├─ Straight lines appear curved
  ├─ Objects appear distorted
  ├─ Depth measurements inaccurate
  └─ SLAM performance poor

After Calibration:
  ├─ Straight lines remain straight
  ├─ Accurate object localization
  ├─ Correct depth estimation
  └─ Improved SLAM performance

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
• Printed checkerboard pattern (see Calibration Checkerboard PDF)
  • Flat surface to mount checkerboard
  • Good lighting conditions
  • Jetbot with camera ready

docs.title: Software
docs.text:
• OpenCV installed
  • ROS2 camera drivers running
  • Image capture tools

docs.title: Optional But Helpful
docs.text:
• Tripod for consistent camera angle
  • Multiple print sizes of checkerboard
  • Dark and light backgrounds for testing

docs.title: 2.1 Setup Camera

Bash

docs.title: 2.2 Capture Strategy
docs.text:
Capture ~20-30 images from different angles:

YAML
Image Captures:
  1. Front view (center): 1 image
  2. Rotated left (30°): 2-3 images
  3. Rotated right (30°): 2-3 images
  4. Tilted up (30°): 2-3 images
  5. Tilted down (30°): 2-3 images
  6. Different distances (near/far): 4-5 images
  7. Different heights: 3-4 images
  8. Corner views: 4 images

Total: 20-30 images

docs.text:
Bash
# Create capture directory
mkdir -p ~/calibration_images

# Method 1: ROS bag (captures video)
ros2 bag record -o ~/calibration_images/camera_calibration \
  /camera/image_raw /camera/camera_info

# Move camera around for 20-30 seconds with different angles
# Then press Ctrl+C to stop

# Method 2: Manual capture script
python3 << 'EOF'
import cv2
import rclpy
from sensor_msgs.msg import Image
from cv_bridge import CvBridge
import os

class ImageCapture:
    def __init__(self):
        rclpy.init()
        self.node = rclpy.create_node('image_capture')
        self.subscription = self.node.create_subscription(
            Image, '/camera/image_raw', self.image_callback, 10)
        self.bridge = CvBridge()
        self.counter = 0
        self.output_dir = os.path.expanduser('~/calibration_images')
        os.makedirs(self.output_dir, exist_ok=True)

    def image_callback(self, msg):
        cv_image = self.bridge.imgmsg_to_cv2(msg, desired_encoding='bgr8')

        # Show image
        cv2.imshow('Camera Feed - Press SPACE to capture, Q to quit', cv_image)
        key = cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF

        if key == ord(' '):  # Space bar to capture
            filename = os.path.join(self.output_dir, f'calibration_{self.counter:03d}.jpg')
            cv2.imwrite(filename, cv_image)
            print(f"Captured: {filename}")
            self.counter += 1
            print(f"Total captured: {self.counter}/30")

        elif key == ord('q'):  # Q to quit
            cv2.destroyAllWindows()
            rclpy.shutdown()
            return

if __name__ == '__main__':
    capture = ImageCapture()
    rclpy.spin(capture.node)
EOF

docs.title: 3.2 Method 1: OpenCV Calibration Script
docs.text:
Bash
# Create calibration script
python3 << 'EOF'
import cv2
import numpy as np
import glob
import os

# Checkerboard dimensions (10x7 with 30mm squares)
CHECKERBOARD = (10, 7)
criteria = (cv2.TERM_CRITERIA_EPS + cv2.TERM_CRITERIA_MAX_ITER, 30, 0.001)

# Prepare object points (0,0,0), (1,0,0), ..., (9,6,0)
objp = np.zeros((1, CHECKERBOARD[0] * CHECKERBOARD[1], 3), np.float32)
objp[0, :, :2] = np.mgrid[0:CHECKERBOARD[0], 0:CHECKERBOARD[1]].T.reshape(-1, 2) * 30  # 30mm squares

# Arrays to store object points and image points
objpoints = []  # 3D points in real world space
imgpoints = []  # 2D points in image plane

# Load calibration images
images = glob.glob(os.path.expanduser('~/calibration_images/calibration_*.jpg'))
print(f"Found {len(images)} calibration images")

for fname in images:
    img = cv2.imread(fname)
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

    # Find checkerboard corners
    ret, corners = cv2.findChessboardCorners(gray, CHECKERBOARD, None)

    if ret:
        objpoints.append(objp)

        # Refine corner positions
        corners2 = cv2.cornerSubPix(gray, corners, (11, 11), (-1, -1), criteria)
        imgpoints.append(corners2)

        print(f"✓ {fname}")
    else:
        print(f"✗ {fname} (no checkerboard found)")

if len(objpoints) < 5:
    print("Error: Not enough valid calibration images (minimum 5 required)")
    exit(1)

print(f"\nUsing {len(objpoints)} images for calibration...")

# Calibrate camera
ret, mtx, dist, rvecs, tvecs = cv2.calibrateCamera(
    objpoints, imgpoints, gray.shape[::-1], None, None)

print(f"\nCalibration Results:")
print(f"Reprojection Error: {ret:.4f}")
print(f"\nCamera Matrix (K):\n{mtx}")
print(f"\nDistortion Coefficients:\n{dist}")

# Save calibration
calib_data = {
    'mtx': mtx,
    'dist': dist
}
np.savez(os.path.expanduser('~/camera_calibration.npz'), **calib_data)
print("\n✓ Calibration saved to ~/camera_calibration.npz")

# Test undistortion
print("\nTesting undistortion on first image...")
img = cv2.imread(images[0])
h, w = img.shape[:2]

# Get optimal camera matrix
newcameramtx, roi = cv2.getOptimalNewCameraMatrix(mtx, dist, (w, h), 1, (w, h))

# Undistort image
dst = cv2.undistort(img, mtx, dist, None, newcameramtx)

# Display comparison
cv2.imshow('Original', img)
cv2.imshow('Undistorted', dst)
cv2.waitKey(5000)
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

print("✓ Undistortion test complete")
EOF

docs.title: 4.1 Load and Test Calibration
docs.text:
Bash
# Create verification script
python3 << 'EOF'
import cv2
import numpy as np
import os

# Load calibration
calib_file = os.path.expanduser('~/camera_calibration.npz')
if not os.path.exists(calib_file):
    print("Calibration file not found!")
    exit(1)

calib = np.load(calib_file)
mtx = calib['mtx']
dist = calib['dist']

print("Camera Calibration Parameters:")
print(f"Camera Matrix K:\n{mtx}\n")
print(f"Distortion Coefficients:\n{dist}\n")

# Verify with live camera
cap = cv2.VideoCapture(0)

print("Live preview (press 'q' to quit):")
print("Left: Original | Right: Undistorted")

while True:
    ret, frame = cap.read()
    if not ret:
        break

    # Undistort
    h, w = frame.shape[:2]
    newcameramtx, roi = cv2.getOptimalNewCameraMatrix(mtx, dist, (w, h), 1, (w, h))
    undistorted = cv2.undistort(frame, mtx, dist, None, newcameramtx)

    # Display side by side
    comparison = np.hstack([frame, undistorted])
    cv2.imshow('Calibration Verification', comparison)

    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

cap.release()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()
EOF

docs.title: 6.1 Mission: Patrol Rectangle
docs.text:
Objective: Robot moves in a 1m × 0.5m rectangle pattern

Bash
# Create mission file
cat > first_mission.py << 'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import rclpy
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist
import time

def main():
    rclpy.init()
    node = rclpy.create_node('first_mission')

    # Create publisher for velocity commands
    pub = node.create_publisher(Twist, '/cmd_vel', 10)

    # Initialize twist message
    twist = Twist()

    print("Starting patrol mission...")

    # Forward (1 meter)
    print("Moving forward...")
    twist.linear.x = 0.2  # 0.2 m/s
    twist.angular.z = 0.0
    for _ in range(50):  # 5 seconds at 0.2 m/s = 1 meter
        pub.publish(twist)
        time.sleep(0.1)

    # Turn right (90 degrees)
    print("Turning right...")
    twist.linear.x = 0.0
    twist.angular.z = -0.5  # -0.5 rad/s (clockwise)
    for _ in range(32):  # ~3 seconds for 90 degree turn
        pub.publish(twist)
        time.sleep(0.1)

    # Forward (0.5 meters)
    print("Moving forward...")
    twist.linear.x = 0.2
    twist.angular.z = 0.0
    for _ in range(25):  # 2.5 seconds at 0.2 m/s = 0.5 meters
        pub.publish(twist)
        time.sleep(0.1)

    # Turn right (90 degrees)
    print("Turning right...")
    twist.linear.x = 0.0
    twist.angular.z = -0.5
    for _ in range(32):
        pub.publish(twist)
        time.sleep(0.1)

    # Forward (1 meter back to start)
    print("Moving forward...")
    twist.linear.x = 0.2
    twist.angular.z = 0.0
    for _ in range(50):
        pub.publish(twist)
        time.sleep(0.1)

    # Turn right (90 degrees)
    print("Turning right...")
    twist.linear.x = 0.0
    twist.angular.z = -0.5
    for _ in range(32):
        pub.publish(twist)
        time.sleep(0.1)

    # Forward (0.5 meters)
    print("Moving forward...")
    twist.linear.x = 0.2
    twist.angular.z = 0.0
    for _ in range(25):
        pub.publish(twist)
        time.sleep(0.1)

    # Stop
    print("Mission complete! Stopping...")
    twist.linear.x = 0.0
    twist.angular.z = 0.0
    pub.publish(twist)

    node.destroy_node()
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
EOF

# Make executable
chmod +x first_mission.py

# Run mission
python3 first_mission.py

Your Jetbot includes several sensors:

YAML
Primary Sensors:
  Camera: 1280×720 @ 30 FPS (calibrated)
  IMU: 6-axis (accel + gyro) @ 200 Hz
  Encoders: Left & right motor feedback
  Battery Monitor: Voltage & current sensing

Optional Sensors:
  LIDAR: 360° distance scanning
  Thermal: Infrared imaging
  GPS: Global positioning (if equipped)
  Compass: Magnetic heading

docs.title: 1.1 Understand IMU
docs.text:
YAML
6-Axis IMU contains:
  Accelerometer (3-axis):
    - Measures acceleration in X, Y, Z
    - Affected by: gravity, vibrations, mounting offset

  Gyroscope (3-axis):
    - Measures angular velocity
    - Affected by: bias, temperature drift, mounting tilt

docs.text:

# View raw IMU data

# Expected output format:

#   x: 0.05  # Small offset from gravity
#   y: -0.02
#   z: 9.81  # Gravity (9.81 m/s²)

docs.title: 1.3 IMU Bias Calibration
docs.text:
Bash
# Create calibration script
python3 << 'EOF'
import rclpy
from sensor_msgs.msg import Imu
import numpy as np
import time

class IMUCalibration:
    def __init__(self):
        rclpy.init()
        self.node = rclpy.create_node('imu_calibration')
        self.subscription = self.node.create_subscription(
            Imu, '/imu/data', self.imu_callback, 100)

        self.accel_readings = []
        self.gyro_readings = []
        self.collecting = True
        self.start_time = time.time()

    def imu_callback(self, msg):
        if not self.collecting:
            return

        # Store readings
        self.accel_readings.append([
            msg.linear_acceleration.x,
            msg.linear_acceleration.y,
            msg.linear_acceleration.z
        ])

        self.gyro_readings.append([
            msg.angular_velocity.x,
            msg.angular_velocity.y,
            msg.angular_velocity.z
        ])

        # Collect for 5 seconds
        if time.time() - self.start_time > 5:
            self.collecting = False
            self.calculate_bias()
            rclpy.shutdown()

    def calculate_bias(self):
        accel_array = np.array(self.accel_readings)
        gyro_array = np.array(self.gyro_readings)

        # Calculate averages (biases)
        accel_bias = np.mean(accel_array, axis=0)
        gyro_bias = np.mean(gyro_array, axis=0)

        print("\n=== IMU Calibration Results ===")
        print("\nAccelerometer Bias (offset from gravity):")
        print(f"  X: {accel_bias[0]:.4f} m/s²")
        print(f"  Y: {accel_bias[1]:.4f} m/s²")
        print(f"  Z: {accel_bias[2]:.4f} m/s² (should be ~9.81)")

        print("\nGyroscope Bias (should be near zero):")
        print(f"  X: {gyro_bias[0]:.4f} rad/s")
        print(f"  Y: {gyro_bias[1]:.4f} rad/s")
        print(f"  Z: {gyro_bias[2]:.4f} rad/s")

        # Diagnostic
        print("\n=== Diagnostics ===")
        accel_mag = np.linalg.norm(accel_bias)
        if 9.5 < accel_mag < 10.1:
            print("✓ Accelerometer gravity magnitude OK")
        else:
            print(f"✗ Warning: Gravity magnitude {accel_mag:.2f} (expected ~9.81)")

        if np.linalg.norm(gyro_bias) < 0.05:
            print("✓ Gyroscope bias acceptable")
        else:
            print("✗ Warning: Gyroscope bias too high")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    print("IMU Calibration: Keep robot STILL for 5 seconds...")
    print("Place robot on level surface, don't move it.")
    time.sleep(2)

    calib = IMUCalibration()
    rclpy.spin(calib.node)
EOF

# Run calibration
python3 imu_calibration.py

docs.title: 2.2 Encoder Alignment Test
docs.text:
Bash
# Create test script
python3 << 'EOF'
import rclpy
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist
from jetbot_interfaces.msg import MotorState
import time

class EncoderTest:
    def __init__(self):
        rclpy.init()
        self.node = rclpy.create_node('encoder_test')

        self.motor_pub = self.node.create_publisher(Twist, '/cmd_vel', 10)
        self.motor_sub = self.node.create_subscription(
            MotorState, '/motor/state', self.motor_callback, 10)

        self.motor_state = None

    def motor_callback(self, msg):
        self.motor_state = msg

    def test_forward(self):
        print("\n=== Testing Forward Motion ===")
        twist = Twist()
        twist.linear.x = 0.2  # 0.2 m/s forward

        print("Sending forward command for 5 seconds...")
        start_pos_left = 0
        start_pos_right = 0

        for i in range(50):  # 5 seconds at 100 Hz
            self.motor_pub.publish(twist)
            if self.motor_state:
                if i == 0:
                    start_pos_left = self.motor_state.left_position
                    start_pos_right = self.motor_state.right_position
                if i == 49:
                    dist_left = self.motor_state.left_position - start_pos_left
                    dist_right = self.motor_state.right_position - start_pos_right

                    print(f"Left distance: {dist_left:.3f} m")
                    print(f"Right distance: {dist_right:.3f} m")
                    print(f"Difference: {abs(dist_left - dist_right):.3f} m")

                    if abs(dist_left - dist_right) < 0.05:  # < 5cm difference
                        print("✓ Encoders well aligned")
                    else:
                        print("✗ Encoders misaligned - may need adjustment")
            time.sleep(0.1)

        # Stop
        twist.linear.x = 0.0
        self.motor_pub.publish(twist)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test = EncoderTest()
    test.test_forward()
    rclpy.shutdown()
EOF

python3 encoder_test.py

docs.title: 3.2 LIDAR Calibration
docs.text:
Bash
# Create LIDAR calibration script
python3 << 'EOF'
import rclpy
from sensor_msgs.msg import LaserScan
import numpy as np

class LIDARCalibration:
    def __init__(self):
        rclpy.init()
        self.node = rclpy.create_node('lidar_calibration')
        self.subscription = self.node.create_subscription(
            LaserScan, '/scan', self.scan_callback, 10)
        self.scan_count = 0

    def scan_callback(self, msg):
        self.scan_count += 1

        # Filter valid ranges
        ranges = np.array(msg.ranges)
        valid_ranges = ranges[(ranges > msg.range_min) & (ranges < msg.range_max)]

        if self.scan_count % 10 == 0:  # Every 10th scan
            print(f"\n=== LIDAR Scan {self.scan_count} ===")
            print(f"Ranges: {len(valid_ranges)}/{len(ranges)} valid")
            print(f"Min distance: {np.min(valid_ranges):.3f} m")
            print(f"Max distance: {np.max(valid_ranges):.3f} m")
            print(f"Mean distance: {np.mean(valid_ranges):.3f} m")

            # Check for bad scans
            if len(valid_ranges) < 100:
                print("✗ Warning: Few valid ranges - check LIDAR connection")

        if self.scan_count >= 100:  # Stop after 100 scans
            rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    print("LIDAR Calibration: Collecting 100 scans...")
    calib = LIDARCalibration()
    rclpy.spin(calib.node)
EOF

python3 lidar_calibration.py

docs.title: 5.1 Run Full Diagnostic
docs.text:
Bash
# Create comprehensive test
python3 << 'EOF'
import rclpy
import time
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist
from sensor_msgs.msg import Image, Imu
import numpy as np

class SensorTest:
    def __init__(self):
        rclpy.init()
        self.node = rclpy.create_node('sensor_test')

        # Subscribe to all sensors
        self.camera_sub = self.node.create_subscription(Image, '/camera/image_raw', 
                                                        self.camera_callback, 1)
        self.imu_sub = self.node.create_subscription(Imu, '/imu/data', 
                                                     self.imu_callback, 10)

        self.camera_ok = False
        self.imu_ok = False

    def camera_callback(self, msg):
        self.camera_ok = True

    def imu_callback(self, msg):
        self.imu_ok = True

    def run_test(self):
        print("\n=== SENSOR DIAGNOSTIC TEST ===\n")

        # Check ROS2 nodes
        print("1. Checking ROS2 Nodes...")
        topics = self.node.get_topic_names_and_types()
        print(f"   Active topics: {len(topics)}")

        # Wait for sensor data
        print("\n2. Waiting for sensor data (10 seconds)...")
        for i in range(100):
            rclpy.spin_once(self.node, timeout_ns=100_000_000)
            if i % 20 == 0:
                print(f"   ...{i/10:.1f}s")

        # Report results
        print("\n3. Results:")
        print(f"   Camera: {'✓' if self.camera_ok else '✗'}")
        print(f"   IMU: {'✓' if self.imu_ok else '✗'}")

        # Final status
        if self.camera_ok and self.imu_ok:
            print("\n✓ All sensors operational!")
        else:
            print("\n✗ Some sensors not responding")

        rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test = SensorTest()
    test.run_test()
EOF

python3 sensor_test.py

docs.title: 2.1 Create Alert Rules
docs.text:
Bash
# Create alert configuration
cat > /etc/prometheus/alerts.yml << 'EOF'
groups:
  - name: jetbot_alerts
    interval: 30s
    rules:
      - alert: HighCPUUsage
        expr: (100 - (avg by (instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}[5m])) * 100)) > 80
        for: 5m
        annotations:
          summary: "High CPU usage on {{ $labels.instance }}"

      - alert: HighMemoryUsage
        expr: (node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes) < 0.2
        for: 5m
        annotations:
          summary: "Low available memory on {{ $labels.instance }}"

      - alert: HighDiskUsage
        expr: (node_filesystem_avail_bytes / node_filesystem_size_bytes) < 0.1
        for: 5m
        annotations:
          summary: "Low disk space on {{ $labels.instance }}"

      - alert: HighTemperature
        expr: node_thermal_zone_temp > 80000
        for: 2m
        annotations:
          summary: "High CPU temperature on {{ $labels.instance }}"

      - alert: ROS2NodeDown
        expr: up{job="jetbot"} == 0
        for: 1m
        annotations:
          summary: "ROS2 node down on {{ $labels.instance }}"
EOF

docs.title: 3.1 Create ROS2 Metrics Exporter
docs.text:
Bash
# Create metrics collector
cat > ~/ros2_metrics_exporter.py << 'EOF'
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from prometheus_client import Counter, Gauge, Histogram, start_http_server
import time

class ROS2MetricsExporter:
    def __init__(self):
        rclpy.init()
        self.node = rclpy.create_node('ros2_metrics_exporter')

        # Start Prometheus HTTP server on port 8080
        start_http_server(8080)

        # Define metrics
        self.cpu_usage = Gauge('ros2_cpu_usage_percent', 'CPU usage percentage')
        self.memory_usage = Gauge('ros2_memory_usage_mb', 'Memory usage in MB')
        self.node_count = Gauge('ros2_node_count', 'Number of active ROS2 nodes')
        self.topic_count = Gauge('ros2_topic_count', 'Number of active topics')
        self.latency = Histogram('ros2_message_latency_ms', 'Message latency in milliseconds')
        self.messages_published = Counter('ros2_messages_published', 'Total messages published')

        # Timer for updates
        self.timer = self.node.create_timer(10.0, self.collect_metrics)

    def collect_metrics(self):
        """Collect ROS2 metrics"""
        import os
        import psutil

        # CPU and memory
        cpu = psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1)
        memory = psutil.virtual_memory().used / (1024**2)

        self.cpu_usage.set(cpu)
        self.memory_usage.set(memory)

        # ROS2 nodes and topics
        try:
            result = os.popen('ros2 node list 2>/dev/null').read()
            nodes = len(result.strip().split('\n'))
            self.node_count.set(nodes)

            result = os.popen('ros2 topic list 2>/dev/null').read()
            topics = len(result.strip().split('\n'))
            self.topic_count.set(topics)
        except:
            pass

def main():
    exporter = ROS2MetricsExporter()
    rclpy.spin(exporter.node)
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
EOF

# Run exporter
python3 ~/ros2_metrics_exporter.py &

docs.title: 4.1 Create Maintenance Script
docs.text:
Bash
# Create maintenance routine
cat > /usr/local/bin/jetbot-maintenance.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash

echo "=== Jetbot Maintenance Routine ==="

# 1. Clean temporary files
echo "1. Cleaning temporary files..."
rm -rf ~/.ros/log/*
rm -rf /tmp/jetbot_*
find ~/.cache -type f -mtime +7 -delete

# 2. Update packages
echo "2. Checking for updates..."
apt update
apt list --upgradable

# 3. Disk cleanup
echo "3. Disk cleanup..."
sudo apt autoclean
sudo apt autoremove -y

# 4. Log rotation
echo "4. Rotating logs..."
sudo logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/jetbot-ros2

# 5. Database maintenance
echo "5. Checking disk space..."
df -h

# 6. Verify services
echo "6. Verifying services..."
systemctl status jetbot-ros2 --no-pager
systemctl status prometheus --no-pager

# 7. Backup configuration
echo "7. Backing up configuration..."
tar -czf /home/jetbot/backups/config_backup_$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz \
  /home/jetbot/ros2_ws/src/*/config/

echo "✓ Maintenance complete"
EOF

chmod +x /usr/local/bin/jetbot-maintenance.sh

# Schedule weekly maintenance
(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "0 2 * * 0 /usr/local/bin/jetbot-maintenance.sh") | crontab -

docs.title: 4.2 System Backup
docs.text:
Bash
# Create backup script
cat > /usr/local/bin/jetbot-backup.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash

BACKUP_DIR="/home/jetbot/backups"
DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)

echo "Starting system backup..."

# Backup ROS2 workspace
tar -czf $BACKUP_DIR/ros2_ws_$DATE.tar.gz \
  --exclude='build' --exclude='install' \
  /home/jetbot/ros2_ws/

# Backup configs
tar -czf $BACKUP_DIR/configs_$DATE.tar.gz \
  /home/jetbot/.ros/ \
  /home/jetbot/.config/

# Backup calibrations
tar -czf $BACKUP_DIR/calibrations_$DATE.tar.gz \
  /home/jetbot/camera_calibration* \
  /home/jetbot/imu_calibration*

# Cleanup old backups (keep last 10)
ls -t $BACKUP_DIR/*.tar.gz | tail -n +11 | xargs rm -f

echo "✓ Backup complete: $BACKUP_DIR"
EOF

chmod +x /usr/local/bin/jetbot-backup.sh

# Schedule daily backups
(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "0 3 * * * /usr/local/bin/jetbot-backup.sh") | crontab -

docs.title: 5.1 Common Issues
docs.text:
YAML
Issue: High CPU Usage (>80%)
  Check:
    ros2 topic bw /camera/image_raw
    ros2 topic hz /camera/image_raw
  Solutions:
    - Reduce processing frequency
    - Optimize algorithms
    - Profile with ros2_tracing

Issue: Memory Leak
  Check:
    free -h
    top -p $(pgrep -f ros2)
  Solutions:
    - Check for circular subscriptions
    - Limit message queue size
    - Restart nodes periodically

Issue: Network Issues
  Check:
    ros2 daemon status
    netstat -an | grep ROS2
  Solutions:
    - Restart DDS middleware
    - Check firewall rules
    - Verify domain ID consistency

Issue: Sensor Failures
  Check:
    ros2 topic hz /sensor/topic
    ros2 topic echo /diagnostics
  Solutions:
    - Recalibrate sensor
    - Check connections
    - Update driver firmware

docs.title: 2.1 Create Update Checker
docs.text:
Bash
# Create update client
cat > ~/ros2_ws/src/jetbot_ota/src/ota_client.py << 'EOF'
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
import requests
import os
import hashlib
import json
import threading
from pathlib import Path

class OTAClient(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('ota_client')

        # Configuration
        self.update_server = 'https://updates.example.com'
        self.manifest_url = f'{self.update_server}/manifests/releases.json'
        self.update_dir = os.path.expanduser('~/ota_updates')
        self.firmware_dir = '/boot/firmware'
        self.backup_dir = os.path.expanduser('~/firmware_backups')

        os.makedirs(self.update_dir, exist_ok=True)
        os.makedirs(self.backup_dir, exist_ok=True)

        # Current versions
        self.firmware_version = self.get_current_firmware_version()
        self.software_version = self.get_current_software_version()

        # Timer for periodic checks
        self.timer = self.create_timer(3600.0, self.check_for_updates)  # Check hourly

        self.get_logger().info(f"OTA Client initialized")
        self.get_logger().info(f"Current firmware: {self.firmware_version}")
        self.get_logger().info(f"Current software: {self.software_version}")

    def check_for_updates(self):
        """Check for available updates"""
        try:
            response = requests.get(self.manifest_url, timeout=10)
            manifest = response.json()

            # Check firmware updates
            latest_fw = manifest['firmware']['stable']
            if latest_fw > self.firmware_version:
                self.get_logger().warn(f"Firmware update available: {latest_fw}")
                self.schedule_update('firmware', latest_fw)

            # Check software updates
            latest_sw = manifest['software']['current']
            if latest_sw > self.software_version:
                self.get_logger().warn(f"Software update available: {latest_sw}")
                self.schedule_update('software', latest_sw)

        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Failed to check updates: {e}")

    def schedule_update(self, update_type, version):
        """Schedule update in background"""
        thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self.perform_update,
            args=(update_type, version),
            daemon=True
        )
        thread.start()

    def perform_update(self, update_type, version):
        """Perform actual update"""
        try:
            if update_type == 'firmware':
                self.update_firmware(version)
            elif update_type == 'software':
                self.update_software(version)
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Update failed: {e}")
            self.rollback(update_type)

    def update_firmware(self, version):
        """Update firmware"""
        self.get_logger().info(f"Starting firmware update to {version}...")

        # Download
        url = f'{self.update_server}/firmware/stable/firmware_{version}.tar.gz'
        filepath = os.path.join(self.update_dir, f'firmware_{version}.tar.gz')

        if not self.download_file(url, filepath):
            raise Exception("Download failed")

        # Verify checksum
        if not self.verify_checksum(filepath, f'{filepath}.sha256'):
            raise Exception("Checksum verification failed")

        # Backup current
        self.backup_current_firmware()

        # Install
        self.install_firmware(filepath, version)

        self.get_logger().info(f"✓ Firmware updated to {version}")
        self.firmware_version = version

    def update_software(self, version):
        """Update software packages"""
        self.get_logger().info(f"Starting software update to {version}...")

        # Get manifest for this version
        response = requests.get(self.manifest_url)
        manifest = response.json()

        packages = manifest['software']['releases'][version]['packages']

        for package in packages:
            self.get_logger().info(f"Updating {package['name']}...")

            # Download package
            filepath = os.path.join(self.update_dir, f"{package['name']}_{version}.tar.gz")
            if not self.download_file(package['url'], filepath):
                raise Exception(f"Failed to download {package['name']}")

            # Extract and install
            os.system(f"tar -xzf {filepath} -C ~/ros2_ws/src/")

        # Rebuild
        os.system(f"cd ~/ros2_ws && colcon build --symlink-install")

        self.get_logger().info(f"✓ Software updated to {version}")
        self.software_version = version

    def download_file(self, url, filepath):
        """Download file with progress"""
        try:
            response = requests.get(url, stream=True, timeout=300)
            total_size = int(response.headers.get('content-length', 0))
            downloaded = 0

            with open(filepath, 'wb') as f:
                for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=8192):
                    f.write(chunk)
                    downloaded += len(chunk)
                    if total_size:
                        percent = (downloaded / total_size) * 100
                        self.get_logger().info(f"Download: {percent:.1f}%")

            return True
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Download error: {e}")
            return False

    def verify_checksum(self, filepath, checksum_file):
        """Verify file checksum"""
        try:
            with open(checksum_file, 'r') as f:
                expected = f.read().split()[0]

            sha256_hash = hashlib.sha256()
            with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
                for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(4096), b''):
                    sha256_hash.update(chunk)

            actual = sha256_hash.hexdigest()

            if actual == expected:
                self.get_logger().info("✓ Checksum verified")
                return True
            else:
                self.get_logger().error("✗ Checksum mismatch")
                return False
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Checksum verification failed: {e}")
            return False

    def backup_current_firmware(self):
        """Backup current firmware"""
        import shutil
        backup_file = os.path.join(
            self.backup_dir,
            f'firmware_backup_{self.firmware_version}.bin'
        )
        shutil.copy2('/boot/firmware/firmware.bin', backup_file)
        self.get_logger().info(f"Firmware backed up to {backup_file}")

    def install_firmware(self, filepath, version):
        """Install firmware"""
        import subprocess
        try:
            # Extract
            extract_dir = os.path.join(self.update_dir, f'firmware_{version}')
            os.system(f"tar -xzf {filepath} -C {extract_dir}")

            # Install (requires sudo)
            firmware_bin = os.path.join(extract_dir, 'firmware.bin')
            os.system(f"sudo cp {firmware_bin} /boot/firmware/firmware.bin")

            # Reboot required
            self.get_logger().warn("Reboot required for firmware update")
        except Exception as e:
            raise Exception(f"Firmware installation failed: {e}")

    def rollback(self, update_type):
        """Rollback to previous version"""
        self.get_logger().error(f"Rolling back {update_type}...")

        if update_type == 'firmware':
            # Restore from backup
            backups = sorted(Path(self.backup_dir).glob('firmware_backup_*.bin'))
            if backups:
                os.system(f"sudo cp {backups[-1]} /boot/firmware/firmware.bin")
                self.get_logger().info("✓ Firmware rolled back")

    def get_current_firmware_version(self):
        """Get current firmware version"""
        try:
            with open('/boot/firmware/version.txt', 'r') as f:
                return f.read().strip()
        except:
            return "unknown"

    def get_current_software_version(self):
        """Get current software version"""
        try:
            import pkg_resources
            return pkg_resources.get_distribution('jetbot-core').version
        except:
            return "unknown"

def main():
    rclpy.init()
    client = OTAClient()
    rclpy.spin(client)
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
EOF

docs.title: 5.1 Track Update Status
docs.text:
Bash
# Create deployment monitor
python3 << 'EOF'
import os
import json
from datetime import datetime

class UpdateMonitor:
    def __init__(self):
        self.log_file = '/var/log/jetbot/ota_updates.log'

    def log_update(self, robot_id, update_type, version, status):
        """Log update event"""
        event = {
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'robot_id': robot_id,
            'update_type': update_type,
            'version': version,
            'status': status  # started, completed, failed, rolled_back
        }

        with open(self.log_file, 'a') as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(event) + '\n')

    def get_deployment_status(self):
        """Get deployment statistics"""
        events = []
        with open(self.log_file, 'r') as f:
            for line in f:
                events.append(json.loads(line))

        completed = sum(1 for e in events if e['status'] == 'completed')
        failed = sum(1 for e in events if e['status'] == 'failed')
        in_progress = sum(1 for e in events if e['status'] == 'started' 
                          and not any(e2['robot_id'] == e['robot_id'] 
                                    and e2['status'] in ['completed', 'failed']
                                    and e2['timestamp'] > e['timestamp'] 
                                    for e2 in events))

        print(f"\n=== Deployment Status ===")
        print(f"Completed: {completed}")
        print(f"In Progress: {in_progress}")
        print(f"Failed: {failed}")

        return {
            'completed': completed,
            'in_progress': in_progress,
            'failed': failed
        }

monitor = UpdateMonitor()
monitor.get_deployment_status()
EOF

# Create test suite
python3 << 'EOF'
import subprocess
import time
import sys

class ProductionTest:
    def __init__(self):
        self.tests_passed = 0
        self.tests_failed = 0

    def test_ros2_connectivity(self):
        """Test ROS2 network"""
        print("Testing ROS2 connectivity...")
        result = subprocess.run(['ros2', 'node', 'list'], capture_output=True)
        if result.returncode == 0:
            nodes = result.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')
            print(f"  ✓ Found {len(nodes)} nodes")
            self.tests_passed += 1
        else:
            print("  ✗ ROS2 not responding")
            self.tests_failed += 1

    def test_sensor_fusion(self):
        """Test all sensors"""
        print("Testing sensor fusion...")
        result = subprocess.run(
            ['ros2', 'topic', 'hz', '/odom'],
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=5
        )
        if result.returncode == 0:
            print("  ✓ Sensor fusion active")
            self.tests_passed += 1
        else:
            print("  ✗ Sensor fusion failed")
            self.tests_failed += 1

    def test_motor_control(self):
        """Test motor response"""
        print("Testing motor control...")
        # Send command and verify response
        result = subprocess.run(
            ['ros2', 'service', 'list'],
            capture_output=True
        )
        if b'motor' in result.stdout:
            print("  ✓ Motor control available")
            self.tests_passed += 1
        else:
            print("  ✗ Motor control unavailable")
            self.tests_failed += 1

    def test_cpu_usage(self):
        """Test system resources"""
        print("Testing system resources...")
        result = subprocess.run(['free', '-h'], capture_output=True)
        output = result.stdout.decode()
        print(f"  {output.split(chr(10))[0]}")
        self.tests_passed += 1

    def run_all(self):
        print("\n=== Production Readiness Tests ===\n")
        self.test_ros2_connectivity()
        self.test_sensor_fusion()
        self.test_motor_control()
        self.test_cpu_usage()

        print(f"\n=== Test Results ===")
        print(f"Passed: {self.tests_passed}")
        print(f"Failed: {self.tests_failed}")

        if self.tests_failed == 0:
            print("\n✓ System ready for production!")
            return 0
        else:
            print("\n✗ Fix failures before deployment")
            return 1

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test = ProductionTest()
    sys.exit(test.run_all())
EOF

python3 production_test.py

# Create stress test
python3 << 'EOF'
import rclpy
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist
import time
import threading

def stress_test():
    rclpy.init()
    node = rclpy.create_node('stress_test')
    pub = node.create_publisher(Twist, '/cmd_vel', 10)

    print("Starting stress test (30 seconds)...")
    start = time.time()
    count = 0

    while time.time() - start < 30:
        twist = Twist()
        twist.linear.x = 0.2
        twist.angular.z = 0.1
        pub.publish(twist)
        count += 1
        time.sleep(0.01)  # 100 Hz

    # Stop
    twist = Twist()
    pub.publish(twist)

    print(f"✓ Published {count} messages over 30 seconds")
    print(f"✓ Average rate: {count/30:.1f} Hz")

    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    stress_test()
EOF
